I’ve deeply appreciated not scalding delicate white teas, or fruit teas, allowing me to enjoy their subtle flavors. It makes an excellent black tea — so robust and again, no scalding.I often offer guests my favorite lychee tea (so fragrant and potent it makes you feel a bit high). It’s so easy to scald and end up with a bitter taste that’s a total turn off. Instead, I can make a fragrant, perfect cup or pot without much skill or attention.If you’re contemplating this kettle and feeling nervous about the price, you will spend $200-$400 over the span of 10 years replacing lesser kettles.You’ll buy well, and buy once with this one.Enjoy!

text: Doesn't seem safe to use personally
Body: Personal preferences:1. They call out stainless steel in the product title. It is not fully stainless steel inside. None of the product pictures shows in inside. The top of the cap is stainless steel as you can see in the pictures, but the bottom of the cap is hard plastic.2. The inside of the kettle, around the spout area is hard plastic, including the frame for the filter. The water filled to the max line touches the plastic.The main issue:1. There's a weird smell that doesn't seem to disappear. You can't really smell it unless you boil water. That is when the smell becomes really strong. I tried washing it with dish washer, using baking soda, using lemon, and I boiled it with clean water over 10 times. The smell is still there. The first few times, you can actually smell the weird smell in the water even after poring it out of the kettle.2. There's a weird, white and transparent filling between the spout and the kettle. It seems to be "attaching" the spout to the kettle. Not sure what it is. Personally, I don't want to take the risk. Images attached.I will be returning.

I drink a variety of teas and coffees that I make by the cup and that all brew best at different temperatures, so having a kettle like this sounded like just the thing for me.After using it for a few months I'd say it's mostly OK.  According to my measurements the temperatures are reasonably accurate for a consumer device (within a few degrees of what the button says).  the top no longer flips fully open.  The labels have worn off the buttons I use most often, so now I just have to remember what they used to say.  This should not happen on a $100 product.And the user interface is wrong:  You should be able to just press the button of the temp you want and have it start heating up, but no -- you have to first press the desired temp button then press the Start button.  On the other hand if you press the Start button first it will start heating up to the temp you last used, which is fine if you always use the same temp, but I don't -- and I thought the point of this was to easily be able to bounce around between different temps for different beverages.  Oh well.If this kettle lasts many years before needing to be replaced I'll feel it was worth the cost.  If it doesn't then I'll wish I'd bought something else.

Overall this kettle is well made and sturdy. I paid a premium for this thing because I want it to last for years, which to be fair I expect it to.So why only three stars? Because it's SOOO frustrating. It has multiple settings for different temperatures of water. Handy, right? Making green tea? Use that setting. Set it to boil, and it will boil like a champ. Until it randomly forgets what setting you set it to, and Cuisinart inexplicably made the default setting 160f (the coldest possible). Why not set boiling as the default when that's what 99.9% of the time most users will want?The other setting is "Keep Warm", or as I call it "Poltergeist Mode". It just keeps turning itself on to keep the water at temperature, which is a colossal waste of energy. And again, the default setting for this mostly useless and electricity-hogging feature is ON instead of OFF.The upshot is that three or four times a week the damn thing's goldfish memory strikes and I have to reset it to boil and non-haunted mode. It might not sound like much, but it gets really old, really fast. And all this user frustration could have been easily avoided by sensible design choices. Avoid.

I expected a fine product, being familiar with many Cuisinart items and loving them over the years. Instead I received a vastly disappointing item. I'm busy, and needed a kettle, an old other-brand one having died, so I haven't sought to return it. But it's really poor.  For starters, I was sent the kettle model with a bunch of choices that I did not ask for. Bunch of unneeded choices that can go wrong. The kettle is heavy. The lid drips. One can burn one's hand as one tries to hold this heavy hot item. (In my case, the left hand, as I try to balance and lift this too heavy item with both hands.) There is sparking at the plug, if one replaces the emptied hot kettle onto its plugged in base. I have to unplug it before I put the kettle back on the base. Such a disappointment! Even the button that opens the lid is stiff and tight after some weeks of use. As you see, we're talking DUD.

text: Very Good, but misses the mark a bit
Body: I drink a LOT of tea. The taste and smell of coffee is repulsive to me; so I drink tea the way others consume coffee, i.e. multiple times a day. The onset of COVID-19 means I am now home enough to require a teakettle that can handle daily use and then some. Prior to selecting this Cuisinart, I was a loyal owner of the similar, but more expensive, Breville model. When my 8-year-old Breville gasped its last, due to the stress of said daily use, some research was in order. It seemed these two models were comparable, but the Cuisinart was available on sale for a much lower price, so I took a chance. After using it for 2 months, I feel confident in my assessment. Here's the positive: this kettle performs very well, just as well as the Breville. The design is similar, save for the settings being on the handle rather than the base. It's reliable, the bell is exactly loud enough, it's fast, consistent, and easy to use. There are just two design flaws, and they are annoying. First, due to the operational buttons' location on the handle, the one that opens the kettle is pretty far up. So far that it is impossible to press the button with my thumb and empty the kettle one-handed, which I could easily do with the Breville. Second, and most irritating, is the Keep Warm function. It does not de-activate when you lift the kettle off the base. So, if you pour out the water and place the kettle back on the base, without remembering to hit START again to shut it off, within about 15 seconds the Boil Dry alarm will commence beeping and you will have to run back to the kitchen to manually turn it off. I waited a couple of months before writing this review to see if I would adapt to these changes, but they are still just as bothersome as they were on Day 1. I'm subtracting 1 star for the design flaws, because I'm sure they won't matter to some, and it is otherwise a very good teakettle.

What a device. You would not believe that someone actually spend some thought on designing it's functionality.And i am still wondering if they have, or if it was a sample product manufactured on blueprints from a 7th grade student project.First of all: Who likes his kitchen being light up by blue light if your water boiler is plugged in? Hands up please! I count zero.Unless you dont have lights in your kitchen - (a problem in it self, i guess) this may be a useful device.Secondly: A memory function to continue boiling my water as i left it off? Please! I take it off, i want it to cool down. I want it to re-heat: I push the button to re-heat. I don't like (super dumb) artificial intelligence in my water boiler.Third: look at all these nice stains you get when touching it! A criminal scientists dream - but not mine.You may be able to handle the device without fingertips - if you are good with your elbows, have supernatural powers or wear gloves all day.Me - none of the mentioned - hence i spent more time cleaning the damn thing than using it.Fourth: after you have done your water this ingenious device keeps lighted. Is it a sign of pride of having done such a great job of boiling that water? Must be - because it completely beats me why anyone would want his kettle light up after use. (Ok - the folks without kitchen lights maybe).Oh Fifth: The thing actually broke after day 4. It would continue boiling after the water was heated, and beep like mad because you actually used it for what you have bought it for - boiling water and using the water, once it is boiled. I understand that this is a use case the designers of thisingenious masterpiece clearly did not have in mind (Kitchen lamps were haunting their minds!)  - so maybe it wasn't broken but it worked as designed.Now this could again be a design feature - i simply call it broken. And am extremely happy to have returned this piece ofcompletely useless junk.After all - it did actually boil water. But i just cannot be asked to give it a second star for it, as there are so many products out there that dothat for a quarter of the price - and they actually work.

I looked for a long time for the kettle that was going to be the best fit for me, and I am so glad I finally found it. This is just what I needed.Pros:- Easy Setup: Just open the box, give it a quick rinse before filling with water, plug it in, and you're good to go.- Easy to use: The intuitive design makes it quick and easy to see if the kettle is on or not, how much water is inside, and what temperature the water is.- Multiple temperature settings: No matter what kind of tea you are brewing, you can get the water to just the right temperature to bring out the best flavor of the tea.- Tea in minutes: No more waiting for water to boil and then cool to the right temperature, or starting the water boiling and forgetting to turn it off. The water is quickly heated to the correct temperature, and the kettle keeps it at the temperature for up to 30 minutes. You can turn it on, walk away, and when you come back your water is perfect for whatever tea you are making.- Light weight: Easy to pick up and pour, even when it is full.- Cordless: The cordless design and swivel base make this work a lot like a traditional stove-top kettle.Cons:- It's louder than I expected while heating the water. It doesn't disrupt other activities, but it was a surprise the first time I turned it on. It's also only noisy while the water is heating, so just for a few seconds at a time.- The outside of the kettle gets really warm. The handle stays cool, so I didn't notice the heat until I accidentally bumped the side. No injuries, but I would definitely take care to keep it away from small hands.- The small top opening makes it hard to get clean. Luckily, my hands are small enough to fit in there to dry it out between uses, but I don't think my husband could clean it.Overall, the few problems are relatively minor compared to the ease of use and overall design of this kettle. I am sure this will stick around for a long time and see a lot of use in our home.

Everyone should have a good electric kettle, but finding the right one is hard.  This product falls right in the mid range of prices, but has qualities that make it better than the price tag.  It has a large capacity in the reservoir and I can easily make 5 mugs of hot chocolate or tea to satisfy everyone immediately.  I really like the variable temperature so that I can better gauge cool down time and do some subtle brewing as I learn more about teas.  I also love the stay warm feature so that I can go back for a second cup any time.  Even if it cools, don't worry, this heats a pot faster than a single mug in the microwave.If asked a few days ago I would have nothing bad to say about this kettle, but having used it for just a little over a month and half, it has developed a squeal when it brews.  I can't figure out why and it is a bit ear piercing.  It was pretty silent until now.  If I figure out what is up or someone else knows, I will pass it along.

This is the BEST purchase I have made in the last 5 years, maybe longer.  "The kettle is best thing since sliced bread." So glad that I spent the extra few bucks for the Cuisinart brand. This kettle heats very quickly.  The different temperature settings are fantastic and accurate (I checked). My husband is in a wheel chair and being able to set this kettle on the counter for his use has been a life and labor saver.  He has been unable to safely use the stove and over-stove microwave safely. He drinks several different hot beverages each day.  I to love the convenience of the kettle.  I really like the capacity, even with the nice size between the two of use we run atleast 3-4 liters of water through it daily.  Now my husband can have his desired beverages when he wants them even when I am unavailable to lend a hand. Thank you so much for a quality product. I just read this to my husband and he says that the convenience of this product has added significantly to his quality of life.

text: It's pretty random. I almost regret getting a fancy electric ...
Body: Stopped working after about 1.5 years. It was working well up until that point. I didn't drop it or mistreat it in any way. What happens is I turn the unit on, it indicates it's heating, but it doesn't heat fully or not at all. After 15 minutes or so the unit will start making a long steady beep. It's pretty random. I almost regret getting a fancy electric kettle. Perhaps I should have stuck with the basic model of on/off. It's been over a week and I've had to heat my water with a pot on my stove...I contacted customer support and they are processing my replacement delivery. I had to pay a $10 processing fee. It's been a week now and the replacement has not yet left the warehouse. They are requesting that I cut the cord of the old unit and ship it back to them. I have to pay the return shipping of the cut cord. I'm assuming this is to show proof that I am not a fraudster.I'll update this review after I receive the replacement.UPDATE 04-17-2018The replacement finally came. The $10 processing fee and the wait time for the replacement was a bit annoying, but otherwise I'm happy. Upgrading this to 4 stars. They honored their warranty agreement.

I was really in two minds about paying this amount of money for a kettle but with myself and my wife being heavy tea drinkers and on the back of a glowing NYT Wirecutter review, I decided to splash out. My previous kettle was a $30 Hamilton Beach model that had worked well but it was the third one I'd owned in the last 8 years. They seem to last about 2-3 years before something fails, usually the catch on the lid.This $100 kettle lasted a week before it completely died. No power was going to the kettle and no lights were coming on. One morning it just decided that it didn't want to work anymore.Now, while I might just have had a lemon (it happens), getting customer support was a complete pain. Amazon directed me to Cuisinart. Cuisinart's online customer support form is broken and just doesn't work. We eventually got through to someone on the customer support 800 number who said we had to return it through Amazon. Round in circles we went. Eventually I figured out how to get the return done (apparently being a Prime member made me eligible for a return... go figure) and I got a refund.To be honest, I would rather pay $30 for a kettle that I know is going to work for 3 years than $100 for a kettle that might work for a week.

text: Base only worked for 6 months - terrible customer service
Body: I was completely in love with this until one morning it just stopped working. It was only 6 months old. All the lights came on but when I pressed the "start" button it didn't heat.  In the product manual for quick solutions it said to call the Customer Service number which I did since I wanted my tea maker back up and running quickly.  Once I finally got through to an agent they told me my base was broken and that since it was on back order they couldn't help me until a month after my initial  call to them.  It has now been four weeks and after three more calls to their customer service I finally have a date when the base will be available - it isn't for another 4 weeks!  So by the time I receive the new base it will be a total of 8 weeks.  I am now in the market for a new kettle because I am so fed up with waiting on a base unit.  Too bad my kettle didn't last - it was great until it broke and the Cuisinart Customer Service is terrible.  It seems to me they should have a faster fix for a product that gets used everyday by their customer.

text: Emperor's clothing or a disguised space rocket from the 1950s?
Body: Looks the part, but has gone up over $10 in price since we purchased it 17 months ago. I certainly wouldn't get it again. It looks nice, and the blue glow is pleasing enough, but for what it is and seeing people struggle with it, nahhh.It comes down to poor design, not the functionality of being able to change the temperature of water. For an old tea-bag like myself, I have to wonder whether the designers actually ever used it to make something as simple as a cup of tea.Once the kettle has more than a teaspoon of water in it, people tend to hold the handle much higher up due to the displaced weight and the required manipulation, combined with wrist strength when holding it in the middle or lower end. You won't want to hold it near the bottom, it's hot, and that makes for a burny-burny boo-boo.Having over 30 years experience of kettle manipulation for lots of "cuppas" (tea), the weight balance is very poor. I can cope, but my wife, her mother, her father, and any visitor (welcome or not) clearly struggles to not hold the handle at the top when it's not near empty. And guess what? The top is where all the temperature and keep warm buttons are. I.e. anyone that isn't the spawn of Xena and Hercules is going to constantly be crushing the buttons while they move or use the kettle. Which means putting it back on its phallic charger base protuberance with undesired settings EVERY TIME!The actually container shape is also complete rubbish. When it contains plenty of water, the pour is fine and consistant, but as the water depletes, the water doesn't pool sensibly inside when poured. The top is thinner that the rest, this creates a reservoir of water below the regular pour-line. Bionic individuals can anticipate what's going to happen and react the femtosecond in question, but puny mortal humans will discover a 0.00001° change in inclination at this point will transform the escaping water from the mere dribble to a torrential deluge shaming Niagara, and over-filling the desired live in the mug.tl;dr: it boils water, it's ergonomically challenged. I like the blue illumination.

text: Good.  Could be better if some plastic was removed
Body: Pros: Heats Quick, Easy Temperature Control, Looks good.Cons: Plastic under the lid, Plastic in the pour spout. Plastic in the measurement display.It would be great if Cuisinart would make a version of this with absolutely no plastic inside, if they do I'll replace this with that one.  It does heat the water accurately.  However, where the water sits, it does come in contact with a little bit of the plastic that displays the amount of water in the unit. Also there is some plastic in the spout, but I was able to remove that with needle nose pliers.  There is also plastic under the lid, so we just run ours with the lid open, I'm not sure if the lid would shut if this plastic was removed.

text: Sleek kettle for your morning brew
Body: Intuitive kettle with lots of options .We have had it for a few days and it has worked for our French press coffee in the morning. It does get hot, so be careful.

I have been trying to buy an electric kettle with zero plastic that is in contact with the water. I am so frustrated! This is a very expensive model which claims zero plastic & water contact which is completely wrong! The ‘filter’ is enclosed in plastic & it is not removable!  The ‘filter’ is a small screen covering the exit hole where the spout meets the pot. For a high end model this is un acceptable!  The ‘filter’ is also poorly made and fitted to the water exit. Being returned. I expected more from Cuisinart!

text: 3 mon Followup: Small but unpleasant caveat… NO LONGER SMALL!
Body: This is today:Absolutely HATE!!!! The auto-warm up!!!You can NEVER be 100% attentive and you WILL start baking a dry kettle!!!This was a waste of money!Back to searching for a new one.Below is my original review:Everything in this kettle spells "perfection".The speed of heating is fantastic!I knocked one star because the default mode is "Reheat" and in my case the kettle is always empty in one go. So we constantly need to watch it when putting it back on the base as it starts heating the empty kettle.Then the clicking starts until you manage to turn it off.I wish the default was to always be OFF after use.This is bad design, assuming that you always need power - which is by definition NOT a safe assumption.You basically have an appliance insisting on delivering power after you told it not to.Yes, it does have a safety switch which will turn it off to prevent a meltdown ... again ... bad design. You are now using a safety feature which is supposed to occasionally save the day routinely.What about the day the sensor malfunctions ... ?

*Update 8/29/19: I thought I would share that I emailed Cuisinart through their contact form on the Cuisinart website. A representative responded to me and asked for the date I purchased my kettle, product serial number, and my mailing address. I responded. Two days later, I received another email asking me to send them my original receipt. I responded accordingly. Today I received a third email from Cuisinart that explains my kettle's manufacturer's warranty lasts only for 3 years and is expired, but that I am within a 6-month grace period. If I'd like, I can mail my kettle to an address they will provide to me at my own expense. This is all well and good, but I'm very frustrated that it took three email to tell me that I have no recourse for my suddenly broken kettle. Again, I've had enough of small appliances made with substandard materials that cost more money than they're worth. I'll be going back to basics with food preparation and will support any decent, consumer-friendly company that will manufacture a simple tea kettle or coffee maker with quality stainless steel and quality components. I hope more consumers will do the same. I'm sorry to say it, but products made in China are not made well nor are they made to last. Consumers have the ability to take a stand against poorly made products with their voices and their wallets.* Update 7/11/19: This is a review of my third kettle. My first experience in 2011 was so good, I just had to try again. This kettle worked flawlessly for three years. Then suddenly and unexpectedly, the base went out and the kettle is now useless. Three years is not long enough for an $80 kettle to last, in my opinion. I'm moving on from Cuisinart.2016: I actually purchased two of these kettles, the first in the fall of 2010 and the second, one year later. The first kettle worked great in every aspect, and is still working perfectly today in year 2016. No rust ever, but occasional mineral deposits that are easily removed with a vinegar rinse. The second kettle regrettably never worked, not even for a moment. I'm not sure if the kettle itself is faulty or if the problem is in the base. Due to my locale not having access to regular mail (extreme rural Alaska), it was simply too difficult to try to return it. My husband is still optimistic he can do something to make it work. If nothing else, perhaps the working part can be switched out with the first kettle when it finally fizzles out, whenever that is. So I have a mixed opinion: one kettle rates 5 stars while the other rates 0 stars. I'll be generous and give a mean review of 3 stars for the two. I'm interested in buying a new kettle to use while visiting family during a lengthy stay, but am concerned whether I'll receive a 0 star product or higher. Consistency in quality seems to be an issue, reading through a number of reviews. Here's hoping...  By the way, I'm extremely appreciative to those genuine reviewers who are not posting as a result of obtaining their kettle 'with a discount in exchange for an honest and unbiased' review.' If this is where Amazon sellers are headed, I'm not biting.

Short version: I liked the kettle when it was working, but it stopped working and after I sent it back, Cuisinart waited out the warranty period and said they wouldn't do anything for me. So basically they took my money and left me with nothing. 4 stars for the kettle, -4 for malevolent customer service then +2 just to keep this out of the hater category of 1 star.Long version: I was impressed with this kettle when visiting my brother so I bought my own. Simple to use, well marked temperatures and tea types. Looks nice. It worked as expected for a couple months then stopped working. No indicators of declining function, just wouldn't heat anymore one day. I called Cuisinart and followed their instruction about cleaning the unit in case a temperature sensor was blocked, but no result. Sent it back to Cuisinart and didn't hear anything for months. Almost a year, actually, which is when I called them to see what was up. As with probably most other busy people out there, an automatic tea kettle is not my top priority, especially when it's just a convenience over the standard tea kettle that is still on my stovetop. In any case, I was told that a "referral to corporate" was being made and that I would get a call back in a couple days. No call. Now, three months later and no returned calls and I called them today and was told that it's now past the warranty period and because I didn't call within a month from the original claim, they don't consider it their problem so they are not willing to do anything for me. Keep in mind that the kettle supposedly carries a three year warranty so one might think this is still under the warranty period. Also, when I called three months ago- under the "one year" they keep claiming is preventing them from taking action- the customer service rep said nothing about their expected protocol from customers or about a kettle which they now claim was sent to me via USPS with no delivery confirmation. This last claim was made by a customer service supervisor moments before ending the call and was not mentioned in any previous interactions with them, an action which gives me no confidence that they are telling the truth. Now they say the best they can do for me is give me an address for their corporate office to which to lodge a complaint, though given their tactic of doing nothing until the problem (ie customer) goes away, I have no faith that my letter will produce any results. For future kitchen appliance needs, I will avoid Cuisinart and recommend others do the same.

OK, this is the first day I am using it, and if it performs tomorrow as it does today, it goes back!  This variable-temperature kettle:  A) does not beep when it's done heating, contrary to what the manual says; B) It smells of melting plastic - fumes emanate and can be smelled all over the house, and the source seems to be somewhere near the "Start" button.In short, a kettle must be a kettle first, and bells and whistles only after that.  If it stinks of hot plastic and does not switch off when the water is boiling, all those "oolong" and "french press" temperature settings are useless.Or maybe I just got a lemon?[Same day, 9 Jun 2011, evening]  It spewed its last portion of poisonous vapor and died.  Buttons light up when I press "boil" and "start," but it does not heat water.  Why this costs $100?  My first cassette player which I bought in 1987 for $99.99 in 1987 dollars still works! This is just a kettle, and a bad one too!

I'm very pleased with this product because it was so convenient to have on hand recently for serving company.  They really admired it and I must say it is very attractive with its brushed stainless steel finish and light up buttons.  I continue to use it on a daily basis.  I love that it has a setting for green tea (which I use and drink all the time.  Yes, my green tea is better now) Besides that being my favorite feature I also enjoy how it pleasantly beeps when it reaches the desired temperature setting.  I thought I'd miss my whistling tea kettle, but rather this is so much less stressful than jumping for that noisy stove top version!Pros:*Attractive*entirely stainless steel*convenient easy to operate light up buttons (one each for 160 degrees= delicate, 175=green, 185=white, 190 = Oolong, 200=French Press, Boil=black, start, and keep warm printed on each button) and stay warm feature*small foot print and easy to set up*Pleasant beep sound when ready*works fast*pours nicely*plenty big enoughCons:*Entire outside gets extremely hot and could severely burn if not picked up by the handle (entire handle stays cool though)*a little pricey (entirely stainless steel finish so forgivable in my book)Amazon shipped this out with lightning speed, at better pricing and free shipping which saved me about $20 over my local store so that made me very happy.  My husband is disappointed by how hot the outside gets (similar to how a stovetop teapot gets).  We are spoiled by our insulated coffee pot and if this item were insulated like that it would be perfect, however I still love it! (he on the other hand would have given it less stars for that)I wondered if it would continue to heat once removed from its base (I was hoping it had some sort of charging feature), but that disconnect stops all electricity and all the lights turn off, etc.  However, it stores the settings for up to 2 minutes so it will automatically return to its last setting if you return it in time.In summary, I'm very happy with this purchase and recommend it.PS:  I haven't had any scaling issues as other people have mentioned.  I use filtered water and feel that any complaints on that have to be directed to the water used, not the kettle.

This water heater is not aesthetically pleasing but it is SO useful. The lower temperature setting is perfect for matcha. The fact that you can control the temperature is very convenient. In addition, I really like the “keep warm” setting that keeps the water at the temperature I want instead of me having to continually heat up the water heater.One con is that when you heat up the water heater, the outer layer gets very hot so you have to be careful to only touch the handle. Other than that, I love this water heater.

text: BEST RECENT KITCHEN APPLIANCE PURCHASE - SEE 2017 UPDATE!!!
Body: 01/17 Update:  Well, after almost a year of use, I happened to, quite by accident, hear a dripping noise in the studio where I use this electirc brewer.  At first, I thought it was due to condensation from the water I had just brewed, but after tracking dow the 1/2 inch of water in my trash can, I found that there was a steady bead, by bead, leak in the bottom of the handle.  The electric base was sitting in a puddle of water and the water fortunately dripped down the line and into my waste basket before hitting the electrical socket.  (That would have blown all of my equipment in my studio.  Phew!).  I have given it a three based on the fact that I have used it for a year, and didn't have any problems, but I have not been able to contact Cuisinart to see if they will still repair/replace this product.  Will update again once that happens.03/16: Best recent kitchen appliance I have purchased. After nearly burning up my kitchen with a conventional tea kettle (yeah, yeah, forgot it was on. Shout out to Max, my barking dog on the save) I purchased the CPK-17.  I noticed a vast difference in the taste of the tea from the very first pot.  As most have said, green tea tastes bitter, and hence they do not drink it.  The green tea I've had for nearly a year now is gone, and I now know what green tea should taste like.  I'm also experimenting with other brews now as well.  Fast, safe, easy to use with multiple presets for the perfect cup of tea. Purchase and enjoy!

We’ve had the old one for over a decade. My wife says 18 years. She was cleaning it and put it back on the base and it made bad noises so time for a new one. Yeah, the button descriptions wore off eventually and we wrote new ones on. A decade or so in the hinge on the top broke and we made a cute handle for it. But it kept working and heating water to the temp of choice. Time for a new one. Really, I have no complaints. Few things last this well given the abuse we put it through between hot cocoa, French press, oolong, white, and earl grey. It just kept working.

I bought this based on the recommendation of Wirecutter which appears in the new York Times website. I had dropped (and broke) my very inexpensive basic Hamilton Beach water boiler. Rather than just buying the same unit, I researched and chose this recommended unit, based on the temperature control features.After using the Cuisinart unit, I discovered the following issues:1. the water dribbles and pours out of the spout inconsistently. The is due to the design of the spout which has a screen and plastic ribs on the inside. I find this to be a huge omission buy the Wirecutter testing team. How did they not see this?2. I found the unit heavy and difficult to pour due to all the electronics in the handle.3. I thought that having different water temperatures is a nice feature, and if you drink a lot of tea, I guess it's beneficial, but in my case, all those added electronics in the handle made lifting it clumsy and heavy (and my palette is not that sophisticated).4. Even though the product states that is has "free returns", the Amazon seller tried to charge return shipping. I had to ask Amazon to intervene, and eventually theseller  agreed to pay for the return shipping, but said they would be charging a "restocking" fee which would be at least 15%, and could be as much as the entire cost of the unit, if it had been used and not returned in the original box. I appealed to Amazon to assist, but they declined and said that I had not contacted them within the correct time frame for a return (I had)., but left no other option, so I have the unit sitting on a shelf in the pantry. Oh well, live and learn.Moral of the story: Buy from a local retailer such as target where returning an item is easy and a no-hassle event

text: The Best Kettle of All Times!
Body: This is by far the best programmable kettle that I have owned. I've had it for more than 2 years and it is still in perfect condition. It's great for those who drink white, green tea as they don't need the temperature to be as high as black tea for example. The fact that it is stainless steel also gives me a peace of mind as I wanted something with least plastic possible in the inside. The inside of this kettle is all stainless steel and you won't see any heating element like the old/cheap ones. Also I love the fact that it is can be detached from the base so easily and smoothly which make it super easy to work with. Even for those who are not tea drinkers this is good for making hot chocolate, french press coffee, instant coffee, cereal, oat meal, etc. I also love that when it is ready it makes a beep so that you won't need to stay next to it in the morning waiting for it to be ready. The kettle has this awesome function that it keeps the water warm for about 30min even after it beeps (reach the set temperature) so if you have guest over or can't get to it right away you hot water will stay hot. The outer side is also super easy to clean. The handle feels very solid and sturdy and the top lead opens and closes very securely. Overall, this is a well made kettle for multiple purposes!

text: Kettle is fantastic and worth every penny!
Body: We were gifted on of these for Christmas and it has definitely become the most used item in our kitchen.  First off, it's chrome finish is very esthetically pleasing.  I am a stickler for a bare-bones clean kitchen countertop but this kettle is certainly attractive enough to be left on the out all of the time.  I certainly like that it is cordless, so is easy to move and it pours very well.  The non-slip base is a great safety feature as is the boil-dry prevention that is built in.  Anyone who enjoys tea will appreciate the ability to control temperature and warm up features.  Heating to a boil is astonishingly quick.  Caution - the exterior of the kettle gets very hot and is potential burn hazard if not handled with care.  It has a large volume capacity of 1.7 L, and is very easy to clean.  Typically just a simple wipe is all that is required.  I have had a handful of different kettles over the years - some better than others.  This is by far the most superior that I have used and would highly recommend to anyone.Caution - the exterior of the kettle gets very hot and is potential burn hazard if not handled with care.

text: Slightly confusing but makes fantastic tea
Body: I didn't realize how much precise temperature control would improve my tea.  I had an old, simple, low end Bodum plastic kettle in safety orange that I loved until it died after eleven years of heavy use.  An exact replacement wasn't available and the price of fancy kettles like this one has come down quite a bit, so I figured it was worth the upgrade.  My tea is so much better now that I'm using the correct temperature for each type of tea.  My prior method was boiling water for every type, then waiting for it to cool somewhat for more delicate teas, as I figured being exact didn't matter until you got to much higher end teas than I use. I was wrong. It matters a lot. I didn't know what I had been missing until I made green/white teas with the exact correct temperature water.I do miss the simplicity of a single button, and found the user interface slightly confusing.  Lit up blue is not on, which it should be. It's standby.  It has to have a flashing white light to be actually heating your water. That's quite silly and counterintuitive.  But you get used to it.I can't speak to longevity, as I've only had it a few months, but so far, I love it.

I bought this model because Wirecutter rated it highly, and, as a tea drinker, I liked the ability to set specific temperatures. It was replacing a basic Breville kettle I'd had for years that started to leak.First, the handle is not comfortable for a smaller hand (mine). It is wide to accomodate all the controls, but the shape makes it difficult to control when full of water.  If I steady it with my other hand, the outside is very hot when the water heats.Second, the water gauge is hard to read. It's located under the handle, and although lighted, it was difficult to see the water line.Third, and the reason I returned it, is that after only two days of use, I couldn't turn the control panel off. It stayed lit and no matter what button I hit, it stayed on. I unplugged it, waited, then re-plugged it. Phew, lights off. I hit Start and the control panel lit up, but the kettle didn't start. That's it. Back to Amazon it went.PS -- I bought the newer, but same basic Breville as I had before. The handle design is excellent and the water level is displayed on BOTH sides of the kettle, clearly visible. My previous one was plastic and while it got warm, never got too hot to touch. The new one is metal and gets hot on the outside. My only gripe.

This kettle is very disappointing. Leaks from the top part of the pouring spout when low water level.I did thorough research before buying a new kettle to replace my 5-year-old amazon basic kettle.I looked for 3 main features: fast heat up, temperature control, and elegant looks. In addition, I was looking for a stainless steel kettle to avoid the plastic odor.Most kettles with temp control look very rough so I decided to purchase the Cuisinart.THERE ARE SO MANY BAD THINGS ABOUT THIS KETTLE so it is hard to pick the one to start with.1. It is very slow in boiling and noisy. My amazon basic kettle has the same efficiency.2. It leaks from the top part of the pouring spout when low water level.3. The kettle body is hot.4. The blue light is annoying especially because it doesn't turn off when the boiling is done. It takes a couple of minutes for the light to fade away.5. The "stay warm" button is on as a default, so you have to turn it off actively, otherwise it will continue to perform rounds of heating indefinitely.6. It beeps like a body thermometer!Good things:1. No odor2. Looks OK, but still not elegant.The bottom line,  I would not buy this kettle for that price with all the listed bad features. The real problem is that there is no good alternative. Probably I would go for something cheaper with fewer expectations.

text: In The Event Your Cuisinart CPK-17 Has Ceased To Function
Body: After about 8 months, mine stopped working in the same way it seems others' have - still makes lights and sounds but no heat. I was able to revive it though by disassembling and cleaning the bottom of the circuit board with rubbing alcohol. I'm not an electrical engineer and have no idea what I'm talking about, but this is what worked for me. It is probably very dangerous though, so don't do it.With that said:you will need this screwdriver h[...] (in case this link is removed, search amazon for "triangle screwdriver", first result)remove the 3 screws from the bottom of the kettlegently dislodge the plastic bottom piece - there are fine short wires connected to it, so be careful you don't yank itthere are 3 white connectors attached to the circuit board - carefully slide them off, trying not to bend the long thin contact wiresnow that the bottom piece is separated, you have to get the circuit board off - there is one screw in the middle and 3 (or 4) plastic tabs that must be brokenthe back of the circuit board will most likely look grimy and corroded - try to clean it with a cloth and rubbing alcoholok, now put it all back togetherof course the circuit board is just going to dangle in there now, since you've broken the tabs. I didn't even worry about it.You can test it on the base plate before completely reassembling, to make sure there aren't loose wires. I mean, I did, but it's probably dangerous, so understand you alone are responsible for your health. Hope this helps. Wish I would have taken pictures, but it's really pretty self evident once you start, as long as you've got some intuition for these things.

text: Just bought my 2nd Cuisinart electric kettle; the 1st one lasted almost 10 years
Body: I think the title of this review says it all.  I wrote a glowing review the first time I bought it (10 years ago???) and it was used most days. It lasted a long time.  When it died, it was because the power stopped working - which was probably my fault since I tended to really YANK the plug out of the socket each time after using the kettle since I don’t like leaving appliances with heating elements plugged in when no one is around.So I looked up on my Amazon account to see what I bought last time (love this feature), then looked at the competition today.  I couldn’t find another kettle that I liked as much as this one.  The recent reviews made me hesitate, but overall the kettle’s features still resonate with me: it is heavy and solid - no one is going to knock it over by accident; it heats up quickly; it holds a lot of water; it beeps when its finished; its aesthetically pleasing, which is important since it sits on our counter; and it is simple and uncomplicated.I’m crossing my fingers we have good luck again; so far so good.  Highly recommend.

text: DO NOT recommend wasting your money on this piece of JUNK. Rust all over the place
Body: Looking nice and sophisticated with all those bells and whistles, BUT there is HUGE problem with it. It gets rust inside where the boiling water is after a year or so of use.  I've already purchased it 2 times and I had to change it every 2 years. No more for me. Junk made in China. I'm getting something else this time. DO NOT recommend wasting your money on this piece of JUNK. I'm very upset and disappointed, paying $100 for this JUNK REALLY? Take a look at the pictures I took as a prove.

text: Shitty warranty, noisy, and temperature decal is disappearing after only 2 months of usage
Body: Just got off a call with cuisinart. They clearly don’t stand behind their products. The numbers coming off after 3 months is just not acceptable at that price. Argument for this not being a  warranty issue is because the kettle still works, but in 6 months when all the numbers have come off, I’ll wonder what the functionality of a kettle is that allows you to choose the temperature when you can’t read the temperature anymore. Seems utterly stupid to think I’ll have to resort to a sharpie or an engraving pen to make sure I recall the temperature locations. I will think twice about buying anything from cuisinart again because they obviously are not supportive to their consumers. The kettle is also annoyingly noisy - so that is another strike against it.

I have had three of these kettles. The first one failed within a year and was replaced for free by Cuisinart. The second one lasted another two years and then was out of warranty and would not be replaced. I went without one for a period of time and then bought another. After thirteen months, it failed. I called Cuisinart and was told I would have to pay to ship the broken item to Cuisinart in order to get a replacement. I declined. I'm done with this junk.

text: The top doesn’t open all the way without hand assistance
Body: This is my second Cuisinart kettle. The last one I had for 7 years. When that top broke( it would no longer close) I replaced the kettle. I’m very disappointed that from day one, the top wasn’t working.

text: Not a good product from Cuisinart
Body: I wanted to love it. Nice color, good temp control and water capacity. However, after every use (no matter the temperature setting) the water tastes like burned plastic. We used it for months and the burned plastic taste never went away.  This is more than an inconvenience. We can’t use it at all. The water tastes terrible. The kettle is stainless steel but the inside of the lid it is black plastic. For this brand and price I was expecting a great product. I wished I return it, but I thought it was something temporary.I had tu purchase another electric kettle from another brand that is stainless steel outside and  inside the lid and it works great.

I have had a couple of these over the years and they performed well --- till this one.  A couple of months after use the lid button began to fail.  I got around it by adding a button on top to lift the lid and fill the pot.  A couple of months after that the lid would not stay open making filling the pot a chore.  We read reviews on other sites which described the same problem with nightmare results in trying to get repair/refund, etc. from Cuisinart  I don't know if they changed mfg or outsourced, but the quality is not what I'd expect from Cuisinart.  I won't purchase again.

text: Worked OK, broke after two years, warranty useless
Body: This was an alright kettle, with a sensible selection of temperatures for my teas and coffee.  It heated water in a reasonable time. (I never boil water for tea/coffee so I can't say hew it would fare in such use.)  There was nothing stellar about it but it was fine, it worked well.  It did at times fail to shut off at the right temperature (but would rather boil and then shut off) but this was very rare, so fine.  It was pricey at $70 when I got it.After about two years it broke. It stopped shutting off reliably so that it would just boil sometimes regardless of temperature control and a few times it didn't even seem that it would stop so I had to shut it off.  What finally did it is that it started leaking, nearly every time it's used.  And these were good leaks, the counter would have a little paddle. One can see scale from leaked water all along the edges of the bottom half of the window and handle.  So it started breaking up at the seams, literally.  It is far too early for a product with the prime price to break apart like this after two years, I think.I'd like to add, I didn't abuse it in any way. It was used a few times a day, nearly every day, to warm up water to 175 -- 200, for (green/oolong or black) tea and coffee.But then comes the kicker: the 3-year warranty?  Well yes I presume, but you pay all shipping.  It actually says this loud and clear. Go find the warranty information on this page and click on it and read the page.  (Also, at least one other review talks about it.) So I'd be  paying altogether at least a half of its (then) retail price -- so that they take care of their faulty product.  A little funny isn't it.  Needless to say I'm buying another, and not this brand unfortunately.Altogether, it worked OK (4/5), broke up too early (-1), warranty is misleading unless you actually read it, what most people don't do (-1) -- the fairest I can do is thus 2/5.

text: Spout Contains Black Plastic Besides the filter
Body: While the Cuisinart 1.7 Tea kettle worked very well, I did not like the fact that there is black plastic piece down inside the front of the spout where a removable filter sits. This black plastic part does come into contact with the water when boiling, something I did not want in a tea kettle. Also the lid top opening where you fill for water is small and if you like to clean your kettle by hand you would need a child's hand to get into it.

text: Started to malfunction 1 year into 3 year warranty
Body: I did extensive research before buying this kettle in March 2016. Cuisinart is supposed to be a very good brand. I wanted to love it.For almost a year it has worked well. Now, however, it randomly fails to stop at the programmed temperature setting, and will proceed to a full boil without ever shutting off! Even if removed from the base; even if the 'start' button is turned off & no lights are on; the kettle still continues to boil.It does not happen every time. When it does the only way to reset is to unplug the base from the wall. So, now to be safe, we can not walk away from the kettle when it is heating.Also some of the printing is coming off of the water level window.I called Cuisinart & they will replace it, but as others have noted, their 3 year warranty does not cover shipping, so I would have to pay to return the defective kettle AND pay for the shipping of a replacement. I am going to see if Amazon will do anything better for me.As an aside, I've owned a Breville cordless kettle (without temperature controls) for 10 years plus & it still does the job.Unfortunately, I need multiple temperature settings now, and I see similar complaints about the Breville multi-temp kettle.Not sure what brand to choose next.

You can't fit your hand inside the kettle to wash it. The plastic filter is removable, but there is still another plastic grate the water passes through when pouring. Last time I checked, boiling water and plastic shouldn't go together, even if it is BPA free. And finally, the kettle is not insulated. So once the water boils, the outside of the kettle is screaming hot. The handle is fine, but in no way can you touch the kettle. I guess I should have realized that. The description lacks this bit of info, which should have told me that it isn't insulated. But regardless, that is a big problem for us since we have kids, so I'm returning it.

text: Loose screw after 4 months of use, Cuisinart not helpful in resolving issue.
Body: I bought this unit 4 months ago from Amazon and it worked great (and maybe still does). I use the unit once a day to boil water for my newborn so the use of the unit is very light.My issue is simple, I just found a loose screw bouncing around inside the kettle and after calling the customer service I was told that I have to pay $15 to have a new one sent to me and cut the cord of the original unit and send it back to Cuisinart (at my own expense). To me this is waste of resources, time, and money to handle it the way Cuisinart requires me to proceed. I simply want to find out where the screw came from so that I can put it back where it belongs. Its most likely a very minor thing.Looking at Amazon, I don't think I can return it for a replacement so that does not make me happy ether.I'm attaching image of the screw in case someone dealt with the same issue and can help.

text: Works well, base is a bit wobbly
Body: I wish it felt more stable. I’m not sure why it doesn’t sit square on the counter without wobbling back-and-forth….

text: Awesome Kettle-Works Like a Champ....and is going strong after five years!
Body: I bought this over six months ago and heat it up at least two times per day. It is fantasticl Not only can I choose my temperature, it will stay at that temp for another half hour if I'm not around to pour it. It is consistant and has many great features.Addendum: I have now used this kettle for over a year and a half and it still works fantastically!!  Still using it 2x or more per day. I drink many types of tea and love to make French-press coffee upon occasion too. The temperature selections are phenominal for multi-use. It has a window for easy measurment, looks high-tech with an elegant design, and its working quality and features are well worth the rather steep pricetag. I am very happy that I can choose to keep the water "cooking" for a half an hour (for when I'm busy or have company) or program it to immediately shut itself off. I used to have accidents using a stovetop teakettle, no more with this appliance. I couldn't be happier with it.It is now five years since purchase and it's still going strong. My husband and I remain avid tea drinkers. We now use this 4 to 5 times per day, every day, for the last five years. It works so great that they should win a medal for design and durability. Like many others, the lettering on the most used buttons have worn off as you can see in the photos.

text: Hot water comes in contact with plastic.
Body: I regret buying this. I don't know why they included the plastic. I guess they think people want to brew tea inside it. While you can remove the plastic screen, you can not remove the plastic in the spout.

Love this tea pot maker. It's so quick and easy to make tea. Plus if you're in a bind and can't wait for the water to boil while making pasta, this will boil your water immediately and you can pour it into the pot for the pasta.

text: Love it! (well maybe not so much - update Oct 25, 2018)
Body: I've seen a few other reviews about having trouble with this product but mine is great.  I drink tea every day and love that the CPK-17 has different temperature settings based on the type of tea I am in the mood for.  I think it might be a little bit overpriced but that is difficult to judge right now.  If it lasts for 10 years, it a good price.  If it lasts for one year, well then it is a terrible price.  I'll add to my review once I've had it for some time.  But honestly, it seems very well built and I've purchased Cuisinart products in the past and still have them many years later.UPDATE (Oct 25, 2018):  Had troubles after 6 months with the first unit and struggled with Cuisinart to get it returned without having to pay for shipping both ways!!!!  The second unit worked relatively well but I would have trouble setting the controls sometimes and would have to unplug it once a month to get it to work again.  It got worse in the end and I had to unplug it at least once a day! It finally died the other day forcing it into the appliance junkyard:(I decided to buy a completely different brand this time and went with Homgeek electric kettle which looks identical to the Epica electric kettle.  Why do I mention this here.  First, because I have just boxed it up after two days of service. And second, Amazon wouldn't let me review it on it's item page!  This unit has the same six temperature settings as the Cuisinart but the difference is, each time you turn it on you must hit the Set button and cycle through the temps to get to the one you want.  It defaults to 212 degrees!  That's fine if 99% of the time you only use that setting but I'll bet most people that buy a multi-temp kettle would probably find that annoying! I usually use 200 degrees so I had to hit the Set button multiple times each time I wanted a cup of tea.  I drink at least six cups a day so that got old fast!  The other issue is it didn't keep the water hot after it's cycle... you had to hit another button after you started it in order to use the Keep Warm feature. Again, every time you used the kettle.  The lid opener is built into the lid and was quite small (annoying) and also the lid came up at a small angle making it a bit more difficult to fill.  The last issue is that it didn't beep when the cycle finished.  I guess that was something I got used to with the Cuisinart.I have now replaced my Kettle with the Hamilton Beach 41020 Electric Kettle.  It looks identical to the Cuisinart and I'm guessing if I went to China I would find them being made together in the same factory on parallel assembly lines.  The difference is about $11 in favor of the Hamilton Beach!

If Arthur Dent had this, he could make his tea without needing to occupy the whole computer capacity of the Heart of Gold. Think of the whales and petunias that would be better off!If that makes no sense to you, don't panic! Just buy this kettle.Use this electric kettle to heat water to the correct temperature and enjoy a cup of tea while reading "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy" by Douglas Adams. It may not be the funniest book ever written, but it is, undoubtedly, the funniest book ever written that begins with the destruction of the Earth by Vogons, a race of bureaucrats who write terrible poetry.The kettle works simply, quickly, and safely. It lets you heat water for coffee or tea or broth or whatever, and if there's leftover water it will hold that water at the proper temperature for a while, so you can go back for a second cuppa.If you spill a bit of the hot water, just mop it up with a towel. You do know where your towel is, yes?

BEWARE. Wanted to love this kettle, and did for a while until we realized that it left a sediment in our water. My husband did many tests to verify this, including using filtered and unfiltered water and bottled and tap water, as well as two other kettles. It appears that the bottom of this kettle is pitting, which is leaving this heavy residue as shown in the photo. And this was after cleaning the kettle with white distilled vinegar. I try not to think about the amount of whatever this is that I digested. Bottom line, I do not recommend this kettle.

I have loft this product I mean I could get one for much cheaper but I loved the look and though water would stay warm with stainless steel. It has worked well thus far but i took a look inside the other day and it has rust all along the inside seem of the bottom… lord knows how long it’s been like this and we have been ingesting rust! I will be contacting the company and see what happens.

text: This Cuisinart electric kettle is not stainless steel as it claimed it was.
Body: We dislike this product after using three months because it started rusting interior/exterior.  We worry if it is safe to drink the water.  Cuisinart should be a good brand, but it needs to be re-evaluated for this particular product.

I like it a lot as it heats up small and large volumes quickly. All that doesn't matter though if quality fails: the kettle started leaking after 3 months regular usage.I contacted the seller (My Goods) for replacement and hope to update this comment when I have next steps.

text: Beeps non-stop, defective product don't buy it.
Body: This product broke right after the return policy window closed, I cannot longer return this product and now its an expensive kitchen decor, not sure if this helps but I was only boiling water using the preset for french press (200) and never used the keep it warm function. I only boiled water in the morning and never left it wired after using it.

I love Cuisineart and have used them for most of my kettles. This one is super easy to use, has good temperature control and a good water capacity. I love that it has the different water temperatures.The only thing with this one compared to my old one is that if you don’t push the start button after you’ve heated the water, it’ll keep reheating it to keep the water warm for you.All in all, it’s a great study kettle that is worth the money!

This is a great kettle. Worth every penny.  I had my first one for several years, and it worked great the entire time (we had a mishap, no fault of the product) and, I would only replace with the same exact kettle. Heats up quickly. Has various temp controls for different types of teas, from 160 to boil.  The kettle lets you know when it's ready, and easy to see the water level.  And, it looks great!  If you are looking for a quality product that will last, this one's for you.  I would highly recommend.

text: Avoid if you don't want plastic leaching into your hot water, there are plastic parts inside!
Body: There are plastic parts inside the kettle by the spout to hold the mesh filter (which is also plastic). Plastic should not come into contact with your hot drinking water, even if the plastic is BPA free. I personally do not want to be drinking microplastics so I returned the kettle.

text: plastic parts inside will degrade and add microplastic in your water!
Body: plastic parts inside will degrade and add microplastic in your water! buy the full stainless steel interior.

My kettle broke 2.5 years in.  $100 for a kettle that doesn't even last 5 years!  It also broke in a very dangerous way that could easily cause a fire: it started boiling any time you returned it to the stand.  (And yes, I've used this 3-5x daily, so I'm very sure that it wasn't on the maintain heat setting.)Their crappy warranty also didn't even offer to cross ship.  I had to buy another kettle in order to get a replacement... as it turns out, I bought a kettle because I, well, use a kettle.My T-Fal lasted a decade and cost 1/3 as much money.  I'd strongly recommend not patronizing this crappy brand.

We bought this in May of 2024 and as of the second week in November of 2024 it has begun to leak from the bottom of the kettle around the black attached base.Such a disappointment since we had another kettle exactly the same that we used for four years with no problems!  I have purchased a different brand this time because this incident has disgusted me!  It does seem like as time goes by, products become less reliable no matter who the manufacturer is!  Shame on Cuisinart!

text: Broke less than a year after purchase, Cuisinart customer service ineffective
Body: Purchased this kettle less than 1 year ago and it's already broken. The kettle will not heat when placed on the base, and the lights on the control panel blink on and off rapidly. Tried the reset instructions on Amazon and the manufacturer handbook with no success. Tried to submit a product complaint multiple times with Cuisinart directly and the form wouldn't let me submit "due to technical reasons". Save yourself the money and time and don't buy this product, buy elsewhere and from a different brand!

This kettle is not insulated and this means that the entire thing, except the handle, gets scalding hot. This is a potentially hazardous item for anyone with older folks or children who use the kitchen countertops. Absolutely will get burned if accidentally bump an arm into it or try to hold the handle and balance the actual kettle with their other hand. Terribly disappointed and sending it back immediately. I expect better from Cuisinart.

text: Black Plastic spoils a 5 star review
Body: I just received this. One of the first things I noticed was the stainless steel screens were easily removed. The stainless steel screens are contained in a black plastic frame. No problem, I removed the screens. The reason I'm knocking my rating down to 4 stars is due to the holder for the black plastic screen frame also being made of black plastic. When you pour boiling, or near-boiling water into or through black plastic we are now informed that you are releasing microplastic particles on a scale of millions, or billions, or trillions, depending on the source of your information. There is a miniature screw and nut holding that large filter frame in place, so I will remove it at some point soon.I guess we're all around 0,05% plastic at this point anyway, but I'd have been happier if there was no plastic in the path of my boiling water and they'd made these parts out of stainless steel as well.

We bought this water boiler five years ago and just threw it out today. That's a pretty decent run considering we used it multiple times per day. I like the different temperature settings, and it heats up water pretty quickly. The only major negatives other than it breaking after five years or that the bottom ended up getting stained pretty quickly, and I'm not really sure why because I only used water in it

I have been living under a rock and quit using my stove kettle after purchasing this. This thing boils fast and I get to have my coffee and tea sooner! The chamber gets really hot so be careful burning yourself. If you have children please tell them to stay away when in use. Other than that everyone should have this electric kettle.

text: Great Kettle, Unfortunately Electronics are Defective!
Body: I purchased this electric kettle because the one I had prior (though otherwise wonderful) just started to leak one day. This seems to be a chronic hazard of this category, unfortunately. I also have started drinking tea so thought having a device that would heat to different temps might be a good thing. (At the moment, I'm not entirely sure that this is important or necessary.) For these reasons, it seemed as if this, more expensive than I would normally want it to be, high quality kettle would do the trick and it is a different design than most of the others so didn't think leaking would be the problem and, so far, it's not.I've only had it for a few weeks and it is a pleasure to use and wonderful to have a kettle that doesn't intermittently leak all over the counter top at unexpected times. The problem is, as has been noted in other reviews, that the electronics in the kettle are defective. This manifests in it staying turned on long past the short time it's supposed to once it's returned to the platform. Even after I get it turned off, it will turn itself back on (as in the light) after that, at unpredictable times. Most of this is easily solved by simply not returning the kettle to the platform but alongside it, I discovered. (even when it's hot, the bottom is not hot so this can be done). I'd be willing to keep it and live with it that way if it wasn't for the fact that sometimes the electronics malfunctions in a different way, as in not turning on at all or turning itself off in the midst of trying to boil some water.For the price I paid, seems as if this should not be an issue within weeks of receiving the kettle. It was 90 something dollars. Seems to me nothing about these things is likely to improve and it's more likely to get worse until the kettle doesn't function at all. Given that it's not a manual or simple electric connection and depends on the more complex electronics, I will sadly be returning it.Now I don't know what to get.

text: It will break...Sooner or later, but likely sooner than you hope! VIOLENTLY!
Body: All the reviews with 5 stars are from the people who just bought it or owned for a little while.All the bad reviews are from the ones who owned it till it broke.Well, I took the bullet, hoping it will not happen to me, but, alas, it did, of course.While kettle worked, it rated 5 stars. Temp control, all blows and whistle. The only complain I have about its operation is that often times it switches to KEEP WARM setting, but that might be due to user error - I'm not the only one using it, and KEEP WARM button is right under START so it's very easy to push both of them if you are not careful.Goodness lasted only 8 months. From other reviews I gathered none of them lasted more than a year. So, if you find it acceptable to shell out $100 or so for this long, good for you. I certainly do not. The rating drops down to 2 stars right there for me. Customer service gives the same story as to the others - ship it to us, we ship you replacement. I pay for the postage both ways. No, thank you.It gets worse. A friend of mine bought this kettle recently, and when I visited him, I noticed the differences between his and mine.He dug out the box, and his version is Rev2 of this model, supposedly better and longer life.So I bit the bullet again (I never learn, do I? :) But I REALLY loved it when it worked)Well, the second one worked only 3 weeks! (luckily, as I was still in Amazon return window)What was not so lucky, is that it burnt, leaving a foul smell in my whole kitchen and a nasty burnt ring of some fetid black resin-like residue on my counter which I installed just a couple of months ago! And of course it would not come off! Now who's going to pay me for the new counter?Don't walk from this kettle, RUN!

I had high hopes for this water kettle, but there are some serious things poorly designed with this:1) the markings for the water temp wear off over time ( less than 1 year ).  now, i have no idea which temp is which now.  I only remember that the lowest temp is on the upper left and boil is on the lower right.2) it's hard to put on the base.  The portion of the base that has the protrusion for the electrical connection to the kettle is too high, requiring a vertical mount - dismount.  I've had other kettles with this same mechanism that were lower, which made it much easier to put the kettle on the base.  Not sure why this kettle's base needs to be so high.3) difficult to see how much you have filled - when filling from my counter top water dispenser, it's difficult to see the markings, becuase it's behind the handle, which my hand is holding on to.4) difficult to see how much water is actually in the kettle.  you can only see how much water is in there when the blue light is on, which, if you have left the kettle off for a while, turns off.  So you have to go over, pick up the kettle, place it back carefully vertically ( see point 2 ), then you can see how much water is there.  The handle obsures the view of the water indicator.5) the display panel looks like a christmas tree!  so what blue button, flashing or steady, means that this thing is actually turned on ?  or is it a white light that means that its turned on ?This kettle was replacing a $30 plastic krups kettle ( which they don't make any more, but sell a stainless version for $70 ).  The $30 was dead simple to use and solved some of the other serious usability problems.On the plus side, I do like being able to have different temps of water, but that is about the only thing that this kettle does well.

text: burns, pours badly, confusing. But only product that yields water for teas
Body: UPDATE on NOV 19, 2014.2-star review upgraded to 3-starThe problem with the pour I mentioned in my original review can be somewhat mitigated by completely removing the mesh screen. This improves the pour greatly if your kettle has enough water. However, the last half pint or so of water in the kettle will still pour out in a messy, multi-stream fashion. This is due the the fixtures built into the spout to hold the mesh screen in place. This mesh screen is an example of over-engineering a solution to a little problem that ends up creating a much greater problem. It should be kept simple  - like the Hamilton Beach kettle.My makeshift fix has made this much more usable so I've upgraded the rating from 2 to 3.-----------------------------ORIGINAL REVIEW 2-starsI also own this Hamilton Beach 40882E Stainless Steel 7.2-Cup Kettle:http://www.amazon.com/Hamilton-Beach-40882E-Stainless-7-2-Cup/dp/B004XJWQZQ/ref=sr_1_3?ie=UTF8&qid=1415988475&sr=8-3&keywords=electric+kettle+hamiltonThis Cuisinart kettle is better than the Hamilton in three regards:1. The Cuisinart has multiple temperature settings2. The Cuisinart can maintain your water at one of the set temperatures3. The Cuisinart has a nicer closing mechanism (it requires just a light touch)But in every other regard, the Hamilton Beach is superior. Here are a few of the important ones:1. The Hamilton won't burn you if touched by accident. The Cuisinart either is not insulated at all or has poor insulation. Several members of my family (me included) have accidentally burned ourselves when our hands brushed against the Cuisinart. This NEVER happens with the Hamilton. The Cuisinart requires caution that is inconvenient in comparison.2. The Hamilton pours MUCH better. Due to the use of a water screen filter on the spout, the Cuisinart pours miserably. It pours like 5 separate scattering streams of water in different directions when you pour water out. It's incredible that this design flaw somehow got past the product team at Cuisinart because it makes the kettle so hard to pour. The Hamilton has a straight forward, smooth pour that is expected of any Kettle. Cuisinart is just terrible at pouring and can spray water out of your mug accidentally.3. The Hamilton is confusing to use. When you put back the kettle onto the base after pouring out freshly heated water, the background light indicator goes blue. I have no idea what this means and the manual does not describe it either. Neither the "STart" nor the "Keep warm" button lights go on, so I'm not sure if it's keeping warm, reheating or what. It certainly doesn't look off because the blue light indicator is on. So this forces me to press the "Start" button to turn the "Start" indicator button on again, and then re-press the "Start" button again to shut off ALL the lights. This is the only way I can be certain the kettle is off after use and it's very inconvenient. Granted extra features add complexity, but this is still poorly thought through design that got past the product team.There are more smaller issues but they are not substantial.Hopefully either Cuisinart or a competitor comes out with an improved version of this soon.

text: Great kettle functionality - but has serious design flaws (some dangerous!!)
Body: We've had this kettle 2 days now and it definitely is superb with regard to heating water to the best temp for the kind of tea you drink. In fact, I can honestly say now that green and white teas are definitely wonderful when brewed at the proper temp - I never would have guessed. However, I have yet to figure out what they mean by "delicate teas"??Meanwhile, here are the design flaws that bug me and my husband:* The outsides of the kettle get super hot and you can really burn yourself seriously if you accidentally touch the sides once the kettle has boiled. The handle, of course, is fine, but it is easy to brush against the sides of the kettle with your hand.* Another problem with the kettle is the lid for the top opening: if you have boiled water, the lid gets hot like the outer sides of the kettle. This poses a problem if you have run out of water and need to refill -- you pop open the lid with the "open" button, fill the kettle, then you have to use your hand to push the lid closed. BUT... the lid may still be hot from the recent boil and you can actually burn your fingertips slightly!!* I find the kettle is weighted poorly when filled with more than 1.25L of water and it can be very difficult to pour - a dangerous problem when pouring hot water.* I personally find the opening at the top of the kettle is a bit too small. I filter my water and fill the kettle from the filter pitcher instead of the faucet. I find the kettle opening is too small to easily pour into from the pitcher, causing water to spill outside the kettle and onto the base (which is not a good idea). I am learning to stop and take careful aim with the pitcher when I fill the kettle - a really annoying inconvenience.* The beeps that sound when the water is ready are very low in volume and barely audible, even if you are standing right next to the counter.So, beware of these problems, esp. the first three items that I noted. As I indicated in the title, the kettle functionality is excellent and I am now getting to enjoy certain teas more than ever. As we have only 2 adults in our household, we can deal with the dangerous problems, but you need to decide if you want to introduce that into your home.

In April 2022 I will have had this kettle for 2 years.Pro: Sturdy design. Lid hinge is still tight, buttons haven't faded, plastic base is solid. There is plastic in a few areas: on the outside bottom of the kettle where it meets the plastic base, the handle, the inside of the lid, and inside the kettle there is a strainer between the body and spout.Pro: Heats refrigerated water to boiling in 3-4 minutes.Con: The "keep warm" function doesn't actually hold the temperature, it instead reheats the water every 15 minutes or so. This isn't a problem for me, but I understand it could be for others.Pro: Low maintenance. I use it every day, and boil a vinegar water solution in it once a month to keep any buildup away, but you could probably wait every 2 or 3 months to clean it. Keep in mind I use filtered water, not tap, so that could be why it's so low maintenance for me.Con: The opening isn't wide enough to stick my small hand inside, so a bottle brush is necessary to really scrub the walls and bottom if needed.I should also note that I sometimes do forget to pour out extra water, and therefore leave standing water overnight. I also do not dry the inside of the kettle after each use (since I can't fit my hand in there), but that has never caused any buildup or smell in my case.Overall, this is a great kettle for someone who drinks a lot of tea or coffee and wants to spend the extra money to ensure quality, but can't quite afford more expensive models, like the Fellow Stagg EKG.

I drink tea and coffee a lot. I typically boil the water in a small pot on the stove. I've never liked tea kettles with their very narrow spouts, you can't get in there and give it a good cleaning. So I stuck with my pot, until I accidentally burned it a few times and decided it was time for a change. Enter the electric kettle. I think I found out about this particular one on a blog. It's the perfect size for my needs, and I love the features. Multiple heat temperatures, automatic reheating without burning the kettle, and you can lift the pot and pour anywhere. The base plugs into the wall, and the kettle lifts out wirelessly. I also like the little window that tells you exactly how much water is in your pot, and the fact that it is almost entirely stainless steel.I saw another brand or two that looked like they might cost a bit less, but after close comparison and reading reviews, I decided this one was the best. I have not been disappointed! It works flawlessly and boils my water very quickly. When it's ready a little beep goes off a few times, and it automatically switches to warm mode to maintain temperature. So I'll never have to worry about overboiling and burning again. The handle fits my hand well and stays cool.Last but not least, it's beautifully designed, and low profile so it doesn't take up too much counter space in my small kitchen.
