And I'll never burn another pot again. Just be careful about touching the body, the metal does conduct the heat, but the handle always stays cool. Love it! Enjoy!

text: French press setting is the best
Body: I had used a prior model of electric kettle from Cuisinart for years, and was very satisfied with it's performance. Unfortunately, the removable lid had a plastic attachment to the metal dome, where the plastic just gave out. Since it was a pain to fill the kettle from the spout, I looked to see what might be a current replacement. I found a review for this one on Wirecutter, and have been using it for several days.BIG UPGRADE! The new model has a vertical design, making it easier to pour, for one. The programmed buttons for proper temperature is fantastic. I have used a French press coffee maker for decades, and I was always aware the the water temp had to be less than boiling for optimal flavor. Little did I know how much of a difference it would make. The coffee is smoother, less bitter or burnt flavor. A much better cup of Joe. My wife noticed the difference right away, having a more acute sense of taste than myself. Fortunately, she had the good taste to marry me! Anyway, big improvement from my old model. Love that Cuisinart has "smartened" the process of boiling water. I expect many years of use... 3 year warranty, btw.

I purchased this kettle a few months ago but didn’t start using it until now. Unfortunately, when I finally opened the box and tried to use it, the kettle didn’t work at all. The lights flash, but no matter what buttons I press, it won’t function. I’ve always been a fan of Cuisinart products, but this experience is extremely disappointing—especially considering it’s more expensive than other brands.

Hello. I did not encounter any problems when I started using my product. My mother-in-law has the same product. I thought it was moss because it was old and could not be cleaned. Now I have the same problem. The inside of the product has turned green as if it had moss. This second product gave the same problem.

I bought this electric kettle less than six months ago, and it already started to rust, which is extremely disappointing. For the price, I expected much better quality. My previous kettle lasted over five years without any rust issues, so seeing this happen so quickly is unacceptable. I wouldn't recommend this product if you're looking for something durable and reliable. Definitely not worth the money.

text: Rust after less than one month
Body: I purchased this kettle after researching various kettles and thinking cuisinart has good reviews and steep pricetag.This kettle seems its not the best quality. I already have rust inside the kittle (see attached picture) and then writings on the buttons have already scratched partially.

text: Good kettle while it lasts. Warranty sub-par.
Body: I love this kettle. However, the lining has peeled off at the bottom on the kettle. It's now that I realize that Cuisinart makes you pay shipping both ways if you want a new kettle under their warranty. Why should the customer have to pay 30 dollars to the company for a product that is defective and cannot survive the three years covered by the warranty.Update: I loved this kettle, but now I realize it was a waste of money. The lining is completely in disarray with the first layer missing halfway up the kettle and a large portion of the bottom skinned to the black material that is under the first two layers of lining. Poor quality. I expected something more from Cuisinart. Moving onto more reliable electric kettle brands like Zojirushi.

This product is great except leaking at the bottom of the water level indicator after it being used for a while. We replaced the water pitcher but the leaking happens again. Now I may have to look into other brands for the next water heater. I am afraid the leaking may cause short circuits or electrical fire.

After looking out for electric kettle for almost three months and finding it difficult to choose one, I settled in for this Cuisinart electric kettle and sure I don’t regret it. It is so easy to use and the handles don’t slip. I used to own big electric water dispenser and it would take up too much space in the counter. This one is small, looks cute in the counter and perfect for a tea lover. Highly recommend this product.

Bought this kettle in 2016, and it's still working great.  No issues with the numbers wearing off, no issues with the lid, no issues with the base.  A great electric kettle, definitely worth the price.

text: dead after 6 years of hard work
Body: I'm not sure how to rate this product. We own 3 of these kettles and have loved them. Two continue to work perfectly.But one of them died this week after 6 years of service. NOT what I expect from a product in this price range. Full confession - the kettle was a workhorse and was boiling water at least 20 times a day. The first indication of trouble was the kettle continuing to boil and then reboil within a minute of the first boil. Then it just stopped beeping at all. In the end the auto shut off wouldn't work. We ended up buying another of the same model, thinking maybe it was something we did?! But be aware of these issues.

text: Leaked after a year- don't leave full
Body: Props to Quisinart for sending a replacement at no cost.After a little over a year of daily use, the Kettle began leaking from the bottom and onto the base. I contacted Quisinart via their online submission saying that I'mconcerned about a fire hazard.They replied to stop using it right away and they will send a replacement (they requested a photo showing that I intentionally cut the power cord, permanently disabling the kettle).I will no longer leave water in the kettle after use to hopefully avoid this happening again. I like this kettle and don't want to move to another brand.

text: Great functionality, but potential fire/safety hazard
Body: I’ve used two of these kettles now, and have always been very happy with the functionality, but unfortunately both reached the end of their lifespans in the same way: First, the spring-loaded mechanism in the lid failed, so that it stopped popping up when opened, and you’d have to open it manually with your hands or a utensil. More worryingly, both kettles started leaking water all over their electrical base/mount. So, unfortunately I can’t really recommend it as it seems to become dangerous with age.It does seem like the lid consistently fails before the leaking starts, so if you’re determined to get it, I might recommend treating the lid failure as a sign that it’s time to replace the kettle, because at that point, it’s only a matter of time before the leaking starts.

Ok, for the past 6 years I have had a Breville kettle and crew been very happy with it. I use it many times throughout the day as I am an avid tea drinker. When its lid broke I had to buy a new kettle and the Cuisinart has great reviews and is quite a bit cheaper.It does the job. And if I didn't have my breville to compare it against, I would likely have been satisfied.. The prosLike the breville it has settings for different temps which is good for teaIt has a bell to let you know when it's reached tempIt has a small footprint on the counter.It has a very visible window to let you know how much water remains.The consIt's noisyIt doesn't stay to temp as well and isn't automatically keeping it to tempThe top opening is small, making cleaning more difficult.Since the temp. selections are in the handle it is fatter and less comfortable to pourIts has a tad cheaper feel to it than the Breville.I will keep it but, I wish i had just swallowed hard and paid the extra 40 bucks

text: Review 8-years post purchase - Mostly good, some cons
Body: We purchased the Cuisinart Electric Kettle almost 8-years ago. For the most part, we have been very happy. We use it multiple times every day.Pros:- It heats water quickly.- It's easy to use. It has different temps for different kinds of tea at the push of a button.Cons:- The labels have worn off the START, OPEN, and Boil Black buttons as well as the 1,25L, 1.5L, and 1.7L water level markings.- The spring that pops the lid open when OPEN is pressed broke after 6-years of use. The lid was stuck in the closed position. We filled the kettle through the spout.- We've also had trouble removing mineral build-up on the inside, but that would probably happen with any electric kettle. Now that the lid is stuck shut, it's nearly impossible to clean on the inside.We finally decided to get a new kettle and are opting for a different brand adjustable temperature kettle with a glass kettle.

We purchased this tea kettle on our 10th wedding anniversary after the one we were gifted finally gave up. The design is classic and beautiful. It's easy to keep clean. I haven't had any issues with the bottom of the kettle getting dirty or scaly. The auto shut off is great and will kick on after returning water to the specific temp 3 times. It holds almost 2 liters of water. I hope they never change the design. It looks the best of all options out there.

text: Works well with variety of temp settings
Body: Gets as hot as you like, quickly.  The “stay at temp” feature took a minute to figure out.  Just touch START button again to turn off the kettle.  I like it.

Beware of the design flaw! The unit work well until there is mold in water window area. It was used to heat water only.  Since there is no access to the water window area, there is no way to remove the mold and thus making the unit useless now. Contacted customer service to see if they have any suggestion on how to clean it.  They gave me useless suggestion and I quote “wipe the kettle and base of the unit with a soft, damp cloth.”  No other help was offer.

text: Defective kettle Keep Warm feature  turns itself on.
Body: This kettle is horrible. The keep warm features kept turning itself on after I switch it off, to the point that it had damaged the base of my cabinet with steam. I called cuisinart and had the most bizarre customer service experience, the  customer service representative listened  to my complaint and then put me on hold, when he came back, the very versatile customer service  rep. told me that he had 'plugged the kettle in and tested it in the lab and that it is defective as described'. He offered me a new kettle as it was under limited warranty, the new kettle would have cost me $30-. I declined and he said I could file a complaint with upstairs  which I did, He would  only take my phone number and not my email for this complaint and I was  told I would be contacted in 3-4 days. Eight days later I still have not been contacted by upstairs, so  I called again today and this time the rep. did not leave me on hold to run to the lab to test the kettle  and  I was offered a replacement for free.  No thanks, I can't damage another cabinet. I filed another complaint with upstairs  and will hear back in 3-4 days, maybe...

I have purchased this replacement unit in 2022 after the one (same model) I had for 9 years have stopped working.  However, I noticed something wrong with this replacement unit after using it for about a year.  Its auto shut-off feature fails to work occasionally, which causes pot to continue boiling water until the entire water evaporates.  The only way to stop boiling water is to un-plug the power cable from the power outlet.  Basically, the “off” selection button won’t work, and its auto shutoff feature also would not work.  I have reported this problem to Cuisinart’s support team last year, but no response was given so far.  I am very disappointed.

text: Not reliable; going on my third unit under warranty.
Body: Bought this because of the Cuisinart name, stainless steel and apparent discount off retail price ($80 vs. $185), along with pretty decent reviews. It worked fine, even if it heated more slowly than I expected. [Having lived in Europe I've experienced $15 electric kettles boiling water twice as fast as this one.] So while not thrilled, I was content with this kettle because it did what it said it did -- until it didn't anymore. It lasted a year, and yes, I descale every couple of weeks with vinegar. I got warranty replacement, which cost $15 for shipping plus I needed to pay to ship the broken one back to them, and the second unit died after a year. Now I'm going on my third unit (at least they're not charging me for shipping this time, but I still need to pay to ship the broken one to them) and I don't expect it to last much longer than the remainder of the warranty, which is three years from the date of original purchase. Maybe I got a couple of lemons and the third one's the charm; I just think a kettle this pricey should last a minimum of five or ten years.

I really enjoyed using this kettle very much. However, it stopped working after 3.5 years. The electronic buttons on the handle no longer respond. It's been used carefully by one person over the years and the handle has never been exposed to water or mishandled.. I contacted Cusinart but they do not fix these kettles should they break. There is a 3 year warranty but I am just beyond it. I now need a new kettle but as much as I truly enjoyed using this one, I won't purchase again. I don't think it's reasonable for a product at this price point, $80.00,  to not last longer than a few years. Othert than this fatal flaw, I thought the kettle was wonderful and even recommended it many times to friends and family. I did goggle DIY fixes and there were several people who replaced the electronics in the handle themselves. I wouldn't attempt it and would worry should it could be a fire hazard. I'd like to see Cuisnart improve on the quality and value of this product.

This teapot delivers diminished returns with its increased complexity. I go through buckets of tea. This electric kettle has changed for the worse, and at this price, I'm disappointed. More complex mechanisms don't equal a better teapot, just more things that can go wrong. The designer was enamored of cool blue light, so made odd changes that look nice on paper, but don't work in real life. The water-fill line is very hard to read, however lit by the glowing blue light. It's been inexplicably moved from the side, to being placed under the handle. You have to fill the kettle from the top, holding the handle, which makes it hard to see what's going on. And the measurements are now in liters, not cups. Importantly, the kettle is almost impossible to turn off! Even if you turn it off prior to pouring, it will turn-on again the minute you place it back on the heating element, and overheat. If you don't turn it off again by clicking twice, lights will flash. Watch out! Then, the only way you can turn off the demented, overheated thing is fill it with water, turn it on, then turn it off with repeated clicks. Or unplug it. And fill it with water to cool it off. I strongly suggest that for safety, unplug it after every use! If you don't, and it inadvertently gets bumped, even a little bit, it can come back on by itself when empty. Silly, silly design changes. The pour spout doesn't even work as well. We'll see if this works for five years, like the last one did. I don't care about the temp for white tea, and preferred the previous model, a good, workmanlike kettle, unhindered by these "innovations."

text: Very satisfied -- until it stopped working
Body: I bought this kettle three years ago, in 2016, based on a personal recommendation, and I loved it. It boils (or heats to whatever temperature) water fast, has lots of nice settings including keep warm, sounds a gentle tone when the water is ready, and it's made by Cuisinart, a brand I trust. I have a lot of Cuisinart items in my kitchen. This teakettle has been used at least once and up to three times a day for the past three years.Recently, its brain has started to become scrambled. Sometimes, after it boils water, it fails to stop boiling and just keeps going and going until I manually turn it off. Sometimes all the lights blink on and off rapidly and I have to unplug the whole thing to reboot. Often the keep warm function doesn't work, and I love that function as I can't always get to the kettle to pour as soon as it boils. Maybe there's just too much electronic paraphenalia in this device. Sometimes, simpler is better. I have just ordered the bestselling Secura (for less than half the price of the Cuisinart) and am hoping for the best.

There is plastic on the inside!It’s bad enough that the inside of the lid is plastic, where gets hit with steam the whole time. There is also plastic on the inside below the spout, so every time you’re pouring boiling water out, it’s passing over plastic. How is this even allowed?

Was a good kettle while it lasted, but the button to open/close the lid stopped working with minimal use. I called cuisinart and they did not try to help or fix..or give discount words a new kettle. Will be replacing with a different brand that stands by their quality…. Seems like planned obsolescence at play here.

The kettle has been a let down. I've only boiled water in it 4 times and it's already got marks at the bottom and still emits an awful chemical smell preventing me from drinking it. It makes a grinding noise when mounting on the base and the lid was attached askew. My friend has the same model and it's great no issues, but I haven't been so lucky. They have the brushed colour, I chose the normal stainless which is $40 cheaper on Amazon at the moment... concerned they might be selling off 'seconds' instead as the quality is lacking. I have swapped for a second unit but am concerned about getting the same issues, this experience is making me consider a stove top kettle..

text: Wanted to love it and would but.....
Body: I love the design,  the appearance,  and features of this Kettle.Cuisinart really needs to improve this Kettles rust issue.  This Kettle was delivered Dec 3rd, I started using it Dec 4th, and as of today Dec 7th, you can see inside at the bottom of the Kettle it is starting to ware. I've only used the 190° Oolong temperature in the morning.For this price point is it to much to ask for a better material,  metal, coating, whatever other then the "barely" brushed  stainless steel they used.I haven't found a similar Kettle with the features as this one,  which i really like. But I'll keep looking.  This bad boy is headed back to them.

text: Great...for placebo buttons and burning coffee
Body: People must not actually bother testing this product, because the fancy buttons are just a placebo.The 200°/"French Press" setting literally pegged my thermometer that I use to stir the grounds with, meaning the temperature is closer to 260°, and it scalded my coffee.The 160°/"Delicate" setting almost did the same thing, pegging the meter at least at 220°.The whole point of this stupid thing was so that I didn't have to fiddle with heating up and cooling down and heating up and cooling down boiling water in the morning to get 200°.What a piece of garbage.

text: Poor reliability for a near $100 kettle.
Body: Like many other reviews, my kettle started leaking at the base after the 3rd month of near daily usage. There is nothing to try adjusting to see where the leak is coming from but it's dangerous to use at this point so we are in the process of working through warranty support.

I literally just had this arrive on my front door earlier today and it already stopped working. Cleaned it/rinsed it to test boiling feature  and it worked but took about 3-5 mins. Then when I washed it, left it alone for an hour to cool down to test again, and the temp sensor suddenly doesn’t work or the heating element ?? Totally weird… maybe I got a dud? Returning to get a new one but if the new kettle doesn’t work either then I’m just going to go back to a cheap Hamilton beach kettle honestly …

2 stars only for the amount of years which kettle can work😃 The best kettle for 2 years only( It’s start dripping after 2 yearst. I bought first kettle in 2018 and it stop working (dripping water) in 2020 - got a new one by the warranty and now (2022) the new one start dripping again( Their support team is real good - they are trying to solve your problem as fast as possible.

text: I now have owned two if those.  Both started to leak on a bottom side within 15-18months.
Body: I now have owned two of those.  Both started to leak on a bottom side within 15-18months...and  it becomes a stainless steel junk. I would like to see those last at least 5 years for the money spent.... Is it really that hard to design a kettle that can work that long? About to get one for 1/3rd or 4th of the price of this one and see how those other work. Unless this major leaking problem is resolved I would  stay away.... I guess if you don't mind getting a new one every year and a half go for it. At this point they should have a kettle subscription service where they just every year and a half send you a new one for $99. :/

text: Decent, but not buying another one.
Body: After about 4.5 years, one of the springs in the lid broke, so it wouldn't open properly. We started filling it through the spout instead.  At 5.5 years, the heating element has failed, rendering the unit inoperable.  I tested the element with a multimeter to confirm it. The element is fused to the base of the kettle, so I can't replace it.We used this kettle every day and often multiple times per day. We frequently used the different temperature settings and were happy with the performance. The outside gets hot which makes it tough for kids to handle. Overall we were reasonably satisfied with this kettle, but would have liked it to last longer for the price.  Probably the most useful feedback I can offer is that we are not buying another one. We're looking into a hot water tap instead.  Failing that, we'll look for a cheaper option that will probably last equally long.
I had to buy another one after my previous same model kettle lasted 8 years!!!!! I know I can trust this brand. I make tea for my family 1-3 times each day. This is #1 kettle.
Have had this for four years and it’s still works like it was new. I highly recommend this product. While it is a little more expensive, you are paying for quality, dependability, and reliability.

Love love love!!!! I am a very big tea drinker and I have been looking for an electric kettle like this one for awhile. I seen this one in a few stores but found it $20+ cheaper on Amazon so I decided to go ahead and buy it. So glad I did!! This kettle is so easy to use, just 2 buttons and your kettle is brewing at the perfect temperature. This kettle heats up so quickly. I also love the swivel base which makes it easy for us leftys or my right handed husband to pick up. I love the keep warm option so I can have multiple cups without waiting. It looks great on my countertop too! Only thing is to be aware of is the outside of the kettle gets really hot, so keep out of reach from little ones!

The Cuisinart gives me exactly what I need.  Convenience. As a Tea blogger, brewing a good cuppa at the right temperature is critical.  The only thing I needed the directions for was to make sure there were no top secret rituals I needed to do in order to initialize the thing for its first run.  It was pretty simple. Just rinse, fill and go.  It is pretty darn self explanatory.  In FACT, it is so awesome, if you forget which tea requires which temperature, that’s okay.  The handle temperature buttons have the tea recommendations written on them!  Needless to say I am quite pleased with my new Temperature variable tea kettle, and I hope I will brew many wonderful cups of tea from the water I heat with it. MY full review from my blog:teawithlia dot com

text: Lasted 3 months then began to rust!
Body: I love the way you can control the temperature. However, the bottom on the inside began to rust after just 3 months. Contacted customer service and they said they don't warrant against rust. Imagine that!  A product that claims to be stainless steel begins to rust. No telling what chemicals or bits of metal we have been drinking! Stay away if you value your health.

Worst product I ever purchased in my entire life. You boil water, then you serve your hot beverage and you put the pot back and if god forbid you forget to press Start to stop it … it goes back and the only way to turn it off is pouring water again and then only it will turn off…. Mine flew outside the window and I will never buy an article from this brand again.

text: Broken in less than a month!
Body: This was our 2nd Cuisinart electric tea kettle.  The first one worked perfectly and lasted for many years.  I ordered this replacement about 3 weeks ago, and in that time, it has overheated, failed to turn on when buttons were pressed, would turn on for 30 seconds and shut itself off, started a rapid boil when it was just supposed to be warming the water, and generally behaved like it was hacked or was completely defective.  I would NOT recommend this product due to safety concerns.

NONE of ANY manufacturer's offerings of Electric Kettles are worth cr-p, and this one this Cuisinart is no exception.  They ALL are designed to fail in a year or two.  Lid failures are number one (and this one has a fancy pop up lid); base failure/connectivity are number two (it looks like Cuisinart made the center post on the base higher for this reason, and this could be a "plus" for longevity).  Problem is there's other stuff:  The pour spout being quite wide at the tip, combined with an unusual "lip" or "baffle" inside the vessel makes pouring erratic and uninspiring.  In fact, when the vessel is about half full, it can commence pouring quickly and with considerable volume with the slightest tip. Not something I like when I'm pouring water over coffee grounds in my single serve coffee filter (it sloshes).  The large diameter handle is also cumbersome.  The temp selections work well for now, but I have to wonder how long the contacts inside these will last.  Seriously, all these kettles are junk, that are DESIGNED to break, but some are better than others (for awhile).  For $100 Cuisinart could have put one of their better engineers on this; clearly they did not.

text: If you are buying this because of wirecutter, reconsider their motives and critical thinking
Body: We were ready for a 2nd kettle, replacing a braun that has served us well and still works.This is a kettle. A unique thing that I don't really care about, but took the reviewers word for it, is the temp control. It works, but it's inferior to our 10yr old braun in many ways.1) The exterior gets hot enough to severely burn you. Why would they do that? The handle is fine, but the entire body is the same temp as the water. A major safety concern.2) There is no way to turn off the unit unless you remove from base or unplug it. Lots of annoying blue blinking lights. Also, hard to tell if it is heating or not.3) It's actually slow to boil, this blew me away. Our old braun is about 20% faster for the same rated output.4) Ours failed after a week of use. It no longer stops heating when the water starts boiling, it continues to boil the water until you remove it from the plate or unplug. Super dangerous, so we're returning this.It's so crazy to me that wirecutter rated this their top unit. I have typically followed their recommendations without second guessing. Good lesson.
Cuisinart has another kettle with zero plastic touching the water. Not sure why they can’t do that here too. Returned because of the plastic.
I have had this kettle a few years, so maybe it is just old, but it no longer turns off, but keeps boiling water even when I switch it off. I have to unplug it to get it to cool down. Not great.

text: 3 things I don't like; 1 I do.
Body: I am comparing this to my Braun (German-made) electric kettle, which stopped working after 20 years.  Braun no longer makes an electric kettle for America.  First, the design.  The window for seeing how much water is in, is under the handle.  This makes it difficult to see, as your hand is there.  The Braun had 2 windows, one on the left, and one on the right, so  you can easily see as you fill it how much water you are putting in. Second, The Braun had a filter in the spout that prevented anything other than water from pouring out of the kettle; for instance, calcium deposits from hard water.  I have hard water,  and this means I have to clean the Cuisinart more often than I did the Braun. Third, you have to have at least half a liter in the Cuisinart, whereas I only had to have 6 ounces in the Braun.  I make a 12 oz. coffee in the morning, dripping directly into my mug, so I have to eyeball the level in my mug.  These things might not matter to you, and maybe Cuisinart has a more expensive electric kettle with these features corrected.  On the plus side, I can program the Cuisenart to keep the water warm.
Heats water fast. For the price, there should not be marks and discoloration on the outside of the pot

I've used the Cuisinart CPK-17P1 frequently for two months now. The temperature functions are good, the speed of heating is good, it's very sturdy. What prevents it from being among the better kettles I've used is that it does not pour very well once water level gets low. A smooth pour turns into a splash and spray, and then the last of the water comes out very reluctantly. I believe it has something to do with the assembly insde the kettle which holds the screen which covers the spout. I don't think the screen is necessary, but simply removing the screen does not fix the issue. I would probably look for a different kettle next time, but l'll give this kettle four stars.

text: This is our third one...They last about 7-8 years but work reliably in all that time.
Body: We use this kettle 3-4 times a day on average...that's about 1,200-1,300 times a year.  It has ranked as one of the best in all of the reviews and after trying others we agree that it is still the best one we've come across.It is not as fancy as some of the new ones, but really, how fancy do you need to heat water?!?  It has all of the preset temperatures we want and need, it stores plenty of water, and when you hit the hold temperature button it will continue to hold the temperature even if you pour some and put the kettle back on the base.

This is a WONDERFUL kettle!!!! I love that I can pick the temperature that I want the water to be for the type of tea I am making! The water heats quickly and the kettle is also very easy to keep clean.

text: It’s the best teakettle I’ve ever had.
Body: Looks nice on my counter and to boil water, it is very quick and easier than boiling water in a pot as I’ve had to do! Capacity is large, and shuts off automatically! I love it!

After booking water, if you leave the water in it, its outside temperature is more than 180F.  The photo shows 174F because I couldnt hold longer, I then saw 183F. Also it is not by any means faster than T-Fal Vitesses kettle I bought 10 years ago. It boils 1.5 liters in 6 min 35 seconds, versus T-Fal boiled in 6 minutes 10 seconds.

Got this about a month ago and have used it nearly every day since, usually multiple times a day.  The water heats quickly to the desired temperature.  In addition to heating cups of water for tea, I also use it to quickly bring water to a boil for cooking pasta, etc.  I love being able to heat the water to specific temperatures for different types of tea, and this was the main reason I selected this kettle.While I was also looking for a stay-warm feature, I now find that I hardly ever use it.  The water retains its heat for long periods anyway, so I usually find it is easier to just quickly reboil the water when I'm ready for more than to keep it heating for a half-hour straight.  I think this feature will be much more useful for entertaining.As some people have noticed, this kettle is pretty loud when boiling water.  I use another electric kettle at work (also Cuisinart) which is quieter, as is my good-old-fashioned stove-top kettle.  I find it's louder when boiling smaller quantities of water, but I still love the kettle.  This is just a heads up.One other small annoyance is that the water level guide fills slowly, so if you're trying to be precise you have to pour slowly, pause, and wait for the guide to catch up.  I'm assuming it is designed this way so most of your boiling water isn't touching the plastic guide, which is nice, just something to be aware of.Overall, this is a fantastic kettle which is absolutely worth adding to your kitchen!UPDATE: I've been using this kettle multiple times a day for nearly a year and I still love it.  As some others have mentioned the text rubs off on the most used buttons. I've found this mostly happens if you touch them when your fingers are wet. Love this kettle!

I love cuisnart products, and I was very happy to find this stainless steel electric water kettle. However, despite the reviews I have read  here, I bought the item, and I was disappointed. It looks very chic on the counter top but the water it boils smells like plastic. I boiled 5 pots of water before I actually used it and the smell still didn't go away. On the website, it says the plastic they use is BPA free so thats not the issue but I hate the smell. I will be returning the item for sure.But if you don't mind the smell, this kettle boils the water in 7 min if you fill it to the max amount (1.7 Liter) - which is pretty quick. Also, when its boiling water, the outside surface is hot to touch. when I was cooking, my arm touched it by mistake and now I have a minor burn on my arm :/ yeah I know thats my clumsiness, but if you have kids around the house or if you are clumsy like me, thats another issue to watch out for.I gave 1 star to this item because 1) the water it boils smells like plastic, 2) I would rather to have all stainless steel and glass compartments rather than plastic compartments for the price I paid, 3) I will burn myself with this item  -  But on the plus side, it looks fancy and boils water fast.

Yes, it heats well, and probably to the temperature I set. Variable temp is nice. I don't care that the outside gets a little hot. We've had it for a while so it seems to last (so far).Now the cons:-The beep. For a tea lover, for whom tea represents a gentle morning wakeup, chai on Indian trains, hearty mugs in old English kitchens, and tea salons in Paris, the clinical-sounding beep when the water is done was a turnoff from the first boil.-The logic. This pot thinks it knows me. It's like the Apple of electric kettles. If you take the pot off before the completion beep and put it back on the base, it continues to heat (guess what? I already poured my water, which is why I took it off). It defaults to the Keep Warm setting, so it continues to waste energy and add mild noise pollution to my kitchen unless I remember to turn off that setting.-The choices. They obviously just threw in an Oolong setting to have an even six buttons for symmetry. In the morning, when my kids haven't slept and I need my cup of strong black tea, my eyes can hardly sort through all the text and numbers.I was going to give this three stars, but as I write this I realize just how much this kettle annoys me. Two stars.

text: I loved it when it worked!!
Body: I had this product three months and it died.  The worst part is when I called Amazon I was told I could return it, but would have to repay the original shipping cost, pay a 20% restock fee and pay to ship the defective one back.  Can you say utterly horrible customer service?!?!  I have bought many items from Amazon and only had to return a couple.  I guess I should be thankful they arrived damaged and that I haven't encountered this dismal policy until now.  I will never purchase a more expensive electronic item from Amazon again and am SO thankful I opted to buy my food processor from Costco last month instead!  If I have a problem with it I know Costco will simply return the item.  Thanks, but I'll stick with them in the future.  On the up side... The third person I spoke with at Cuisinart, Craig, was fantastic!  I made several phone calls due to troubleshooting.  Craig agreed that three months was an unreasonable product life and shipped me out my new tea kettle at no charge.  I'm waiting for it to arrive and will return this one in the same box. Thank you Craig and thank you Cuisinart, because I do love this machine!  I have owned their standard kettle for several years and never had a problem with it.  I bought this one, because Teavana has made me tea crazy and I wanted the different temps.  It's a great machine - just hope my first one was a fluke and my second is as reliable as my old standby.

text: Doesn't always work, replaced first one, customer service a nightmare
Body: The first kettle I received worked for a few weeks, then the blue LED refused to turn off while the unit was plugged in. I called customer service and was initially told that I was wrong and that the blue light is never supposed to turn off. I called back and the second rep confirmed that I was indeed correct, that pressing the "Start" button twice should turn the unit off completely, LED and all. She sent a replacement and requested that I return the original, and that I pay postage myself for the return. I have never been lied to by a customer service representative and I have never been asked to pay to return a company's defective product before. I will never buy another Cuisinart appliance ever again. The replacement unit works better than the first, however occasionally when I turn it on to heat up water and walk away I return several minutes later to find that the unit has turned itself off. This is frustrating when I am on a tight schedule and sometimes I have gone without tea because I did not have the time to turn the unit on again and wait for it to warm up before leaving the house. I give it two stars instead of one because the replacement unit does work 90 percent of the time.

text: Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp Kettle - Life Story - Continued
Body: Had our CPK since May of 2012 - using it 2-4x per day without a problem - just failed today not quite 3 years old.  Would give it 3.5 stars but had to commit - so only 3.Like the kettle very much - was clear what temperature you have selected, beep to indicate temperature has been reached is fairly loud but not obnoxious.  Keep warm is nice but being able to have it shut down when temp is reached is very good as well.  Handle remains cool even after repeated uses (we often would boil water to use for cooking / makeup of loss when preparing food for company).Having said that there are issues to be aware of.Less than 3 years of use before it failed (not a statistically- significant sample size of one unit - should see how many folks have had failures and withing what length of time).Numbers/text on the buttons is silk-screened. Numbers on the most used buttons wore off in about 1 yr.  After a year or so of more of cleanings the balance of the numbers and text wore off.When hot the lid would stick shut and required a tap in order to pop open.Never had any other issues - looking for a new electric kettle and depending on available capacity and features may buy this one again.== 6/1/2016 Update == Bought a replacement February 22nd 2015 - this one worked until May 25th 2016.  Daily use - actually 2-3 x per day is pretty typical as we are a familiy of tea / coffee drinkers.  This unit's numbers stayed on - no issues. Lid also sticky hot or cold but worked better than the predecessor.  Will attempt to get warranty replacement / service but will order a replacement unit in the near term as it is now an integral part of our lives...  will add to this update after trying to get service.  Stay tuned...

text: Works great, once you get one that works
Body: Update as of 01/01/2013:  I have had my replacement for a little over a month now and it is still working and I love it, though I still half expect it to not work every time I plug it in.  It is fast (much faster than my stove) and I like being able to set the perfect temperature for every cup of tea.  Cuisinart seems to have some production quality issues, and I am still disappointed that they don't stand behind their products better, but based on the reviews of the other kettles out there, this isn't unique to Cuisinart.Original review:  I read the reviews on the various electric kettles and between the mostly positive reviews and my satisfaction with other Cuisinart products, I made my purchase.I loved it for the first week and a half; we used it every day.  Then it just stopped working. The back-lighting for the water level comes on but none of the other lights come on and none of the buttons work.  I tried to "reboot" the system by removing the kettle from the base for 5 minutes then replacing it.  When that didn't work, I tried unplugging the unit and leaving it for an hour before plugging it back in. Neither worked.I then called Cuisinart.  They informed me they would be happy to replace it - but that I would be responsible for paying shipping each way.  I was disappointed by this (though I had read about it in other reviews so wasn't surprised).  Amazon is wonderful - they are refunding my purchase.I do plan to place an order to replace this and give Cuisinart another chance - I do understand that there are always defects in the manufacturing process.  I'll update this review after the new one also stops working, or after a reasonable amount of time of continuous functioning. (For reference, this review was written 11/12/2012.)

I bought this kettle when my previous one wore out.  It was more expensive than other kettles, but the features sounded useful and it had great reviews.  After using it for months, I'm tossing it in the goodwill bin because it's so frustrating to use.  The multitude of buttons and lights means I sometimes think it's boiling water, but it's not.  It is almost impossible to monitor the water level as I fill it in the sink, due to the narrow window to the interior.  I haven't found the keep-warm feature to be helpful.  As for safety , when it recently ran dry it didn't shut off, but instead made frightening cracking noises until I turned it off manually.  I'm going back to a glass kettle with a simple on-off switch.  Unless you really need water to be heated to different temperatures, save your money and skip this one.

text: First look at what teas you drink! (avoid my mistake) also the outside does get hot
Body: I had high hopes. This does work great, but I thought the outside would not get hot and it does get hot. My daughter loves to make tea and I thought she could use this, especially since I am thinking of tossing our microwave since I try to avoid using it. I drink a lot of herbal teas, and my husband black tea, so I'm not sure if it is worth the extra money to have all the temp settings since they recommend boiling water to steep, but I personally like the water less hot so I can drink it without the wait to cool off. Again, I'm not sure if this is worth the extra money for most of us tea drinkers. I was very surprised that the teas I drink call for boiling the water."The temperature at which you steep tea matters - delicate leaves steeped at too high of a temperature will burn and leave a bitter flavor in the cup. Each two leaves tea company™ tea has recommended steep temperatures, but there are a few hard and fast rules you can follow to determine what steep temperature to use:Below Boiling Water TemperatureWhite and green teas have delicate leaves, and therefore require below boiling water temperatures between 170 and 185 degrees Fahrenheit. Too high of a temperature will cook the leaves and ruin their delicate flavors.Medium Boil TemperatureOolong teas should be brewed at temperatures between 180 and 190 degrees Fahrenheit.Full Boil TemperaturesBlack and Herbal teas brew best at a full boil temperatures 208 and 212 degrees Fahrenheit." From Two Leaves website"

::::: BACKGROUND :::::After years of having really bad coffee and tea, I started to educate myself. While there are SO many elements that go into a good cup of joe/tea, one of the biggest and most overlooked issues is brewing temperature. I have and use both afor pour-over coffee (the best method I've ever used) and a Teavana Perfect TeaMaker for teas. Both require pouring water through the top.For the longest time, I used a tea kettle for all of my water-heating needs. Then I thought I wanted an inexpensive electric kettle, one that just heats until boiling and then shuts off (I'm not sure why, that wouldn't have done anything differently). But then I realized that I really need precise temperature control; a different temperature for every kind of tea and coffee is different still. That's when the Cuisinart came into view.::::: PERFORMANCE :::::The kettle heats very quickly. It's really nice that the heating element is actually in the base of the unit, shaving off a cord and weight from the kettle itself. While I haven't double-checked the temperature to see how accurate it is, I must say that I have noticed a drastic difference in taste with all but black tea (which should be brewed at boiling anyway). My whole life I thought I hated green tea and I couldn't figure out why oolong from a Chinese restaurant tasted so much better than at home. The brewing temperature!::::: BUILD :::::This has a very nice, strong build and looks very handsome on the counter. At first I thought the blue light on the water level window and buttons looked tacky, but now I rather like it. The "stainless" steel exterior is incredibly vulnerable to smudges and fingerprints, to the point that some marks seem to be permanently on there, no matter how hard I scrub. The lid has some sort of spring mechanism and opens very smoothly. There's also a removable screen in the spout that seems kind of silly to me; it could only filter very large particules, larger than anyone would have in their source water. Seems kind of pointless to me!::::: ERGONOMICS :::::The handle has pretty good placement, balancing the weight of the water quite nicely, allowing a nice, even pour. The spout also gives a nice, steady stream. The streamlined base is really nice and includes the heating element and single cord.::::: OPTIONS :::::The temperature selections are pretty convenient; that IS the point of this product. In a perfect world, this would be a variable selector, allowing you to dial in the exact temperature, but I'm guessing that would be more costly. Each button not only has a prescribed temperature, but a suggested substance to brew with that water. For example, I most frequently use 200º French Press, which really should just say "Coffee". Coffee is optimally brewed at 195-205º, so this preset is spot-on.The keep warm function works really nicely for me. In the case of brewing coffee via Chemex, you need to pour over rather slowly, as to not flood and underexpose the grounds. Periodically placing the kettle back on the base instantly heats the water right back to 200º and I'm good to go.::::: OVERALL :::::All in all, I'm very happy with this kettle. It's a great brand, is nice looking, free of BPA, and offers convenient and (at least relatively) accurate presets. Most importantly, it helps me brew all of my favorite beverages at the proper temperature, yielding a VERY noticeably better drink. Though it's relatively expensive, its very worth it to me! Highly recommended!::::: COFFEE SETUP :::::Just as an extra plug, I use this as a part of my perfect-coffee trio:---I've never had a better cup than what this makes!

I’ve been very happy with this purchase so far. I gave up coffee years ago and switched to tea, which is still an important ritual for me every morning. It was only recently that I learned the importance of steeping tea at lower temperatures.My teapot was getting shabby and I was tired of pouring scalding water into my cup so I bought an inexpensive electric kettle thinking that would be enough to regulate the temperature. I ended up returning it because it made the water taste like metallic plastic. The next kettle I bought (which was a bit more expensive) was a very different color than advertised and the “Keep Warm” function was defective.You get what you pay for. I decided to shell out for this one because Cuisinart is a trusted brand and it’s an appliance I use multiple times a day. I haven’t been disappointed. What I like the most is that the kettle knows how hot the water is. It will adjust how long it boils the water depending on the current temperature, which is how it keeps it warm.It’s also quick and quiet. I wish I could have gotten it in a more aesthetically pleasing color, but I’ll live. Five stars.

text: Works great, a little noisy, but reliable
Body: I bought the "premium stainless steel" on.  I've been using this daily for over a year now, sometimes twice a day, for personal use.  I haven't had any issues - I don't let it run down to empty, I don't keep it full all the time, and I haven't cleaned it out.  I usually keep the lid open because of concerns about rust from other reviewers, but I haven't had any yet.  I will note that it's going to be tough if you want to wash it out, but with water, and water that's boiled every day, I don't think there is a huge risk to not cleaning it.  The outside of the container gets very hot, so keep that in mind if you have kids who like to touch stuff, but I haven't accidentally hurt myself in any way.  It's easy to pour, pretty easy to fill, easy to use, and I've been very happy.  I haven't tested the accuracy of the temperature setting, but it seems fine for me.  The worst thing that has happened was a stink bug found its way inside, not sure how long he was in there before I found him.

text: Fire Hazard! The blue Indicator light blinks nonstop
Body: This by far is the worst Cuisinart Electric kettle !The massive blue light indicator & those numerous lights all over the buttons are nonstop blinking!They would come on automatically anytime even when not in use hence make sure to plug it out the wall otherwise this will cause a fire 🔥! Dangerous product!

I purchased it on Jan 27, 2022. As of today Jan 20, 2023, I have been using it almost 1 year. Two days ago, in the morning I noticed that there was water dropping from the button. I added water in the kettle and I did not see water leaking immediately. I left the kettle on the countertop for 2-3 hours, then when I pick up the kettle again, the water was dropping continuously. Very disappointed, $100 dollars kettle only good for 1 year usage.
Dent and the plastic was made much smaller then the space, also is not turning on
Just want to warn everyone thinking of buying this product. After only a few uses the numbers and letters started to fade away.

text: Rusts on the inside after a month
Body: Not easy to clean and there’s a metal bolt near the top that made the insides rust out after less than 2 months
What wrong with the plastic scroll, the interior of cuisiart kettle. It arrived onJanuary 13, 2017 at 1:45pm and I opened it at 1:55pm. I Disappointed with that product. I need to return it back.
After 3 uses the "Open Lid" button became stuck and would not open so I am unable to use this product. Was excited for it and the construction but let down but this defect.

I have used this pot quite often since I bought it in Sept 2023. Today I looked inside, not sure why I did, but the inside was disgusting. I am not sure how mold like this formed when I only put water in it and it boils all the time, but there it is. I will be tossing this thing and never buying a non-clear kettle again.

Purchased back in Nov 2018, when it was only $60. About two months ago, the kettle started to leak. Well, at first I didn't know it was a leak, I just saw water pooled around the base (see photo), and I spent quite a while blaming everyone else in the house for not being careful when filling the kettle and spilling water all over the electrical base, which you can imagine is pretty dangerous.......all suspicions toward my family members were assuaged one day when I filled the kettle with all care, set it down to heat, and when I picked it up - water on the base! When I went to pour water from the kettle, that was when I realized it was dripping from the bottom of the kettle.After some intense detective work, I deduced, my dear Watson, that the Kettle would leak only when filled above the 1L level (max is 1.7L so this is nowhere near max). This is fine since we rarely use more than 1L at a time anyways.... that is, until we started having company over and needing to serve hot water to several guests at once.Lo and behold, when I went to look for a replacement, I was hit by sticker shock. $99, are you kidding me?? Then I looked up the warranty. 3 years! Wait a minute, I realized I literally had two days left before I was over the 3 year warranty.I've since contacted customer service at Cuisinart. The warranty claim process was actually not too bad - until we got to the part where we needed to cut the cord on the base and send in a photo before they'll send us a new unit. Well, around the holidays during winter season is a terrible time to be without a kettle, so that's kind of a pain. I understand the policy, but it's still a pain.Will update when I've received the new kettle. In the meantime, if you have one of these and it's been almost 3 years since you bought it..... check for leaks. And have your receipt ready.

text: Product has reliable heat control but the inside base material got corroded in less than 6 months.
Body: I like the temperature control and the safety aspects. However, the base material inside is badly corroded within 6 months of purchase. I have added pictures that show the corrosion.

The quality of this kettle is different from the original kettle we use to own. You can tell the steel is not smooth at all on top as well as a dark black stain on the rim on the inner kettle that looks like it wasn't polished properly. You can feel all the steel ridges on top. They must be using a different supplier or maybe met some supply chain issues because this kettle was sold out at one point and then jumped to $150 then went down to $99.

text: Temperature sensor to turn off kettle malfunctioning after 1 year use!
Body: This is our 2nd Cuisinart electric kettle, the first one lasted a good number of years, therefore we purchased the 2nd one based on that experience, afterall it is still the recommended kettle on Wirecutter, fortunately it is still under warranty so we shall see how the 3rd one work out!

I actually love this electronic tea kettle!! I does everything I need it to do perfectly! However! Although even though I have only had this for a few months, the printing is already starting to wear off! For instance, the START button faded first. I thought I could fill it in with a sharpie. Bad idea!! I made it ten times worse so I removed the whole thing with a dry eraser which looks so much better. Now the OPEN button is starting to fade. I am just leaving it alone. Also since the 175 degree button is the one I use most often, the degree sign is starting to fade. I have read quite a few reviews from the past where this flaw is noted continuously so I thought for sure they would have found a resolution for this!! Wrong! I am not sure why they can’t just coat those buttons with plastic or something AFTER they print the labels??In any case, except for the labels flaw, this is an incredible product which I highly recommend to anyone. I would have given it a FIVE except for this!!

So far I really like the different temperature features for this kettle. Having the kettle maintain the heat for a period of time has definitely been beneficial for my second cuppa. The blue light adds some cool ambience. I’m coming from a plastic kettle and the biggest learning curve for me here is that the outside of this metal kettle gets just as hot as a kettle coming straight off the stove and because it insulated better and automatically keeps heating up it stays hot for a lot longer. I accidentally burned my arm while prepping something on the counter and the mark is still there two weeks later.  My boyfriend did the same thing to his hand  a couple of days later while making his coffee.  I had to move it to the other side of the kitchen because it was in a high traffic part of the counter. Make sure you put it someplace where you and other family members are not actively working. Or make a tea coozie maybe…

This has heated water 2-3 times a day in a business (multiple users) for four years, best kettle ever!  It would still be with us except someone hit the metal rack with the spout and the spout fell off.  The spout is spot welded in two places, then glued.  So be a little careful with it!  Really anything from Cuisineart is going to be a good product!

I purchased my first Cuisinart tea kettle in 2018. That one still worked, but it leaked somewhat. I couldn't have that. But all and all it was a fantastic tea kettle. I just purchased this one. Looking forward to making my coffee tomorrow. French press.

Finally had to replace the kettle after 10 years of daily use and pulling the plug multiple times a day.  I even took it with me on vacations. You guessed it the cord is failing. The pot itself is great and temp controls still work. I use it for all types of tea and to boil water. I never had a problem until now. I was pleased to see that the price actually dropped but the product and quality are almost exactly the same.  Your mileage may vary but I would definitely recommend you give this one a try especially if you are looking for a variable temp kettle.

text: Spend a little more, it's worth it
Body: I appreciate the temperature guidelines and quick heating. Not all Cuisinart products are this good but this boiler is worth the extra money compared to other brands.
Me encanto, material, diseño, operación sencilla

My complaint with this stainless steel kettle is the use of plastic inside the kettle. The inside of the top lid is plastic. The inside of the spout is plastic (your hot water passes through this plastic). The removable mesh screen inside the spout is housed in plastic. I was looking forward to a kettle with temperature control made of stainless steel to lessen my family’s exposure to plastics. If you share the same goal, this kettle is not the answer you’ve been seeking. I wish Cuisinart would have included the information about plastic parts in their specifications.

Lights turn on, but nobody's home. Heating element not functioning. Trying to upload my receipt to Cuisinart's customer service website, and all I get is a "technical error" message.An electric kettle should be just that - electric, with a simple on/off switch that's triggered by the water boiling. As soon as you start introducing unnecessary features, like multiple temperatures, keep warm, beeping alarms, etc., you're into the world of electronics, with all of the additional opportunities for failure. Once again, the simplified world becomes unnecessarily complicated, to the frustration of consumers. Do yourselves a favor. Stay away from nonsense like this. Get a basic kettle and use it for years.

text: It lasted exactly 2 years! waste of money!
Body: It lasted 2 years. Stop working today! for this kind of money I expected a better product!
It has a useless bright light that turns on automatically every time you put it on the base. Wasted electricity and more light pollution in your home.

text: Used 4 days and it shorted out
Body: Just don't. Cuisinart is not what it used to be. This kettle shorted out after less than 4 days of use. The lid wouldn't open correctly out of the box. The buttons are difficult to push as well. I was very disappointed overall for the price even before it shorted out. I do not recommend this product.

text: Worked till just outside of warranty period
Body: Not worth the money for 3 years. It had electrical issues that caused it to stop working. When I called Cuisinart all they offered was a 20% on a new one. I'm not buying a new one to have to replace it again in 3 years.

I am surprised and disappointed that this major brand manufactured a product that didn't even last for 3 months. The buttons light up. They beep. But the element no longer heats. At most I've used the device three times per week... with less than 1l of water each use.

$$$Expensive and didn't last. Heats quickly but can boil over.  Lid/open button stopped working.  I continued to use by filling with water through the pouring spout.  Now it's leaking from the bottom and it's a shock hazard.  Limited 3 year warranty.  Going in the trash.  I expected a quality product from Cuisinart.  Disappointed.

text: It’s not good as it used to be
Body: This electric tea kettle is a piece of junk. It stop working only after 13 months. The old one i had wotked for like 10 years. I’ll not buy this brand again.
It is easy to use and looks good. But the lid and the body were very hot when I make a hot water. We can touch an only handle.

First one failed at 2 years old - base station dead. Second one, replaced under warranty, failed after 2 years- lid mechanism, kettle can’t be opened. 3 year warranty from Cuisinart clearly not long enough, product quality at this premium price

I have mixed feelings about this electric kettle. On one hand it has fancy temperature controls but on the other hand electronics is a bit finicky and durability is not great.First issue is the design of a handle and location of "keep warm" button. Button is at the very bottom of the controls and handle is quite slick with no stop before controls. So, if you do not have a firm grip and lift the kettle, your hand will slide up and you will turn on "keep warm" feature which is very annoying. This always happens with my kids when they try to lift full kettle.Second issue it that often electronic freezes and none of the buttons are operational. You have to lift the kettle from its base to reset.Lastly, it does not seem to be all that durable. Granted I had it for 3.5 years now, but right now lid does not open and does not close properly. To open it you have to gently pry it open and to close you have to push it to a side and down.So, considering price, I am not too happy with this model. My previous kettle cost me third of this and lasted twice as long -- did not have multiple temperatures though.

text: Upgraded my review. Worked as discribed until temperature sensor? or something internal failed.
Body: I found and fixed the problem. The relay inside the base got stuck in the on position. Gave the relay a sharp rap the handle of the screwdriver, started working again. Has happened several times and each time the fix works. They need a more robust relay. The kettle is supposed to shut off automatically when it boils, and it usually does, but just after a year, it doesn't, and continues to boil, even though all the lights are off. I have to unplug it to turn it off or remove it from the base. Even then it starts boiling again when returned to the base despite all the lights being off.Ordered similar item on Amazon from different company and about half the price.

Worked great until it started to leak. Eventually the glue dissolves and the kettle will leak. Cannot be fixed. Don't buy if you want something that lasts a decade. It's great but has a limited lifespan due to glue sealants.

text: it failed after two months of use and has to go back to manufacturer.
Body: I really liked it when I first got it but it now won't work.  I have to wonder if all the bells and whistles and the memory make it more likely to fail.  Perhaps consumers would stick with a hot water kettle that is a lot simpler.

Worked amazingly well the first week or so. Now it is taking close to 8 minutes to boil from the same starting temperature. Fairly disappointing.The rest of the kettle is working great, so i am at least happy for that.

This unit functions great, however I am disappointed in the points of contact the boiling water will have with plastic.  There is no way to fully remove the spout filter, only the fine screen.  The lid is metal for show but seals to the inside with a plastic face. Even part of the temperature sensor appears to be plastic.

text: Not what it used to be
Body: Purchased one of these around 6 years ago and used the heck out of it. It saw daily use with multiple rounds of tea/coffee/cocoa etc. Solid machine that stopped working, possibly after I boiled water at a level below the recommended amount. There was no question we'd get another. The build quality on the new machine feels cheaper; the lid rattles and there's loud clicking noises when you change temp settings. Its heating the water so it gets 3 stars, but I feel like I should have tried something else.

1. temperature control settings are questionable. I make Americanos and the coffee setting is WAY too hot. So is 200 for that matter. I finally settle on 190 degrees so that I could actually drink my Americano without scalding my mouth.2. the pot is WAY WAY too heavy and I'm not a weakling. But I don't have right neck pain so I try to use my left arm to pour if 1/2 or more full. Can't imagine an elderly person or really anyone without much arm strength comfortable using this. I'm quite strong despite my neck pain. I just prefer not to aggravate it and this pot definitely does!3. pour spout is OBNOXIOUS. If pot is very full then it's very challenging to control the flow as it comes out forcefully. if pot is low filled then it's hard to get water to empty without tilting the bottom 180°.4. lid does not come completely off and opening is small so you won't get even a med size woman's hand inside to clean it.I REALLY wanted to love this kettle as it's my 3rd one. None of them with temp controls so far have been worth the excessive cost. I thoughtly surely Cuisinart will be a winner but nope, worst one yet.Now I'm just gonna buy the cheapo deluxe Chefman and cross my fingers since I've had good experiences with their crock pots. We shall see...

text: Didn't last as long as I'd hoped
Body: I just bought my second one of these kettles after the lid mechanism on the first one fell apart after about five years, which is a bit disappointing considering the price. I'm hoping it's a bit of a one off, but upon taking out the lid mechanism of the old one I saw so much plastic that I was not surprised a couple of those hinge parts eventually broke with the constant heating/cooling cycles.It still blows my mind that manufacturers will not use more metal parts instead of plastic in such critical areas. The hinge arms of the lid are metal, the hinge pin is metal, and the springs are metal, but those metal parts rotate on/in plastic and are held in place by plastic (the lid broke because one hinge pin holder fractured and one hinge pin retainer fell off). It would be so easy to make those key structural parts of the hinge mechanism metal as well and would probably cost pennies to do so. I've kept the old kettle and might try to re-engineer the lid mechanism myself because the rest of the old kettle still works fine.

text: It's a kettle that tries too hard
Body: It's an electric kettle. It boils water. It's almost exactly like the one I used to own years ago but must now replace. What's the difference between that and this? This model has a dozen useless buttons, each of which a mere pathway to planned obsolecence. My advice: move along. Nothing to see here.

I drink a lot of tea and coffee (mostly tea). And my fellow tea drinkers recommended this. After years of a boil only kettle, I sprung for an upgrade.This is the greatest kitchen gadget I've ever purchased in my life. Heats up wicked fast and has a special setting for every kind of tea and coffee (6 in all). Simple to use. Just buy this, you won't be sorry.

With the current cold snap, my lovely wife and I decided to start drinking tea in the afternoon and herbal tea in the evening. We have a natural gas cooktop, and heating up a pot of water means running the range hood to maintain our indoor air quality, exhausting all that nice warm air along with the gas fumes.To solve this problem, and after checking reviews, we ordered this Cuisinart 1.7-Liter Stainless Steel Cordless Electric Kettle.  It definitely does the job.  It heats quickly (faster than our stovetop kettle), holds a lot of water (I won't repeat the specs here), can keep the water hot, and has multiple temperature settings for different kinds of tea.  I hadn't previously noticed that tea bags specify the water temperature, and this makes it easy to follow directions. The only thing it's missing is a timer, but my watch works just fine for that.Really the only annoyance is that the window that shows the water level is underneath the handle.  While that's not a problem when heating or dispensing the hot water, it's mightily annoying when I'm filling the pot from our refrigerator's filtered water dispenser.  While I've become adept at aiming the stream into the mouth of the kettle, I can't see the water level as it fills because the window is under the handle that I'm holding.  However, I've gotten pretty good at estimating the fill level by weight.  Still, if the window could be moved out from under the handle, this thing would be golden.
The temperature control feature is excellent for anyone who makes black tea, green tea, and coffee. These last a long, long time.

text: As Expected — I purchased the Cuisinart kettle ($99.00) and it died in 8 months. See photo.
Body: The kettle was used for making morning coffee for two and afternoon coffee for 1.

text: Stuck lid FIXED. Details and pictures included.
Body: Stuck lid FIXED. Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp. If you hold down the "open" button and then close the lid, the lid will get stuck. To fix this, simply pop off the metal top from the plastic hatch. The metal is held down with four plastic hooks, and will pop off painlessly. From there you can manually open the latches on each side.

text: might be good, but never found out...
Body: Today I'm returning my second CPK-17.  I really wanted this kettle, but I'm not paying $90.00 for a kettle with a visible discolored mark smack on the front of the kettle.  Cuisinart placed an adhesive sticker (2.5"x4.5") on the front of the kettle to highlight some product features.  The sticker is supposed to be removed before you use the kettle.  When I removed the sticker (both times), it left a dark discolored mark where the sticker had been affixed to the kettle.I would love to try this kettle, but I don't want to look at a brand new product with a large discolored mark on the front.  Sorry Cuisinart, you are screwing this one up. The really silly thing is that the kettle comes wrapped in plastic, the instruction booklet is wrapped in plastic, the cord and base is wrapped in plastic.  Maybe some bright person at the manufacturing plant could think of placing this sticker (which is meant to be thrown away) ON THE PLASTIC and not on the kettle where it ruins the beautiful stainless steel.I've called Cuisinart twice and they don't really seem to care.  I've told the customer service rep to pass on the message not to place stickers right on the product.  I'm not hopeful things will change.The kettle might be good, but I didn't even try it.  It's going back and this time I'm asking for a refund, not a replacement.

text: Premium look (and cost) electric kettle with poor usability
Body: Probably like many others out there, I've used a $10 electric kettle for years, it gets the job done. I decided to upgrade to this electric kettle hoping that the extra features and quality would be worth it, but my experience with this kettle was very poor for a few major reasons.1) The pouring spout is HORRIBLE. The spout itself is way too wide, and for some reason just never pours in a steady stream. I think this is due to the design of the mesh filter and all that plastic that gets in the way of a smooth pour. It's like nobody ever tried pouring with this kettle before.2) The "Keep Warm" feature is a scam. You can set it to keep warm at different temperature points, so I assumed that the kettle would keep the water at that temperature, for example 190 degrees. But that's not what happens at all. Instead of constantly applying heat to keep the water at a certain temperature, what the kettle does is turn off completely, then turn back on when the water temperature drops below a certain point, and heats it back up to your designated temperature. That's not keeping the water at the selected temperature at all!3) It actually boils water more slowly than my $10 kettle. I boiled 1L of water in both, and this Cuisinart one was just slightly slower, but slower regardless. Come on!4) Minor complaint, but the beeping sounds when the water is ready are pretty annoying, I wish I could disable that or at least make it just one beep instead of 3 or 5 (I don't know why it does 3 sometimes and 5 others).Overall, I expected a flawless and well-designed electric kettle for $100, but what I got was one that I wouldn't even use over my $10 one I got right after college. Would not recommend.

*** UPDATE ***My original review of the Cuisinart CPK-17 purchased in 2011 can be found below this updated review:Recently the CPK-17 purchased in 2011 stopped working when I accidentally splash water on the handle control . We've loved the product and immediately bought a new one. The current product on the market is rather inferior to the one I reviewed originally. * Boiling water is 30% slower. The 2011 CPK-17 brought 1L of water to 212°F in 4m 30s, the current one does it in 5m 50s under similar ambient temperatures and starting water temperatures. * The newer model has black lettering in the water window instead of white, which is more difficult to read. * The water window itself is more difficult to use. It often has condensation inside the window that makes it difficult to gauge the water level.If you've never used the earlier model, there is still plenty to like in the CPK-17, but if you have you are likely to be somewhat disappointed.*** ORIGINAL REVIEW ***My fiance were originally considering buying a Japanese style water boiler like this one, but changed our minds when we couldn't find one that had a metal interior -- most are plastic -- nor one that could be set to go directly to the desired temperature without boiling first. I'm glad we decided on the CPK-17, because it is a great kettle and perfect for our needs. We drink a lot of tea, so it's nice to be able to set the temperature for delicate tea, green tea, white tea, oolong tea, french press coffee, or black tea.As I mentioned before, the kettle will not boil the water first and wait for it to cool down to the correct temperature like all of the Japanese dispensers I've seen. This is important to me, because it can take quite a while for 1.7L of water too cool from boiling -- 212°F -- to the correct temperature for green tea -- 175°F. In addition, there are no plastic parts that touch the water, so there isn't any off-taste you can sometimes get with kettles with plastic interiors.I use this kettle all day long, almost every day, and have had no issues with it. It's well-built and looks great in our kitchen.For those interested in heating times, here are some quick measurements I took to heat water coming from the refrigerator dispenser which is approximately 50°F at sea level in a 75°F environment:0.75L to 175°F : 3m 5s1.00L to 212°F : 4m 30s1.70L to 212°F : 7m 55s

Et tu, Wirecutter?This is not a good kettle. It is impossible to empty completely, it refuses to turn off reliably and the fill gauge glugs rather than smoothly showing the water level.The outside also gets very hot, as it is uninsulated.I'm not sure how this was Wirecutter's top pick. Yes, you can pick exactly how hot you want the water, but once it's boiled and beeped and you pour the water, it often (not always) refuses to turn off. Twice in the day and a half I used the thing I had to unplug it to keep it from heating back up once empty. The user's manual doesn't even mention that you have to turn it off - had to find here that it's a double-tap to turn it off (and, as I said, doesn't always work).We're back to using our decade-old Hamilton Beach kettle until we find a better model. It's unreliable, but at least it's not trying to burn me.

text: Works fine...unless it doesn't this time and you come back to cold water in 5 minutes.
Body: This is a pretty nice kettle in that it has 6 pre-set temperatures that pretty consistently get water to the same temperature.It feels pretty nice, but overall quality is kind of dubious--the steel top pops off its plastic lid pretty easily, the lettering for all the buttons wore off in less than a year, and, well, it frequently just doesn't heat the water.What happens is you press the "Start" button and the kettle will just sit for half a minute and then emit 3 beeps and turn off.It does this just frequently enough that I don't ever trust it to actually start, and usually stand over it to make sure it is actually going to work this time, which kind of ruins part of the point of being able to select a temperature and come back to hot water.It has done this since new.I also wish the temperatures were just a little different, but, with so many other things wrong with it, I won't press my luck.I will probably keep it until it breaks (probably soon, as has been my experience with other Cuisinart products), and hope something better is on the market by then.

text: Good for precisely heating water, average-to-bad for pretty much everything else.
Body: I hesitate to call this kettle "bad," but it's definitely overpriced. As someone who consumes copious amounts of tea on a daily basis but has only ever used really cheap $20 electric kettles, I figured I'd treat myself to something more professional when I made my purchase. While the Cuisinart has a variety of options for different tea types and heats its water very quickly, it also has a lot of shortcomings that have long been resolved by other, cheaper brands.The most obvious design issue is the spout: it is wide, awkward, pours very unevenly. This often results in a lot of wasted water, either left in the bottom of the kettle or spilled on your countertop when you try to completely invert the kettle just to shake the last remaining bits out. And while I appreciate that the kettle with automatically reheat any water left in the pot when it's placed back on the hot plate, it will start the reheating process even if there is nothing left in the vessel, making it somewhat hazardous for first-time users.Overall, I'd say save your money and purchase something much cheaper. Like I said, I've been using cheap $20 kettles my entire life, and I honestly can't tell the difference between the water boiled in those, and the water boiled in this fancy schmancy one.

This kettle is incredibly frustrating. It is always boiling at the wrong temperature or boiling when you don't expect it to be.After removing the kettle from the base and using the boiled water, the kettle does not automatically disable the keep warm function. So, it'll be boiling again without much water in it once you've got your drink and gone to sit down. What's the point of that? And it'll keep doing that until all of the water has boiled away. In addition, somehow, it keeps forgetting that it's job is to make hot water, and the temperature resets to 160 degrees from 200 every so often.
