Yes, we leave it plugged in and on the base.Noise - seems quiet, but often it's only boiling to 160, so that's cheating.Overall, the behavior of the Keep Warm and variable temperature is a frustration, because every interaction with the kettle requires active attention to stop it doing the wrong thing. Other kettles like the Kenwood SJM610 just do the expected action by default.We brought this as a replacement for the Kenwood SJM610 after the Kenwood developed a leak. Overall the Kenwood was a far better kettle, until it began leaking.

I didn't expect much out of this kettle, but it fell a bit short on one critical point.  The only thing that I was looking for was that it was primarily stainless steel on the inside (minimal amounts of plastic or rubber).  On that note, this kettle did fine.  There is a small rubber piece (presumably where the temperature control feedback thermocouple is), and then the plastic on the back that displays the volume of water.  There is also a bit of plastic near the spout, but that doesn't touch the water until you pour.  The temperature control is nice, and it holds ample water.Here is my disappointment: If you only heat up one person's worth of water (~8oz), you cannot pour the water cleanly.  The first time I poured water out, probably 1/3 of the water missed my cup.  Note that this is not a lack of hand-eye coordination, but a poor design.  The small piece of plastic near the spout somehow prevents water from exiting cleanly.  It ends up coming out of the edges of the spout.  This does not seem to be a problem when you fill the kettle full - only when you fill up a small amount (1 serving) of water.  In order to avoid spilling now, I have to pour tremendously slow (10 seconds per 8 oz cup).Will I return it -- probably not.  I usually feel bad about returning used equipment that still functions.  That said, if I had to purchase again, I would buy a different product.  The temperature control is nice, but not worth the difficulty in pouring.

text: Designed for my entire tea collection, does the job nicely!
Body: This kettle is attractive, with its stainless steel carafe, updated shape, and pretty blue display - it should be, for its price. It's extremely easy to use, as the temperature, start and hold buttons all do exactly what you'd think they would do. And the fact that the kettle itself is cordless (the cord connects to the heating base) optimizes freedom and comfort of use.I have an extensive collection of teas of all types, so the various temperature settings take the guesswork out of heating water in a stovetop kettle. (I regularly use every one of the temperature settings!) Although my ear was becoming fairly well tuned to the sounds of my stovetop kettle, nothing takes the place of absolute certainty!Besides the various temperature settings, I am happy to finally have a kettle with a volume window. Before, if I wanted to use my larger teapot to make a partial (not full) pot of tea, I had to use a measuring cup to ensure the proper amount of water for the quantity of tea leaves I was using - a big pain. Although this is a common feature of electric kettles, I'm happy to have this feature combined with the various temperature settings this kettle offers.I'm not crazy about the way the Cuisinart pours, however. The somewhat irregular flow is probably due to the presence of the removable filter at the inside entry to the spout, but this is no excuse. It could have been better designed. It's especially annoying when I am pouring the last of the water out and, in order to get the last ounce or so to pour, I have to return the kettle to upright and then pour the last bit out.The half hour hold feature is nice, but I'm finding I need a bit more time. An hour would have been better. As it is, I find that many times I need to manually turn the kettle back on, once its passed its half hour hold time, in order to finish up the remainder of the contents.All in all, this product was thoughtfully designed and appears to be the only kettle on the market that truly satisfies the needs of the consummate drinker of a wide variety of teas.

Good: Great kettle and has worked well for me after 3 years of daily use.Bad: 1. The button writing wearing off. I did the nail polish trick, which was a pain because I couldn't use it for the first 2 days I had it because I was being very cautious and making sure the polish had enough time to completely dry. It did the trick for a couple of years, but now there has been some rubbing off. Looks bad. I don't know why they can't just fix this.Bad: 2. I hate how it beeps very loudly 5 times when ready. 3 beeps would be plenty, and 1 beep would be just fine for me. 5 extremely loud beeps is very aggravating. I guess Cuisinart wants people to know when their water is ready even if they're out mowing the lawn with headphones on. I'm sure some people even wish theirs would do no beeps, for whatever reason. It should be a user-configurable setting. That would be fantastic.Bad: 3. Some rust near the lid. They really should use better quality parts to prevent this. And it can cause the lid to pop up very slowly. That happened with mine, but it was temporary and not a dealbreaker issue.Overall still a great product but I wish the company would up the quality to solve the nagging quality issues. I'd be willing to pay more.

Well, I got into tea, apparently, in March 2012, when I bought this kettle. It has worked extremely well for the past 7 years. The two bothersome qualities of this kettle are the following:1) The letters will definitely wear off the kettle. Mine did so on the temperature I use the most (Black tea) within about one year or so. This isn't too bad, but if I was constantly making different temps of tea, it would be very problematic.2) The water level gauge forms a white/black crust as though it's not perfectly sealed, and there's no way to get in there and clean it. I believe it's just water calcification but it's still somewhat disgusting and bad design. I tried filling the whole kettle with vinegar and letting it sit, but that didn't do anything but remove the scale.I see on here that a lot of people got defective units. I may have been lucky. I feel like I got my money's worth as it's been 7 years and it's still working. I may replace it due to the water calcification, though.

I've used the Cuisinart CPK-17 for almost a year (bought on 02 August 2014), and I'm really pleased with it.When I was on the market for a kettle, I read the extensive review by The Sweethome (link: http://thesweethome.com/reviews/the-best-home-kettle/ ). I tend to trust these guys given their extensive and thoughtful tests, and so I bought their pick although it's not cheap.I'm a great tea lover, and I drink different kind of teas (mostly greens, but also black, oolong, white, herbal infusions) 2+ time a day.In the morning both me and my husband have tea at breakfast, but since we drink different teas which requires different temperatures, we heat the water separately. In the fall/winter I am sure to have a huge pot of tea in the afternoon, and usually we also have herbal teas in the evening.So in a year we used the kettle pretty extensively, and it still works great!These are the main reason why I like it:1) it heats up to 1.7 liter of water, so if I want to fill a big teapot or I have guest I can heat enough water for everyone2) you can choose among 6 different temperatures for different kind of teas (which makes a huge difference!), and the labels are pretty accurate (I've measured the water both in mug and in a teapot a couple of times, out of curiosity, and there were +/- 2 F degrees difference tops)3) it's quick and noiseless - yes, you'll hear the water boiling, but that's it, it won't make any additional noise4) given its large capacity, it doesn't take a lot of space on the countertop, plus it has a nice design and I don't mind have it around5) it's easy to fill (I love the button to open the lid automatically), and to check how much water you poured in6) the 30 minute keep warm option (although I don't use it that much)As everything, it has a couple of downside:1) it's heavy! especially if filled to its top capacity2) the sides get hot, so pay attention not to touch themBPA controversy: this kettle has minor plastic components, and I was concerned. However on the product description on cuisinart website (link: https://www.cuisinart.com/products/tea_kettles/cpk-17.html ) they explicitly say it is BPA-free.To wrap up, in almost a year of constant use I am really please with my Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp. It is on the expensive side for being a kettle, but it deserves that money.

text: After 5 years of daily use it's my hardest working appliance and has yet to let me down.
Body: I have had this since Feb. 2011 and it's going strong. My mom has one also and turned it on & it boiled dry- it then went into "error" mode and wouldn't work.  My mom called the company and they were really great and sent a new one out (it was within the warranty period).  That was 4 year ago and hers works like a champ.I use it almost daily (HUGE tea drinker) and even use it to boil water for cooking pots.  I have pretty hard water so I clean it about every 8 weeks to get scale out.I have NOT had the issue of the numbers rubbing off...not sure if people are possibly using super strong industrial cleaners on it?  Or I got lucky.It makes a little "beeping" sound when the water is done- it's there but not intrusive, I don't want any obnoxious BEEP letting my know my water for my relaxing cup of tea is done :~) and with the "keep warm" feature it's not needed- it will be there hot & ready for you when you're ready.  You can hear the water change composition as it begins to boil, so I've come to know when it's almost done just by that!The lid pops open very easily and I put it down in the sink, fill it, lift it, wipe the bottom, put on the stand (makes a tiny "click-ish" sound) and hit boil!I brew different teas, some of which are delicate and also use a french press (Bodum- REALLY recommend that also!!!) so this gets a LOT of use from me!It does get hot on the outside (not the handle) but it's not scalding.  It will make you pull away, but it's a metal tea kettle...it's going to get hot.  But you won't be going to the ER.After 5 years of daily use it's my hardest working appliance and has yet to let me down.I know people have concerns about BPA in the plastic- it's such a small amount that I really think it's nothing to worry about.  I am conscious about BPA (use Kleen Kanteens, filter my water), nonstick pans, carpet/furniture "protectors" etc also, and I don't think twice about this kettle.  Of the amount of plastic we are exposed to daily, the styrofoam, nonstick pans, chemicals in our meat, I think this kettle is low on the totem pole for worries to me.

text: First one I bought lasted 19 years
Body: I finally had to buy a new one and really glad it's still on the market.  It gave no problems at all survived 5 moves and worked like a charm.  It only started to act up in the past year when I carelessly filled it over the water mark, from then it was turning on but not heating.  However this was after using it for 19 years...  there is a trick to hold down the keep warm button, on button and a temp button to try to reset it which worked for a time however it finally kicked it.  I recommend this highly because 19 years using this it was amazing it held on so long.  Really cool blue light shows you how  high the water is...be careful not to go over.  You won't be disappointed it's a die hard !!!!

text: The kettle we received was used. Please check it before using it.
Body: Ensure that your kettle box is sealed and the kettle has not been used before. Our ‘new’ kettle had many watermarks and scratches all over. You can even see calcium residue at the bottom of the kettle. Disappointing.

Terrible, terrible, and again terrible customer service!!! First of all it is not working after 2 months of using. Contacted customer service regarding the issue with it, they asked to email them cut cord along with the kettle, so they can send us a replacement. Well its been almost a month, still no update on the shipment. It is not worth for its money. When you buy A kettle for a $100 you at least expect a good customer service, but this is not a case. Better buy something for $25 and don’t waste your money here!!!!

text: Don't purchase! It RUSTS inside! Cuisinart does NOT cover rust in their 3 yr warranty. BUYER BEWARE!
Body: I purchased this kettle Jan 2022.  I read some of the reviews that said it can rust.  I was diligent about heating my water and emptying the kettle completely after every heating thinking this would allay that problem.  Not so!  It's now April 2023 and I have rust developing on the inside bottom.  See picture.When I called Cuisinart customer service they informed me they "do not cover rust in the 3 yr warranty" that comes with the kettle.  So even if I had purchased an extended warranty the first 3 yrs Cuisinart would "cover" the product.  They told me all their kettles have the same metal on the bottom.So the product definitely rusts and they do not cover rust.  Buyer beware!  Waste of $100.

text: DO NOT BUY- BROWN RESIDUE WITHIN DAYS
Body: I have had this less than a week and was really excited for using this kettle for quickly making coffee in the morning. Since I don’t have a gas stove currently, this is much faster than my electric stove. After my experience with this kettle, I saw some negative reviews mentioning this and had hoped it was a fluke. IT IS NOT. I have this disgusting brown residue in the bottom of the kettle after mere DAYS of use. This is disgusting and unacceptable. I would NOT recommend this electric kettle to anyone.
this is the item i received as a "NEW" kettle. it was clearly used. The picture speaks for itself ..

text: Very Disappointed - has brown spots after boiling one pot of water
Body: I purchased this item as a gift.  I have one that I got a few years back and totally like the Cuisinart Kettle.  My gift recipient contacted me after using the kettle twice and asked if it was normal to have brown spots on the bottom.  I looked inside my tea kettle that has been in use daily for several years and there are no brown spots.  I replied I don't think that is normal, let's return it and try another one.  The second kettle was received and the photo that I've included with this review is after heating the first pot of water.  This is so disappointing.  I have to believe that the product is made with a inferior grade stainless steel.  This should not happen after boiling one pot of water.  So, the second kettle is returned and I just asked for a refund and will look for another brand.  So disappointed - especially since I really raved about my kettle and how happy I've been with it's performance.  I hope Cusinart gets their act together.  I don't think anyone should be ingesting water from this item.

FIRE 🔥 HAZARDAUTOMATIC SHUT OFF DOESNT WORKAfter 1 month it stop working, than started to work again for a couple of days and than stopped.....  you got it?YOU CAN’T return it (Although it says that you can return it).

Unfortunately, my review is limited as my kettle arrived damaged and I will be returning. The spout appears cheap and attached with glue to the main body. Hopefully the electronic components outlast the flimsy exterior. I'll update my review once my replacement is received and tested.

text: Just all of the sudden the spout came apart. ...
Body: Just all of the sudden the spout came apart....  that's a lot of money paid for something that can break within the month

The GOOD: Had the unit for almost 3 years, loved it generally.The BAD: The print on the buttons will wear off, so you better manually remember which button is for which function.The UGLY: Today, the keypad stopped working entirely. The unit is dead and Cuisinart customer service is closed today, a Sunday. If they replace or fix the unit, I will update this review. If I don’t update it, assume poor product quality and customer service and go buy yourself a different product.It earns 2 stars from me, since it did work for almost three years.

This kettle has two major fails - both related to cleaning.Firstly - the top opening is too small to fit my medium sized man hand into. This makes washing the thing into much more of a chore than it needs to be.Secondly - there's some things sticking into the chamber. One on the back wall, the other up from the bottom. The attached photo shows them. These too make cleaning the kettle more difficult than it needs to be.I'm being super picky because I bought this kettle to replace my heavily worn Krupps kettle. That kettle is (almost) perfect. Big opening and nothing to snag a sponge.Other than these two fails, this is a good kettle that heats quickly, maintains temperature etc. It's just so annoying to clean it.
Keeps heating water even when shut off (see video) while warranty is 3 years, it requires sending unit with $15 for return shipping, negating any benefit of warranty. Worked well for a year though.

UPDATE: The kettle still works well but I am very disappointed it is rusting at the spout. Yes, I use it daily but stainless should NOT do this. I've only had this since July, 2024!I am a big hot tea drinker. Love that this keeps the water hot for a bit after pouring my first cup. It also keeps my tea hotter than when I was microwaving.

text: It develops rust on the inside bottom. Unsafe.
Body: I absolutely love this electric kettle. I purchased in March 2023. Unfortunately, after only 8 months of use, rust spots showed up on the inside bottom. I don't need rust in my water/tea/coffee! I've now read many users' reviews complaining of rust in various spots inside the kettle. Of course, it's made in CHINA. So go figure. This was the most expensive kettle I could find. I hate things made in China.

Heavy, heavy, heavy even when empty!  All those buttons on the way when you picking  up the hot kettle, or cold. Confusing, too many blinking lights. You can not see the water level when filling up.  Plastic filter, plastic lid , some other plastic parts on inside.  Horrible DESIGN!!!17K customers purchased it? I am returning, sorry!
I loved the tea kettle at first, until it started leaking from the bottom.

I love this electric kettle, I use it every day for boiling water. Great temperature settings for different types of tea. I’ve had lots of these kettles over the years.Russell Hobbs, Chief Man, & Capressio. This is by far the best one.

I use this for heating water for French press coffee.  It's perfect to know know that you can hit a specific temperature in a few minutes and hold it there until you’re ready.  I throw 700ml in it and hit the button, and it heats to 200 degrees in three to four minutes while I grind the beans and warm up the French press with hot water from the sink.  Everything comes together in a few minutes with no mess and no fuss.  Can’t ask for much more than that…except maybe for the European version that’s twice as powerful due to a different electric grid, and twice as fast, but c’est la vie.
Me encanto, calienta muy rapido el agua y no me preocupo por derrames, lo recomiendo mucho.

text: Looks amazing after almost 3 years of use.
Body: I loved this kettle on sight (online) but was put off by the reviews that said the black wording on the handle rubbed off very quickly. Ours is still as good as the day we bought it so no worries there. I would encourage anyone to buy this kettle. It does the job for me and although I’m a dyed in the wool black tea drinking Brit I have experimented with the green, red and white tea temp choices. It has had a huge amount of use in our family as we drink such a lot of tea!

I purchased this cattle in March of 2012, it now began slightly leaking at the bottom of the plastic water level window, I’m still able to use it but began looking for eventual replacement. After quite a bit of research I’m back to this one as my #1 choice for looks, utility and overall performance. Although pricey comparing to other models, considering it lasted over 8 years, it is a good investment. I hope the model improved since 2012 and the start and open markings are more lasting, it nicely matches my espresso machine, so I will be buying it again.

text: This tea kettle base has a cord, the tea kettle does not. Tell us like it is.
Body: I just made a brouhaha over the base having a cord. None of the images and the description mention a cord. I’m fine with a cord. It’s just it said it was cordless. So I just insisted on an exchange and then realize that the model number I received is equivalent to what I ordered. I was just befuddled by there being a cord. Bad bad Marketing. Not helpful explanations . Should be called cordless tea kettle with corded power base or some such .

The exterior of this kettle gets burning hot. Literally! Why? Who wants to carry around a big pitcher whose surface is basically the same temperature as the boiling water it holds? The only part that's not burning hot is the handle, so if you need a better grip or to balance it, I hope you have some burn cream. We have ways of containing heat. I guess they just didn't want to. Returned. Got a cool to the touch kettle. Cost half the price.

It is my second time purchasing Cuisinart. The first time I thought I got a bad tea kettle. But second time, the tea kettle broke down the same way the first one did. They are great when they work. Sadly, they don't work long. I will not be buying another Cuisinart branded item again.

Beautiful, lots of fancy features but not worth all the bells and whistles if it won't even reach temperature. I drink black tea...there is nothing better than a nice hot cuppa! To my disappointment, all presets are about 10F lower - the boiling 212F settling comes in at a disappointing 199F-201F.YES!  I double checked with 3 different thermometers - my instant read digital, infared and candy thermometer AND double checked reading by boiling water the old fashioned way on the stove.Sadly, I think this one will be going back. Hopefullu, my 14yr old, leaky, Breville will hold-up while I continue the hunt for a replacement.

There are multiple pieces inside the kettle that are plastic and cannot be removed. Your water will boil plastic in this kettle. Extremely poor design that cheaper kettles have managed to solve. Piece of junk, really.

text: Trash. Did not even last 1 year!!!
Body: I bought this in March 2024. It is now January 2025. So it worked for about 10 months. It is now on its way to the great landfill. Piece of garbage!!! Im going to buy an old school tea kettle.
The base was missing from the box🙁.  Return window was closed when I finally opened the box for use.

I purchased this item due to Cuisinart's reputation for quality.  The item arrived, worked one time, and then died electrically.  I assumed this was a one-off and so asked Amazon to replace with the same item.  The second one arrived and seemed to operate but then after the first boil, it leaked out all the water from the base all over the counter and floor!  I will never purchase another item from Cuisinart!
The tea kettle leaks out the bottom.
Not reliable.  Stopped heating water.  On the phone to Amazon to see if they will accept a return a few days past their return "window"
I dislike it intensely. It doesn’t turn off automatically. It’s useless. I’m about to throw it in the trash, but even the trash people don’t want it.  Worst purchase I’ve ever made.
I bought one of these three years ago - and it has already started rusting around the spout.  My other kettle (a Russell Hobbs from the UK) that I purchased in 1991 still looks flawless.
The kettle works great until it started leaking.Water came out the bottom and caused a mess after less then handful of uses. Hoping it’s just bad luck so ordering another one

I had a simple glass kettle for years, until I dropped it a few weeks ago. I thought I would "upgrade" to this highly-rated version, but I wish I had stuck with my original.  Here's why:1.  This things beeps so so much.  Beeps when you turn it on, beeps when it reaches temperature.2.  It's hard to see the water level through the little window by the handle.  I'm always boiling more water than I need.3.  Most frustrating is the actual use.  So many buttons, and it's been annoying to figure out which to press and when (and I promise I'm not an idiot - PHD and all).  But for some reason, Cuisinart decided to make boiling water a multi-button-press process.  And when you return the kettle to the stand after pouring your hot water, it sometimes, but not always, reverts to heating the water again!  I'm sure there's a way around that, but I'm sure also that I have more than enough to do without trying to mind-meld with the designers to figure out their intended use process.If I weren't so cheap, I would just toss this thing and get my original simple, "click here to boil water" version.  But if you think you're getting more by paying more, that's just not true in this case.

text: This is not what Wirecutter said it would be!
Body: It is not easy to actually get the kettle to start to heat up. You press start and then select your heating option and then sometimes you have to hit start again. Then after it boils, it doesn’t, shut off automatically but you have to hit start and then hit start for it to turn off. It takes a long time to actually boil the water compared to my old school glass electric kettle. I am sorry I did not act soon enough to return it. I was away for most of January. Hamilton Beach has a much better kettle, I bought one for my daughter. Regrets!

This was a great kettle for about 6 years of light use. Within the last year it had started leaking at the base. It started with just a little water when you’d pick it up and you’d wonder if some had simply spilled out, but now it leaks so much that I’m afraid it’s an electrocution hazard and has to be chucked. A Cuisinart product going for $100 should last much longer than 6 years. Bummer.

We purchased this based on reviews here and in various product review sites.  For example, it’s NYTimes Wirecutter’s top recommended.  The features are nice and it has a sturdy build.  But we purchased in March 2023 and for no discernible reason it stopped working at the end of November 2023.

The plastic hinge on the cover is  cheaply designed considering the cost of the product.  Pot still heats water but for the longest time now we have to manually open the lid because the plastic hinge broke a long time ago.

Great product—at first! A year and a half later the on/off switch and temperature control light work intermittently. Very concerned when the unit went on after turning it off even though the light went out. Had to remove the unit from the heating pedestal over night. Still works intermittently.

text: Worked great for the first 30 days
Body: Bought this from Amazon and used it maybe ten times in the month I had it.  Worked great until it didn't.  Tried to use it this morning (just boiling water) and it would light up but never got hot. Tried unplugging, plugging and using  different settings. Nada. Sent it back but super mad I had to pay $15 for UPS box and packing since I didn't have a box. I trust Cuisnart but this experience  has made me want to buy a different brand or return to just using a stove top kettle.

text: Stopped working after one year of daily use
Body: UPDATE: my husband took the kettle apart and discovered that the most frequently used buttons stopped working due to a failure of the micro-switches. This is after one year of daily use.~~~~~I bought this in Aug. 2021, and it stopped working in Oct. 2022.I paid much more for this electric kettle than any other I've ever owned, and I thought it would be worth it to have the many different temperature selections. Well, the variety of temperatures was a nice feature, but used less often than I had imagined we would -- we tended to just choose "boil." The fact that such a pricey kettle died after a year is extra disappointing.I appreciated the safety shut-off, the re-heating feature, and the noticeable but not obnoxious beep when the water reached a boil.Others have complained about the lettering wearing off on the kettle buttons. I did not have this problem. My husband used a coat of clear nail polish on the lettering when it was new, and perhaps that helped.

This is the most I've ever spent on a hot water kettle and it's my least favorite.  The on/off is not clear and often doesn't work.  I purposely turn it off, but it's still on.  I thought I would use the different temperature controls but I don't as it never seems hot enough using anything less than 'boil.'  I recommend getting something that is a bit simpler with a clear way of turning off and on.

I am a sucker for bells and whistles, yet they always turn out to be a mistake for me. I loved the way this looked, and thought the different temperatures would be good. I found I almost always used the boil setting, because 99% of the time I'm making tea. The water gauge vis ery hard to see, despite its being backlit. The worst part is that, after less than a year. I'm finding the controls are often not behaving. The lights illuminate when I start it, but despite lighting up, it isn't heating. Then I get it going, and it does not turn off when it is done. Or I press the start button, which is also the off button, oddly enough, and look back at it and it isn't off. I started to worry that this kettle is going to burn down my house. I've now pulled the plug (literally), and gone to a nice, simple Hamilton Beach for a quarter of the price. It heats a little faster, too! Don't waste your money on this Cuisinart version.

The way it was handled when delivered. If for some reason I detect any problems with the kettle I'm going to returned it.It is an electrical product, they leave it throw up at the entrance instead of leaving it carefully next to the door.

text: Bought twice, both ended up leaking.
Body: I'm an avid tea drinker, a kettle that has a rolling boil is important to me to get the tea just right. I bought this kettle with that in mind. The first one I had for a while but it started leaking from the bottom, I persevered with it for a while, but the constant water clean up got irritating, so I purchased another. This one has also started leaking everywhere so I'm looking for a new kettle. If they could just fix this fault, this kettle would be great, but I'm not willing to try for a third time!

text: Will Have to Replace it in Less Than 2 Years
Body: Second Cuisinart kettle bought.  The first one lasted just about 24 months.  Bought a second in Jul 2023.  This one lasted  18 months.  The kettle is used once, maybe twice a day.  Why spend $80 when you can buy another brand that does everything the Cuisinart does for half the price.
Inside is Hard to clean. There's plastics at spout, think it could be toxic? Functions are good.

text: Died after 30 months / Clunky to use
Body: Purchased this March 2022.  In September 2024, the sensor that detects when the pot is boiling started failing, and twice we caught it boiled dry and had to dump it. An expensive purchase for two and a half years of service!During its short life, my wife really appreciated the different temperature settings.  However, it had a few nagging issues even when working.  The 'keep warm' button is on by default, so the kettle repeatedly heats itself after you've poured your drink.  And it defaulted to the lowest heat setting after being off its base for a minute or more.  Meaning that I usually had to press three buttons 'Start' 'Boil', and 'Keep Warm' (the latter to turn it off, not to turn it on) just to get a cup of boiling water.  Finally, it seemed to have real trouble pouring the last bit of water - would get stuck somehow in the base of the kettle.  We're replacing it with something with a more classic and hopefully robust design.
Had lots of great reviews.  The on/off button got stuck two weeks after purchase.  Returned

text: Heats up well but for the price spout does not pour well
Body: Have had it for a month. It heats up well. But the spout with filter causes water to come in more than one stream. For the price the spout design is poor. Have had better spout designs for lesser money kettles.

My previous water kettle's lid no longer lifted on its own so I decided to buy a more expensive one hoping it would be better quality. The kettle itself is sturdy and the settings can be nice if you need it, but the pouring is awful. When I pour the hot water, the water splits into multiple streams and it's very hard precisely pour into my thin bottle. I have spilled the hot water multiple times because of this :(
My kettle leaks— I can no longer use it.

This electric kettle is pretty good, but it's definitely not my favorite. My old electric kettle was all tempered glass and, in my mind, perfect. This works well, but I don't like that I can't easily clean it or even see if it's built up scale deposits. In addition, if put back on the heating element with too low of water in it, it starts beeping that it's too hot and there are a lot of cracking/snapping sounds. This won't stop until you remove it or unplug it, even if the heating element is off.

This electric kettle is pretty good but not great.  It was also not cheap.  My old one wore out after a few years; I hope this one doesn't.  What doesn't work well?  The buttons are on the back of the handle, harder to reach than on my old kettle where the buttons are on the side.  having buttons where you hold the kettle makes the kettle more awkward to use.  When you put your kettle back on the power source (stand) after using, if it is dry it lights up because it overheats and then you have to unplug it until it cools and press start for a long time for it to reset.  My old one turned off when I took it off the stand.  So that was convenient and what I was used to. And this one was much more expensive than my other, off brand kettle.  I just hope it lasts a long time; the other one lasted a few years and then just died.  I have only had this one a few months.

I’m usually happy with Cuisinart appliances but this one has two features I dislike. Good news first: nice that it can be programmed to different temperatures and heats water fast. But the opening is a bit small; if you use a mug to measure water volume you need to exercise care not to spill. And the memory function should not turn the unit back on after it has reached temperature and beeped. You have to wait at least two minutes before putting the unit back on its base or it tries to boil again, even in the absence of water. If it just remembered your last temperature setting and delivered that the next time you hit start, that would be fine. There’s no way to change the memory function, so we quickly learned to set it on the counter after use.

I previously had this same pot for a few years. This is my second one. This has started randomly boiling about 2 months ago without an initiator which means it is a hazard. We had it for 10 months when it began. What is going on with Cuisinart?

text: It's okay, feels a little cheap
Body: We got this to replace a Breville Temp Select, whose electrical contacts had become flaky.  Neither wife nor I were crazy about the unit, although it works fine.  One day I used steel wool to clean the contacts on the Breville and we're back to using that one

This kettle is heavy! Even when empty. But it looks good.The temp preset buttons are too small.The water level window is located in the worst place possible. It would be much better if it was on the side.But this kettle does the job, so it stays.

This kettle has good temperature control and the "keep warm" function generally works nicely.  It heats quickly and quietly.  Those are all good, and they are important.But...The top is narrow and hard to fill.  The spout has a filter design that can sometimes result in an inconsistent pour (slow then fast, or swirling off to the side).  The level gauge is all but useless - the placement behind the handle makes it exceptionally hard to see while filling and the internal design has some pressure issues that make it inaccurate, especially at low water levels.  And the "keep warm" function shouldn't be used with "boil" or it will very quickly boil dry and demonstrate that it has an alarm for such occasions.At this price point, I expected better.

Love the temperature settings. Holds a good amount of water and boils quickly. Only thing I don't like is the 5 beeps when the temperature has been reached. 3 beeps would have been sufficient. Reminds me of my microwave beeping.

My kettle is leaking from the bottom and is just worn out. I have used it 2-4 times daily  since buying April 2015 from Amazon.  The letters on the buttons are faded, and has rusted at the bottom, but it has been a great buy and worth the money.  I will not purchase again though, just because the different temps wasn't as big of a deal as I thought- I make coffee in French press in the morning and drink different teas through out day.  I ended up using the same temp setting for everything.

It has multiple temperature settings, including "boil," but it doesn't boil the water. I've had this for about a year and a half. It works well for me because I don't want/need to boil water.  I use the 175 degrees setting for my beverage. I have a friend who also bought one around the time that I did, and she did want to boil water, so she returned hers. If you don't need to boil water, it otherwise works very well.
I loved this kettle. It heats up very fast. Unfortunately after only 6 months it broke.

It works fine.  The product heats water reasonably rapidly.  I like the ability to control temperature.  However the sides get hot.  It is a burn risk, particularly if used around children.  I got a mild burn the first time I used it when I inadvertently touched the side.  I would have given it a five rating if the sides did not get hot.

Basically, it's been a great kettle. We've used it several times a day for over six years. Nothing is completely flawless though and after awhile the weak points will fail. I think having a water window using a valve gives this a weak point. Some may find the water window a convenience without having to look inside the kettle to see water but, ultimately, this does provide a spot that will eventually fail and leak. I'm going to try a seamless kettle to see how long that lasts.

text: Who needs temperature settings for tea?
Body: I received this as a gift last year and thought it was too much.  Who needs temperature settings for boiling water?  But the more I tea I drank, I realized the temperature of the boil is in fact quite important.  I love that you can remove it from it's base.  You can take it to the sink to fill without dragging the cord.  My only dislike, and that is totally on me, is how heavy it is when filled.  I tend to not fill it completely, which only means I may have to half fill it twice a day.

text: Great but less great for small amounts
Body: We've only had this pot for a few weeks and so far it is working fine for our morning French press coffee and our daytime tea breaks. It's quite useful to have buttons dedicated to the different tea styles along with a French press button.Because of the short time I've owned it I cannot honestly give it 5 stars right now. The fill amount indicator facing the handle is very useful for coffeepot amounts of water but not so much if you just want one cup of tea water. Maybe they have or will have another model about 1/2 to 1/3rd the volume.

I use to heat water for single cups of tea and coffee.  It works fine for that. I have not checked the accuracy of its settings, but I can tell that the hottest setting is hotter than the coolest setting.  I have had one for several years and it has not failed. I liked it enough that I bought a second one for my home office so I don't have to go to the kitchen to make myself a cup of tea while working from home.

High quality...fast heating, well made. I use daily for months...multiple times a day and it just works.  High quality parts except for spout (Plastic parts). Just wonder why they went cheap on the spout area which has plastic inside when the rest of the unit is 100% metal. I don't like my high-temp water to touch plastic...as it's known to be bad for you. 1-star removed for that.

I have had this kettle for years and have used it daily for so many different things...pourover coffee in the morning, teas, boiling water for soup cups or quick cooking, even for hot water for cleaning uses. It's finally getting close to needing replaced, so I came back to Amazon to look at ordering another one. Amazon shows me that I last ordered it in Dec 2013. Eleven years and thousands of uses and it's still going!! Though I looked at some other kettles, as there are some very aesthetically pleasing designs out in recent years, the reviews can't compare to this Cuisinart. Don't hesitate to get it!!

I'm so happy I purchased this, and got rid of the other one I had.  I try to always go for quality products that will last.  I'm sick & tired of junk that breaks straight away and ends up in the landfill.  This unit is sturdy, from the kettle itself to the cord.  The buttons even.  Well worth the few extra bucks.

text: Use with Distilled water to eliminate mineral buildup
Body: These are excellent kettles for those who need temperature controlled hot water.  I drink Matcha in the mornings and it requires a lower temp.  I also drink other teas and the temps are noted on the handle.  My French Press coffee is there, too!  TIP:  If you use “distilled water” in these, you will never have build up or corrosion, and they never need cleaning.
The pot works beautifully and is easy to learn the buttons.  Warms the water, keeps it warm and turns off manually or automatically.

It holds enough for 2 large mugs or 3 ordinary cups. Heats up quickly and keeps the water warm at the desired temperature.  It is a little heavy for me when it is full (I am 90 years old).  Nice looking on the kitchen counter which matches my stainless steel appliances.

I am a tea drinker. I was boiling a pot of water and making a cup at a time until my daughter introduced me to the electric tea kettle. Changed things for me big time. Investigating different kettles and finding lots of negatives (including this one) made me nervous.  I decided to give the Cuisinart a try. I've had it about a year with no problems at all. I recommend this one.

My husband is British so this thing gets used MANY times a day. I love the different temp settings. It heats up FAST. The last one we had lasted 5 or 6 years. Then we bought a cheaper, off brand one (husband math) which broke 6 months in. Back to the Cuisinart. Buy this one, it's cheaper in the long run!!

I love the fast heating of this kettle. I love the different temperature settings for the perfect coffee, tea, or whatever you need. It's brushed stainless steel finish is easy to clean and no fingerprints. The only con for me is not being able to put my hand inside to clean it. You will need a cleaning brush that should be provided. It was a great deal, from a quality brand. I'm also happy with the automatic shut off, but wish there was a manual shut off button. All in all a very good product for the price.

text: Beware. The stainless steel coating at the bottom of ...
Body: Beware. The stainless steel coating at the bottom of the interior of my kettle dissolved after a couple of years.

text: Good temperature options but watch out
Body: Kelli works great with good options for temperature.  Keep warm function is nice bout would be helpful if it turned off after three or 4 rounds.We had had ours for about 6 months now and recently found the nut and washer that hold the sediment screen holder in a glass of tea.  So keep an eye out for these coming loose. I expect it will be hard to get this back in place.
Overall a good water kettle, but for the price it is disappointing that the numbers wore off and the water meter on the side doesn’t accurately show the amount of water in the kettle.

I’ve had this kettle for roughly 12 yrs now. It still works really well. The only downside is the temperatures on the buttons long since rubbed away, and I have to look up a picture of the dang thing to know which button I need to choose.

Intent of purchase was to replace a Krups electric kettle that had worn out. The Cuisinart is smaller than the Krups by 0.8 liter and had expanded  performance abilities on paper.  CONS:  The lid often sticks (button is poorly designed).  The exterior gets stains on it from water and they do not come off easily.  The level gauge is difficult to see, while holding the pitcher, because your hand blocks the view. The control panel on the handle is TERRIBLE; it often resets itself, will put the "keep warm" function into play without actually punching the button, or change the temperature to 160 degrees when it was set at 212 degrees. The biggest CON is that the kettle is unreliable and unpredictable.  The purpose of an automatic electric kettle is to operate when you are not watching it.  Fill this kettle and turn it on, then walk away only to find it has not heated the water.  I have tried standing by the kettle to see what happens and it simply signals with "beeps" that it is done, when it has only been heating for less than 90 seconds.  This doesn't happen every time, but frequently enough that I have to now stand by the kettle to be certain it will heat.  This makes me regret buying the device (never had this problem with the Krups).PROS:  It occasionally boils water (when it feels like it). The electric pad design is reasonably functional. Aesthetically, it is pleasant to look at.

Terrible design. Cannot turn the *&%^$#$ thing OFF!!!  Wakes everyone up. Incredibly annoying.Here's how it works. Pour in water, press temp button, press start, water hits temp quickly and kettle beeps like ten times really loudly (which you can't turn off by the way so it wakes up everyone within earshot) , pour out hot water, replace on base, try to turn of by pressing start button as it says in instructions --- but it won't turn off! It just continues to flash and flash and flash at you. Start button has no effect at all.  To get it to turn off after you pour out the water, you have to leave it on the counter, still very hot by the way, and not replace it on the base for a while. Finally after enough time has passed you can put it back on the base and it remains off. Stupid design. Every electrical appliance should have an OFF switch that turns off the item immediately - for safety's sake -- it's only common sense.Do not buy if you have to use this early in the morning and someone in your family sleeps near the kitchen.  It sounds like a really loud alarm clock when it reaches the target temp and it wakes them up. I now have to take it to a bathroom, and use it with the door closed to keep it from waking my kids.  The previous kettle i had may have been cheap plastic, but at least it did not operate as an alarm clock and wake up the baby.

text: Good for coffee, not for tea drinkers, poor quality
Body: I've been using this product for four years and it already leaking. The quality is not what Cuisinart used to be. I will avoid the company's products from now on until it goes back to making better quality products and avoid the trend towards bad quality at an expensive price.As an avid tea drinker, the product turns off after 15 minutes, sometimes less, which is too short when we drink for hours throughout the day.I'm disappointed that after four years, this product leaks. I have to make sure there is no water in it at night or else there is a puddle around it next morning. I will not buy this product and avoid the company's in the future.

I recently purchased this kettle because my old kettle stopped working. I did some research on different types of kettles and decided to purchase this one. Here's what I found so far.The look:I really like the look except for the fact that the window is hard to see so when pouring water into the kettle, you actually have to be very close to the window. This morning I had hard time even seeing the amount of water because the window was all steamy. Even though we haven't used it over night. They should definitely consider moving the window to a side.The feel:This kettle is made of metal and feels a little heavy. After a few minutes of pushing the "start" button, it gets real hot and makes it impossible to touch (even the lid), but the handle stays cool.The functionality:When I plugged in the kettle to the outlet and put it on base, the blue light in the window turned on and stayed on for about 10 minutes. There's no way to turn it off other than to take the kettle out of its base. I guess the light is useful if you want to see how much water you have in the kettle, but it is only useful when the kettle is on the base. I poured water all the way to the max, set it to "boil" and started the process. The buttons are not easy to press, sometimes it takes me a few times before it responds so I have to push the buttons harder. In a software age where gadgets like touch screens make it so easy to touch and expect an immediate response, I'd say this is a big flaw in the kettle. It took about 7.5 minutes to boil water at which point the kettle beeped softly three times and stopped working while the temperature "boil" and "start" buttons started blinking. If I was in the next room, I wouldn't be able to hear the beeps. I poured a cup of water out into my cup and pushed "keep warm" button a few times until it was lit. About a minute later it turned off so I wasn't sure if it was still working so I pushed it again a couple of times so the button lit and then it turned off again. I poured all water out and wanted to test "boil-dry protection" feature. It took maybe half a minute for the kettle to realize there's no water inside and it shut off and all the buttons started blinking. I took it off its base and put it back on hoping it would reset, but it didn't. I started pressing "start" button (according to the manual, pressing "start" will either start or stop the boiling process), but it didn't help. So I took the kettle of its base and left it on the table for about 10 minutes after which point I put it back on the base and it magically reset. I guess the two minute memory feature prevented the kettle from being reset.Overall, I would say it's a safe to use kettle if you don't touch it while it's hot. It definitely boils water fast and signals when it's done.

This is not a quality product. It does boil the water and keep it at temperature, which is why it gets a 2 star rating.Initially this product was great, and invade no problems. However, lately the product has been introducing debris into my otherwise clean water. This was not as noticabke in tea as it was in my coffee. No matter how much I rinsed the product, even with filtered water, the debris did not cease. I believed this was from some piece that was loosening. Hopefully, it was just some harmless glue and not like caulk or something because, as I said, it wasn't very noticeable in tea and initially I mistook this for some issue with my milk. Then some little black pieces began to show and I knew that this was going back.Cleaning was not very easy. The instructions say to wipe down after very use. I, however, had to let it air dry because my hands and several of my co-workers hands were too big to fit inside the unit. The scale filter obviously doesn't work either seeing as though those particles would make their way into my tea and coffee as evidenced by simply looking at the water in a clear glass, such as a french peess.There are also lots of piece that are inside of this product and most of them are plastic. Some plastic glass looking thing covering a screw I guess. Plastic housing for the scale filter, plastic line fo something inside the unit. Plastic top inside, plastic holding the top inside. It seems far too complicated. There are also clips or fastener s that hold the base together at th bottom.Very disappointed in the product.It's also very loud. Even when not boiling water I can hear it clearly over the TV from 15 feet away.

text: The Ultimate Convenience! but it won't last!!!
Body: I HAVE LOWERED MY RATING FROM 5 STARS TO 2:ORIGINAL REVIEW: I finally broke down and bought this kettle after pining after it for some time.  It took my old Braun actually falling apart to get me to make the purchase.  I wish I had bought this much sooner!!  It is an awesome product and looks great on my counter top.  It holds a large amount of water and heats it up fast to your desired temperature.  I use a French press (uses 200 degree water temp), and an AeroPress (uses 175 degree water temp) to make coffee and I love that now I no longer have to use a thermometer to make sure I am using the right temperature water.  I also make a variety of teas; green, oolong, herb and black.  This thing is just so amazing at how it simplifies something so simple as heating water!  LOL!! yeah, I know...some people think that heating water is a "no brainer" and it is.  But the features on this thing make it fun and even more of a "no brainer"!! Also, I love the keep warm feature because now you can walk away and come back to the perfect temp water even if you get distracted by something.  It is great when I have company because now I can have the 200 degree water ready for that second pot of French Press coffee when we want it!UPDATE: This only lasted one year and literally fell apart.  Too bad because I really did like the convenience.  I suspect, based on ratings and speaking to others, that all of the electric temp control kettles on the market are pieces of garbage.  I have gone back to using a good solid stovetop kettle:

I still own the original Cuisinart food processor. I have a newer Cuisinart food processor and many pieces of their cookware. I love the brand. I was looking for a kettle for my morning cuppa tea, and ordered one of these. Initially, I was delighted with it. I've had it about a year, and can now tell you what's wrong with it.The first issue that I had does not apply to many people. I live at 8,300' ASL, so water boils at a lower temperature. If you set the kettle to "Boil", it will not turn off at high altitude. It will finally shut off when the water level gets low, so it's not the end of the world. A minor issue, specific to a tiny fraction of customers.The big problem with this kettle is the construction. There is something about the seam at the bottom that does not take the heat cycle well. The kettle can sit cold, for days, and will not leak. If I fill it, and turn it on, after it comes to a boil there will be a half dozen drops of water between the base and the kettle. That would not be a big deal, except that the kettle has circuits that worry about water being where it does not belong. Ten minutes after you turn it off, it will start beeping and flashing and misbehaving, to warn you that there is water where it should not be. It's annoying. About all that you can do is to set the kettle on the counter, next to its base, rather than on it.I would not buy another one.

I PURCHASED THIS ITEM ON MAY 1, 2013.  ON APRIL 27, 2014 I NOTICED WATER ON MY COUNTER.  I KEPT A CLOSE EYE ON ON IT, THOUGHT I WAS OVER FILLING IT.  IT STARTED GETTING WORSE AFTER 3 DAYS. I NOTICED THE WATER WAS COMING OUT FROM THE BOTTOM OF THE HANDLE.  AMAZON WILL NOT TAKE IT BACK BECAUSE  THE RETURN POLICY EXPIRED. CAN NO LONGER BE RETURNED. SO NOW I AM GOING TO GET IN TOUCH WITH CUISINART TO SEE WHAT THEY SAY.  IT IS NOT A CHEAP ITEM AND SHOULD HAVE LASTED LONGER THAN 1 YEAR. ALSO THE WRITING ON THE BUTTONS HAVE WORN OFF WITHIN 5 MONTHS.  I AM NOT A HAPPY CAMPER, I BELIEVED IN CUISINART. OTHER THAN THAT I WAS VERY HAPPY WITH IT.  LOOK FOR MY UPDATE :  OK GOT IN TOUCH WITH CUISINART AND THANK GOODNESS I SENT IN THE WARRANTEE POST CARD, THEY HAD IT ON FILE AND IT IS FOR 3 YEARS. SO THEY ARE SENDING ME A NEW ONE I JUST HAVE TO PAY A $10.00 SHIPPING FEE AND THEN I HAVE TO RETURN IT ANY WAY I WANT TO AND I HAVE TO PAY TO RETURN IT. WHICH WILL BE THE SLOW BOAT CHEAP WAY.  WAS SATIFIED WITH CUISINART CUSTOMER SERVICE. STILL KEEPING A 2 STAR BECAUSE THIS SHOULD NOT HAVE HAPPENED.

I would not recommend this product. The first one we received was used daily for making tea. Within a month of using it the numbers for measurement/capacity started wearing off. My wife and I also noticed a nasty looking stain/corrosion of some kind on the inside of the kettle at the bottom. I thought maybe it needed a thorough cleaning even this isn’t something I’ve noticed on other electric kettles I’ve used at work and at our friends’ houses. We tried contacting Cuisinart about this and it took 2 weeks for them to finally get back to us only because Amazon had to step in. They sent us a new kettle and instructed us it should be drained after every use and left to drop. So we’ve been doing that and it also started corroding in the same place on the inside after just a couple of weeks of use. This is not worth $70 in my opinion. Spend your money elsewhere!

text: Not all it's jacked up to be...
Body: I bought this kettle in 2014 and have owned it for about 18 months.  I really liked it and paid what I consider to be above the usual price for a kettle.  I have a Cuisinart coffee pot that I love and have owned for 5 years.  The last kettle was a Braun, and it lasted 8 years.  I loved it.  Of course, it wasn't a new fangled contraption that was cordless and lit up with variable temp. control!  It was a plug in kettle that isn't produced any more.So, I bought a new kettle.  It's not a Cuisinart!  If it breaks in a year, I can replace it 3 times before I end up with the same cost and it looks a lot like the Cuisinart, which appears to represent quality, but apparently only if you can afford a replacement every 18 months to 2 years.  Sorry!  If I pay around $100 for a kettle, it should last slightly more than 3 years.I'm looking to make a cup of tea, not refinance the company.

text: Doesn't hold up, the quality is not what you deserve for the price.
Body: I wanted to like this kettle, I really did., so much so that I have purchased two of them.  But no more.  They are sleek, modern looking and seem to do all the things a serious tea drinker wants in a kettle.  Push button temperature controls, warming feature, easy to see water level.  But the fact is, my first one died after a year of use.  It was already looking a bit worn with the labels getting hard to read.  I bought a replacement anyway, and after a year, the labels were almost gone.  And, though it was still operating, the temperature regulation was next to worthless.  I finally gave up the dream.  I now own a Bonavita goose neck kettle.  It isn't quite as slick, and the control panel looks like some sort of lab instrument, but it works like a dream and pours so well. For two years it has been warming my water to perfection to indulge my taste in tea.  So long Cuisinart, You promised, but didn't deliver.  I have found happiness elsewhere.

text: Not Worth the Cost Due to Short Life
Body: I purchased this kettle in 2010. That may seem like a decent life for an electric kettle, but it has been failing for years. I have to keep the cord curved in a slight half circle to get it to work and, even then, it only works sometimes. When it works, it is a great kettle. I would use this multiple times daily for tea but I can only get it to work every few days. This has been an issue for years. Since its purchase, I have made sure that I never leave water sitting in this kettle when not being used, I only use reverse osmosis water in it, and I frequently run the kettle with RO water and some vinegar in it to keep it free of mineral buildup. I only use a damp cloth to clean the outside of the kettle and it has never been submerged. The kettle has always been on my kitchen counter so it never gets bumped around or hit, nor does the cord get bent. I am the child of an Electrical Engineer so I know how to properly care for electrical appliances. For what this kettle cost, I expected a much longer, episode-free life. I called Cuisinart's Customer Service twice and was told that I have had this kettle for years and I should not expect that long of a life from an appliance. Both reps expressed surprise that it has lasted me this long, despite it's sporadic performance. Both offered me a 20% discount off a new $100 dollar version. Cuisinart's temperature variable kettle is not inexpensive. I expect more quality from a product priced as high as this kettle is. If I am only to expect a short life from a Cuisinart product, I will not make the mistake of buying another. I bought a different temperature variable electric kettle as a gift for a family member at a fraction of the price of this Cuisinart unit, the gift kettle has all the same functions and none of the performance issues. I will replace this with an inexpensive temperature variable electric kettle.

text: Dangerous, impossible to empty, but handy for childless lovers of fine tea
Body: I've had this kettle for 9 months. It's my go-to kettle for tea because I love having several options of temperatures, and I love the keep-warm feature which allows me to easily brew several small infusions of tea over 30 minutes (or more). Also it's very quick to come to temp, and I like the audible alert when the water's ready. BUT:This kettle is dangerous. I can't believe this isn't mentioned in every single review. This kettle is a single-walled, stainless steel design. Stainless steel is a fantastic thermal conductor. If the water inside the single stainless steel wall is 212 degrees, what temperature do you think the outside of the stainless steel wall is? About 212 degrees. I'm serious. Do not touch the walls of this thing while water is boiling in it! Or even near boiling in it. How did this get approved for sale in the US? Do not let your kids anywhere near this while you're using it! I don't have kids and I know not to touch it when it's operating (guess how I know!), so this is okay with me since holding it by the handle is perfectly comfortable. But really, I'm stunned that it's allowed on the market.Also, the last ounce or two of water does not pour out cleanly, and you simply cannot completely drain the kettle. This is due to the plastic clip that is bolted over the pour spout on the interior. The clip holds the filter, which is meant to keep flakes from hard water build up from ending up in your cup. But whether or not you use the filter (I don't), that clip interferes with the stream of water in such a way that the last ounce or two of water pours out not in one coherent stream but in 3-5 separate trickles, one of which drips down from above the spout! And the last tablespoon or two of water simply will not come out no matter how you hold / jiggle / shake the pot. Very annoying.Despite those two design flaws, one of which is IMO very serious, I still use it because it's the only option I've found that lets me quickly bring a small volume of water (less than 1/2 liter) to any of several different temps and hold it there for 30 minutes (or more if you hit Start again). But if there was a comparably priced alternative without these two major flaws, I'd buy that one instead.

text: Comparing it with KRUPS, there are highs and lows.
Body: Comparing to.This kettle performs exactly the same - when set to Boil, it boils 1L of water in exactly the same time as the KRUPS.Ergonomically, the handle is less comfortable than KRUPS - you can't reach the Open button as easily.I like that it turns on to the last setting when you pour some water in it and put it back on the base - no chance of forgetting to turn it on, which I do on occasion.  I also like that it beeps when it's done - 5 quiet chimes.  I definitely like that the lid is insulated, and doesn't get very hot.I don't like that the scale is on the back - when you pour water into it while holding it in your hand, it tends to read low (the kettle tends to lean forward, due to the handle not very well designed).  Have to adjust to pour less water into, in the hopes that it'll be correct when it's back on the base.But there is a problem: the lid sticks when the kettle is hot.  Sometimes it takes a few seconds to open, sometimes it doesn't open at all, and you have to wait for it to cool down (or pry it open with something - when is risky if you choose your fingers or nails).  I ordered a replacement./edit Replacement arrived today, and I see the problem.  There is a slight difference in alignment of the lid.  My first kettle has the lid shifted off-center maybe about 1mm toward the front of the kettle.  This is enough to make it bind when it's hot.  The second kettle lid is right on center, so it doesn't bind.  Buyers beware.

Our previous electric kettle after 8 or so years died, and I loved it. Since that kettle is no longer available we ordered this as a replacement. It's ok. I had to carefully read the instruction guide to find out that to turn it off you press "start" a second time. You have to press the buttons firmly, occasionally it doesn't register that you pressed a temperature button. The casing is metal, as opposed to the plastic of my previous kettle. I reached past it to get a teabag and brushed my arm against it and felt like I burned myself. Luckily there was no mark on my arm. It has a water level guide under the handle which is hard to see where it's at unless I jiggle the kettle or pick it up from the base to make it light up. And lastly, if I have a low amount of water in the kettle when I go to pour it I guess condenses on the lid and pours weirdly, like from both the spout and the lid.But it does heat the water for my tea, seems a bit hotter than the previous kettle did, even at the green tea setting. Gets the job done and that's what counts, I suppose. Still wish I could have gotten my other kettle again instead.

text: It does what it's supposed to and it does it well.
Body: Update: it’s now been 10 years, and it’s been acting up so I’m researching what to get as a replacement. The boil is now actually boiling about 30% of the time, the rest of the time it shuts off much faster without getting the water hot.—-I bought this this in 2010, I guess it's time for a review :)I've had this tea kettle for 6 years now, it's moved across the country with me (I only took things that fit in my car, so that's a high bar!) and I still love it.What I like: variable water temperature that makes me excellent green tea - even if I forget to take the bag out, the water cools off quickly enough that it doesn't taste over-steeped. Water heats up fast. Keep-hot feature is very useful.I tossed the filter thing immediately, so I don't have any issues with pouring. I always use reverse osmosis filtered water, so buildup has not been a problemAnnoyances: unlike most kettles, when you lift it off the base, it does not shut off automatically. The water level indicator is not always correct at low levels. Occasionally it does not shut off properly (keeps heating even after it boils or, more dangerously, even when it's empty). This is very rare though.I have not had issues with numbers rubbing off, but that's likely because I don't change settings that often. They're a little faded but still legible.Bottom line: optimal water warmer for tea lovers who don't want to spend tons of money on a

After just a few days of use, we are not impressed.  If you are used to a kettle that auto shuts off once you lift it off the base, be forewarned.  This pot will instead auto warm if it is placed back on the base within a couple of minutes.  There is not an off button, so option is to unplug it or keep the kettle off the base!  We do not use a keep warm cycle as we use the majority of the kettle. We end up keeping it off the base, cuz we  don’t like the gunk of hard water scale being boiled onto the bottom!  The kettle is NOT as easy to clean as previously owned kettles.  The opening is small and the non removable lid makes it challenging to fill too.  Since we need a larger kettle, we will use it, but won’t be buying it again if it fails!

I'm a little dismayed about this product, which I bought several months ago. I love all its features and was specifically wanting a kettle that would let me choose the temperature according to the tea I choose to brew. But the problem is the unit's structure. The lid - that lifts up automatically when you push the OPEN button - stopped lifting. At first, I was able to raise it manually but then it was simply not moving. I tried all kinds of ways to get it open, but eventually gave up and requested a replacement, since the unit was still under warranty. (I'll leave out how long this took, by the way.) I paid $15 for the replacement unit, plus the cost of shipping back the broken one. When the new unit arrived, there were problems getting it to connect with its (also new) base. Sometimes it would fire up, but more often it would not. Jiggling the cord sometimes helped, but clearly it was broken. I called Cuisinart again, and they said the problem was the base and - gratis - sent a new base. Two weeks later when it arrived, I had the same problem, so clearly the issue is with the kettle, not the base. As I type this, they've agreed to replace the replacement kettle and base at no charge (as they should), so we shall see what's up.

I received this kettle a week or two ago and have used it for french press coffee and tea steeped in a mug and in a teapot.  So far everything is excellent.  I love the keep warm feature, as I don't often jump right up to get the water when it says the water is ready. I love how the pot itself is wireless so I can take it across the kitchen.  My tea and coffee are perfect!  No more thermometers to make sure the water is the right temperature!The only things I don't like are that it's not as quick as I'd like, that's not to say it's not faster than boiling water stove-top or in the microwave, but I've had kettles that heated faster.  Also, the outside of the kettle gets very hot, keep things away from it when heating water.  The handle is no problem, that's quit cool, so no worries about burning yourself, just make sure there are no other items touching the kettle and that young hands stay away.Great kettle for the price!A few years later and the kettle works as it always has, it’s just the temp labels on the buttons have all but worn off, leaving me to either remember what they are or look up a picture of the kettle. It also left some rust stains on my counter, but that’s partially my fault for not wiping underneath it when fluids are on the counter, HOWEVER, it’s a high traffic kitchen counter... it’s going to get wet, I just wish the base were as rust resistant as the rest of it.

Works great. I love the fact it keeps the water at the right temp. I french press my coffee so its ready when I am to make another pot. It takes 5 minutes for it to turn off if you don't have it set to keep the water at temp. At first I thought something was not right but after reading the manual that is the design.*** 4 Month update ***Got up this morning to make my coffee and it just beeps at me like so many others. I will contact Cuisinart but I shouldn't have to, it should still be working after only 4 months and used once daily. I was cautious after reading the reviews on this but sure enough, it happened to me as well. I've taken good care of it and before it broke it did work great but with so many having this issue its simply a badly designed product or cheap parts.*** Update to 4 Month Update ***I left it unplugged for a couple of days and it started working again. Don't know why but works for me. It is still working today so only once has it not wanted to heat the water up but does have me worried it won't last near as long as the Breville I have.

text: Love my Perfec Temp - (Edit: slightly less than my initial review due to a couple problems)
Body: I love this Cuisinart Perfec Temp Kettle. Only wish it was came in a 2 liter model as I typically make 2 quarts of ice tea at a time.Only 1 very slight design flaw... when pouring the last cup from the kettle, the water comes from the lip of the spout (where it should) and also from the upper edge of the hole in the kettle where the spout is located. It all goes in the cup, so no problem. But if I were working on the next improved model, there are a couple easy ways to fix this... lower the top edge of the spout hole or put a baffle inside the unit to prevent water from getting to the top of the unit when tipped to get the last cup.June 2017 edit: My initial review was 5 stars. I've lowered it to 4. I was going to lower it to 3, as I was having an issue with my new one, but I begrudgingly give it a 4 as the problem seems to be getting better with time.So, I'm on my 2nd CPK-17 now. My first CPK-17 developed a leak at the bottom of the handle. And, leaving it filled overnight resulted in a small puddle of water below the base in the morning. I really liked my first kettle, so I purchased another. Unfortunately, I'm having a problem that others have mentioned in having difficulty opening the lid. While my 1st kettle only rarely did not open on the 1st press, it always opened on the 2nd. My new kettle has not been as cooperative. And *one* time I had to SHAKE it while half full about 10 times while holding the button, before the lid finally popped open. I've only had this new one a couple weeks now and, so far, that has only happened once, but it frequently takes more that one press of the button before the lid will open. This problem is improving with use so I'm hoping the lid will loosen up further over time.2nd edit: So it's been over a week now since my previous edit and it looks like the lid has loosened. I've been using my 2nd CPK-17 two times a day and the problem experienced with the lid failing to open hasn't occurred once since my previous edit.

4/2024 - Been ~7 years and it still works well.  With the caveat that this basically got stashed until fall and only used until spring the first few years, this electric tea pot is still working great. It’s now getting daily use multiple times a day, as I have donated it to my office break room. Everyone loves it and the option to choose how hot your tea is heated. The only draw back is it does take 5 minutes or so for it to heat to the hottest setting - boil for black tea. Another issue is cleaning. Unless you have small hands, you’re going to need to get a bottle brush or something long to clean…we clean it regularly with vinegar.Just got this  as a Christmas gift as I am a tea lover. So far it is working as  advertised, so I can't speak for those that have had issues with it for long-term use.  I can't say that I do like that it is stainless steel  and fits well on my small kitchen counter considering it size.  However,  this could be designed a little better  and there are a few things to note if you are considering purchasing this. First, the outside, with the exception of the handle, can get very hot. If you have children or any unsuspecting person in the kitchen, this can be an issue. Secondly, the cord to the heating unit is very short, maybe 6-8 inches.  If you plan on having this, make sure you are able to place it very close to an outlet. Will post an update with more use.

Bought my kettle in July of 2019.  I have had no problems with leakage or temp numbers rubbing off as some reviewers have described. Unfortunately, the Keep Warm function has stopped working all together, either in the default mode after the kettle has reached the set temperature or if I try to manually turn on the function.  This is not a large problem for me since I only occasionally use this function.  Otherwise this kettle has served my well for the 2 1/2 years.  I use it MULTIPLE times a day for anything from coffee and tea prep, to heating water for washing dishes and preheating water which will be placed in a pot on the stove for cooking. I suppose my kettle has easily been through three years of use in just 2 1/2 years.  For me, the effort and expense of trying to take advantage of the 3 year warranty for just the Keep Warm function is not worth it and I will continue to use the kettle until it stops working completely. The price has risen so much, since my purchase, I will have to find a less expensive substitute when that happens.

text: excellent right out of the box
Body: update: one month, very happy!! So easy to get hot water, with optional temps!  Prior:  Glad I got this.  Only used two days, happy so far!  Just fill, press the temp you want, start.  Literally less than 3 minutes to heat up.  1L was under 2 mins to 160.  So the Pro's are:  the SS looks nice, sits stable on the heat plate, cordless serving, no spill spout.  A low, blue light is on while heating , easy push button to start.  When done, three low chimes tell you it's done.  This is very low and will not wake the sleeping spouse.  FYI:  the cord is short.  12 to 15 inches short.  You must put base near an outlet.  There is some plastic, inside, due to it having a mesh filter at the pour spout.  I think most people filter water before filling the tea kettle, so it does not do much.  But I also think it's low contact with your water, during a few seconds of pouring.  Having control over the temperature is great.  It's accurate.  I tested first pot to 160, my household meat thermometer said same.  Con:  Only one, you cannot easily clean the inside.  Barely maneuver a bottle brush in there!  Fill hole is large enough to easily fill, but no adult can get their hand in it.  Totally does what it says.  Hope this helps.

text: Awesome kettle (except for the button labels)
Body: Bought this kettle for an office of about 20 people, each of whom have their own favorite hot beverages. And some are very particular about how they brew their favorite teas, so the temperature controls were the main selling point for me. So far we've had the kettle about 8 months and used it daily with great results.The only issue is that the label for each button is wearing off, and the deterioration started fairly soon after we unboxed the kettle. For example, the "Boil" button is now blank because the ink has rubbed off underneath my coworkers' thumbs. So now I have to figure out how to re-label the buttons without making this cool kettle look janky. :)Just putting that out there for any office managers looking for a crowd-pleasing kettle. Add a label maker to your order, and you're all set.UPDATE: It's been a couple years, and now the lid cover keeps coming off, which means the spring mechanism is uncovered and stops working. Our accountant tried repairing it, but then the spring sprang off somewhere and we had to try to make do with a spring from a pen. It was a comedy of errors. I'm psyched that it took two years for it to break like this, but it's getting a tad annoying to keep fixing. Otherwise it's still working fine and still looks good.

Growing up, I was never a huge tea drinker. I never liked the taste. As I've gotten older, I have grown to love chamomile tea as it is soothing and helps relax me before bed. Prior to ordering this electric tea kettle, I was boiling water on the stove. This product has made my tea making process so much easier!
