And for whenever I want to try to branch out to different types of tea, I have the handy little buttons to help me get the water to the correct temperature so I can enjoy each tea as it is supposed to be enjoyed. I would highly recommend this product! Also, while reading reviews for this product before purchase, I noticed a LOT of reviews saying that the beeping is annoying. However, the beeping is much quieter than even my microwave beeping and I have had no complaints about the volume of the beeping since owning it. :)

text: Cuisinart Stainless Steel Cordless Electric Kettle Review
Body: I hadn't had an electric teapot for years, but I started drinking tea again, so I decided to buy another one.This electric kettle is absolutely fantastic! I like everything about it. Multiple lighted buttons for selecting the temperature you want the water to be at when you pour it into whatever you are making. The temperature button you've selected flashes while heating water, and then beeps and shines solid blue when the water has reached the exact temperature you selected. I love the fact that at any time I can lift the kettle from its thin base, with no cord attached to the kettle, to pour the hot water, returning it when done. The water stays at the same temperature you selected before. It heats water quickly, amazingly fast. It's exciting to buy a product that not only does what you want it to do, but you find that it does even more and better than you expected.

text: Probably the best electric pot for the price
Body: I read some outside reviews and thus bought this one.  It was ranked best buy for a great operating tea pot two years in a row.  I did my own checking with a digital thermometer.  I ran it through all the heat settings with one liter of plain water.  My thermometer has a 2% error, and with that each temp setting was only 5 degrees hotter than the setting I chose.  A very consistent 5 degrees, which if you figure in my thermometer's 2% at 200 degrees, that is 4 degrees making the pot only one degree off.  Or you could say my thermometer is dead on and the pot is only 2% off.  Either way that is pretty darn close for a pot less than $80.  It also has a very thick cord to handle the current which is very important.  Too often they cheap out on the copper cord which in a high amp circuit can cause problems.  One other thing to consider is that the cheaper pots us a bimetal thermal disk to shut off at one temp.  My first pot was one of these types and after only a few uses the bimetal disk started to malfunction and keep the pot on far too long.  This can be a fire hazard.  The Cuisinart is digitally controlled and uses a solid base which also blocks the contacts so that a child can't accidently shock themselves, which my first one lacked.  All in all, this is a very well built pot and doesn't look like they tried to cheap out on the important stuff.  It even has two color LED lighting for the switches and water meter, at first thought it was a gimmick until I used it at night.  Unless something drastically goes wrong, I would definitely recommend this pot for the tea brewer.

After researching many electric kettles, I settled on this one as I have had great success with other Cuissenart products and this one is no exception.  The preset temps are accurate and gain that temp quickly.  If you want the proper brewing temperature for coffee for example...it needs to be between 197F and 205F.  (Please note that most of the electric coffee makers are not supplying water  that hot and are not getting proper extraction of the flavor you should be getting).  This kettle will get the water to 200F in 5 minutes.  It will then maintain that temp for 30 minutes and shutting down.  Other brands shut down in 20 minutes.No worries there, so if you need to get more hot water for another pot or maybe a rousing cup of tea, it gets hot very fast.  And I used a Thermoworx probe thermometer that I know is dead on accurate....and this kettle is there!  You will love this.

text: Rust in less than a year
Body: The good: nice size, several temperature settings, gets to temperature quickly, easy to use.The bad: had it less than a year and it's rusting.Do not recommend, unless you like to buy new kettles every few months.

text: Is it still safe to use?
Body: Received kettle on June 1st.  Loved the way it worked however it has developed spots / discoloration on the bottom.  Efforts to clean kettle were not successful.  What are these spots?  Is kettle safe to continue using?
Piece of junk equipment, had this for about a week and now it dosent work. Seems like this is a common problem for this model. It just beeps and flashes and doesn’t heat or anything. Avoid buying

Kettle is 'nice enough'. Works 'okay' I have had cheaper kettles with pre-set temperatures that were easily better and faster. So it is not impressive at all, but - it works - so... I kept it - you know.However, the rust is unacceptable. NEVER seen this in any other kettle.
Purchased this item brand new and it arrived in a box that was not sealed, with rust and scaling all over it, with the packaging torn.

text: Getting rusty for this one too
Body: I bought same kettle 3 times via Amazon; 2 for family members as well. However, I am seeing rusty spots on the bottom of the kettle and been drinking the water from it for the last few months now. Check inside of the kettle regularly.

There was various rust and yellow stains on the kettle! The open button was broken. This kettle looked like it was a few years old and used! I usually love Cuisinart products. I'm not sure what happened here. They must have left a used damaged kettle in with the new products????? I was very disappointed and have never had this problem in the past with any Cuisinart product.
There is rust around the bottom seam after six months.  I don't want to drink that.  I have had cheep kettles that have never rusted.

After 5 months of use twice daily, the words were wearing off on the handle (See photo).  They sent another unit to replace it which was not only not assembled correctly, but also a safety hazard. (See photos). After waiting on hold with Cuisinart 35 minutes, I was told they do not issue refunds so they can only send me another unit and hope that one works. So sad when a good brand goes sour. Maybe 3rd time is the charm? ​I advise you to not trust them and shop for other kettles.

we are very disappointed about Amazon delivery without a quality check. We ordered Cuisinart CPK-17P1 CPK-17 PerfecTemp 1.7-Liter for hot drinking water.Delivered on time when we opened the package it looks used as we saw some watermarks in the bottom of the pot. but we thought its not washed properly during manufacturing. We washed and tried to use it. Lights blinking for some time then stopped but the water was not heated.I called Amazon customer service and he asked to run the same steps again but the same results. He tried to contact the manufacturer put me on hold for more than 30 minutes and told me that they are busy unable to contact them.I have no option just returned and asked for a replacement . We received new one I see the look difference and its working.Please see attached pictures for Old one vs New one.

I was extremely cautious when using this tea kettle to avoid mold spots that people mentioned in the reviews. However after a short three weeks of using the kettle they appeared. This tea kettle is not worth the extra money.
The first time use it already comes out the poor quality

I have owned electric kettles before, and they were "good enough" to boil water, but this one is far superior.  I originally saw this kettle in an article in wired magazine.  I then checked out Amazon reviews to see alot of positive feedback.  It is as promised.  While I do not often use the other temperature settings since I mostly drink black tea, when I do, it is spot on.  If I had to think of a negative, it would be that the kettle gets hot.  I know...so do all the others, and so does a pot.  My only concern is that it can be deceptive.  You can shut it off and it will still be hot.  It is not an issue for me, but might be for someone with small kids.

The kettle worked well for 4 years, loved it. Now it has started leaking from the bottom. Given the price of the kettle it is disappointing to throw it away due to this although kettle is working well.

I was initially very pleased with this electric kettle. It seems to heat water well and keeps it warm by coming back on at intervals. It does get very hot, so I must be very careful not to brush against the outside of the kettle. I never heated anything but water. The kettle is apparently stainless steel, but there is some kind of coating in the interior, at least on the bottom, and that began to wear off almost immediately. I have finally decided I am not comfortable continuing to use the kettle. Whatever is wearing off is ending up in the things I drink. If it were not for this issue, I would recommend the kettle.

After just two months, the spout became detached from the body. After three months, the lid hinge began to show signs of rust. This kettle comes at a premium price point (2x most comparable products), so I was expecting years of use. I am very disappointed with the build quality.

text: The printed Temperature wiped fast. Bottom inside rusted, and, now, the lid fell apart.
Body: See the picture.1. The printed Temperature button numbers on the handle faded fast.2.The bottom inside rusted, although it was stainless, and,3. now, the lid fell apart.It looks fancy with the idea of controlling the temperature of the hot water, but, boiling water was extremely slow, and, it requires quite patience.Now, with the gentle handling each time, still the lid fell apart suddenly, used in a single household."Functional Obsolescence" classic!When the lid was intact, the lid did not open wide enough for the fridge water nozzle, and, I had to use a beaker each time.And, "Keep warm" button sometimes comes on with the ON button, and many times, it did not. Just unpredictable annoyance, too.

text: Good heat power, but dangerous with continuous warming feature.
Body: This is a good looking pot and the kettle produces a great amount of heat in a short time. It is really convenient that you have many preset temperatures that you can choose from. The kettle looks sleek and is easy to clean. However, it is hard to see the amount of water in the kettle as the clear part is small and somewhat opaque. My biggest complaint is the product is dangerous to have the kettle automatically keep the water warm. There is no option to have the warmer on or not, so the kettle will continuously try to heat the water even if there is nothing in the kettle. This is a major downfall since there are not any clear safety features to ensure the kettle turns off when it is done heating.

The item in subject is built fairly well, feels solid and heats water to set temperatures quickly. The reason for the low star review is that the item is subject after a fair amount of uses in less than a month started to leak at the bottom of the handle. I believe whatever the material used to seal the container has degraded.

text: Stopped working after almost two years.
Body: I bought this kettle March 29 2016 as a gift to my husband despite bad reviews. It worked like a charm. The buttons where you choose the temperature never got erased like it happened to some other reviewers. I payed almost a hundred dollars for it.The performance while it worked was great in my opinion. Although I must say we only used boil and 200• for French press coffee. My husband, as much as he loves tea, he never wanted to bother changing temperature .... oh well.... that was his  preference. Like I said I did not get to try the other temperatures but it worked just fine for us.A word of caution: it does get really hot to the touch. it wasn’t an issue for us since the handle is not hot but once while cooking I touched it and it startled me but no bad burns. My husband used to clean it with white vinegar . Three weeks ago the kettle stopped shutting off. A week later it just fixed itself and started working again. Then this week it just won’t hear the water.We used this kettle minimum of 2 times a day ,  4 tops. Every single day.I really enjoyed while it works and looks elegant. I just don’t know What else to say... is it a 100 dlls kettle supposed to work for just two years?.

Bought this in 2016, and use it to this day. Heats up fast, temp control is great, very solid kettle. One thing I want to mention is that I got the base of the kettle wet and that's where all the electronics are. Long story short the water got to the relay inside and overtime it rusted out and stopped working (2019). I ordered a pair of relays from eBay for $2, soldered one in and it's been working ever since. Also, I see a lot of people complaining about letters rubbing off. I have no idea how that's accomplished. It has been over 4 years and all of mine are there (see proof). Not a single one erased. I use this kettle up to 10 times per day every day. Perhaps oily fingers are the culprit? Or cleaning it with an sos pad? :) Anyway, I am sure if you don't submerge the kettle in water it will last you a long time. Oh and wash your hands before pushing buttons too.

Bought this kettle in May of 2015 and have made more hot water for tea and coffee than I can possibly recall.Unfortunately just four months after it's 3 year warranty has expired the base of the kettle where the handle meets the bottom is now leaking each time water is heated (see pic). Since it's out of warranty I don't see how I get this repaired and am likely going to have to buy something new. Bottom line, it's great while it lasts, which in this case is 3 years, 4 months.
I love that I can set the exact temperature depending on what type of tea I’m drinking.

I had no idea how much I would love this kettle! It heats up so quick! I love the different settings for various teas. I warm water for hot chocolate using the lowest setting (160 delicate) and it is the perfect temperature! Have used it every day since it arrived. Awesome purchase!
It’s a little pricey have to admit it but also it looks great and works perfectly! Boiled water within minutes and it is not as loud as my old kettle! Would recommend!
easy to use, easy to clean

This kettle works great in my opinion. I am located on the east coast of Florida, so am basically at sea level. If you live at a higher altitude, you will have different results.  I’ve attached my time and temp results for .5 liters (min) and 1.7 liters (max) of water. All temperature results fluctuated within ∓1° of stated results I normally use .5 liters of water @ 200° in the morning for two cups of French Press coffee.When my kettle arrived I couldn’t wait to try it out. I filled it to the .5 liter line and started it for 200°. When it beeped, I poured the water out and checked the temperature and set the empty pot back on the plate. EGADS! All the light started flashing. The ONLY way I could find to stop the flashing was to unplug the kettle and plug it back in. I thought that I must have gotten a defective kettle. WRONG!This kettle, unlike most kettles, has the “keep warm” function turned on as the default. I thought that this was good feature but, not in my case. When you place an empty kettle back on its base, it continues the keep warm function and since there is no water in it, it flashes all the lights to warn you of low water levels. Once I turned off the “keep warm” function, it worked great. And the nice thing is that once the function is turned off, it stays off for the future… unless you reset the machine by unplugging it.This kettle remembers the settings that you last used (for me 200° and “keep warm” off), so subsequent mornings, all I have to do is hit the start button.I LIKE IT!ADDENDUM: I made a modification. I removed the filter holder assembly allowing the unit to pour smoother. I had to remove the SMALL nut holding it in using a 1/4" ratchet and socket.

text: Best Electric Tea Pot… and I only drink tea!
Body: Easy to use, great speed in heating water and excellent safety features….

text: It’s been five years so I might as well write a positive review because I use it every single day!
Body: Edit 4/2023: we have reached our eighth birthday. I love this thing. The print on the button is starting to wear off where I hit at the most, 200° and start. Eventually I’ll get a new one but it works just fine. I love it and it was worth every dollar.I bought this nice little guy over five years ago. It seems like some people get a lemon every now and again but I surely did not! Even with five years, the lettering has not really worn off very much. In fact it doesn’t look like a five-year-old appliance. It never turned rusty, it doesn’t really require maintenance. Are use it on average at least three times a day plus. Some of them seem to give out earlier in life but I’m very grateful that the one I have is not like that. My biggest complaint is that five years ago  I definitely paid over $99. I can say with confidence that when mine dies eventually, i’m either going to get this exact version again or just one of those pretty clear ones because they are pretty. But I’ve had great experiences. I use the different temperature controls or really expensive tea, so it’s absolutely vital to get the temperature control correct. I’m a big fan of the 200° button because of how much better my coffee tastes, etc.Highly highly recommend, although you might get a lemon like some people do and hopefully you don’t!

text: User friendly and great hearing features
Body: I did a bit of research before ordering as I am an old school teapot on the Stove kind of gal.  The problem is my family thinks I’ve forgotten the stove is on (ignoring the fact that I drink tea ALL DAY LONG) and they turning off...all day long.  Enter the Cuisinart...I really wanted to have temp control, Stay warm, cute and 1.7L capacity.  I had to give up CUTE.  I read reviews here, on America’s Test Kitchen and Other consumer ratings sites, and this won out overall.I like the wide lid opening for refill.  I love the temp controls and the speed so far!Delicate 160• took 5:40 from cold and Boil took 8 min from cold (I’m basically at sea level).  I also love the “keep warm function is auto off at :30 min.I took the pic for scale next to my 10 cup Instapot .It does get a bit warm to you h on the outside so keep your Little’s or your wimpy’s away from it when in use.I did 3 different test runs of boil/ heAt and dump to get rid of factory smell.2nd pic is steeping a cup of black and showing how it looks In “keep warm” mode.Only 4 on cleaning And safety as the outside did heat up and the opening would still be a bit difficult to get my hand OT to scrub if needed (but I have large hands).

text: Still working after all these years
Body: We've had this kettle for at least 4 years now and have had no problems with it, and it still looks great! We use it almost daily for so many things. I would definitely buy this again.

I love this electric tea kettle. I have used it with no problems for 5 years.  I read some of the reviews and noticed some people complaining about the writing rubbing off.  I did have that happen, but it doesn't interfere with the functionality in any way.  I am very happy with this purchase.  It is hard to find things that actually work that long.
I have used it for 2 months now and I have had many complements on how it looks on my kitchen. So far I haven't had any problems with it. I love the beep after the boil is complete.

text: Excelente calidad, buen ajuste de su base.
Body: Un poco cara pero lo vale la compra,  calienta muy rápido, cumple bien su función, fácil de operar. Única desventaja es que no trae botón de apagado.

So sad. This arrived with box damaged outside. Inside was messed up. The pitcher  looked used, had water inside and out. Packaging wet....how can this be if Item is new? I was so looking forward to using it tonight . It is replacing the one that I've had for over 20 years. Very disappointed. Yes I am returning it. So I can't tell you how item was. Won't  let me post photo.
IT STOPPED WORKING AFTER TWO MONTHS. Why did I bother upgrading my electric kettle to something "nicer" just for it to break so quickly. It's infuriating.
product stopped working all together. waste of money. had it for 45 days.
This product has about a four year lifespan, after which it will leak all over your counter.
Do not buy this product. It started leaking from the base after 4 months! Not worth any money.
This kettle worked for 6 months . The temperature selection settings stopped working. I don’t know all these ratings. Poor quality.
Very ugly and company will not process return.  Amazon should provide a warning about this before purchase.

I called last week and complained to a lady, that i used the kettle once. The next day when I tried to use it again, It didn't work. The lady whom I complained to, requested me not to return it, and my account will be recredited. Please arrange to credit my account.
Overpriced garbage if it can’t last a month!
Kettle over boiling and not heating correctly - one month in. Basic household use for 1 person. DO NOT BUY!
Water must come in contact with plastic components inside the kettle
Overpriced for no reason and stopped working today less than a year of purchasing it

text: It suddenly stop working. Not worthy for the price
Body: We purchased it in February of this year, now is it October. It has stopped working. Not working for the price.
I liked this product while it worked but at 14 months it quit working for no apparent reason.  Do not purchase
Too many options and if you don’t take it off from the charger it will always keep warm. And the auto shut off is confusing, the light stays on.

I liked that the water heated quickly  but for someone with small hands, this kettle not so easy to use.  I also found all the blue lights and buttons confusing and the directions not appropriate.  Seems better for tea drinkers--settings not clear for coffee drinkers.
It has plastic part inside ...where water touches.

text: Lid stuck shut 9 days too late to return
Body: We had this same model teakettle for several years and liked it enough to choose the same one when the lid stuck shut last month. Now the NEW teakettle is unusable - just 9 days after the "return window" has closed and we are unable to return it. Unacceptable!
I use my kettles daily and the one it replaced had lasted about 4 years. This one was dead before even six months of use.

text: Kettle leaked at the first use
Body: Brand new kettle leaked right out of the box on the first heating try

text: Very Low-Quality, Starts to Fall Apart Quickly
Body: The release latch to open the top quickly broke on me, and same for the replacement unit I foolishly bought.The number/tea style labels quickly rub off leaving you with blank buttons.Totally unimpressed with the build quality, I had two units have the same issues that left me with a broken device.My last Cuisinart item.
It stopped working 2 months later.Absolute junk.
6 months into getting this kettle it won’t work any more

text: It’s great when it is working .  .  .
Body: I do love this kettle so you may wonder why I’m giving it only two stars.  Here’s why.  My first kettle was a gift.  It was something I didn’t know I needed, and now could not do without.  I really loved it.  However, after two years, the handle began to leak at the bottom.  Cuisinart replaced the kettle.  Two years and four months later, the replacement began to leak at the handle’s bottom - again.  Assuming there would be no warranty on the replacement, I bought a new kettle.  It’s been only a few days since it arrived, and the top of this kettle sticks when you press the button to open it to fill it with water.  Sometimes, it is so stuck that I must pry it open with a tool.  I may try to get a warranty replacement this time, too, or I may just give up.  It’s a great kettle when it’s working properly, but by now, I’m just discouraged.

Why two stars? “Keep warm “ is the default setting. This makes no sense. If you don’t remember to turn “keep warm” off it overheats. Also , if you remove it from the stand before it reaches the desired temperature and then replace it on the stand it continues to heat. If you have emptied the kettle it overheats.What I like: the water heats quickly. It’s all metal. The temperature settings are very convenient.This would have been five stars but the counterintuitive non- shutoff situation is ridiculous and unsafe. I expect better from cuisinart.
This is a beautiful tea kettle and does heat the water. The problem is the outside of it is extremely hot. I have grandchildren here often and for me this is dangerousness
Unit is very heavy and difficult to fill Because of small hinged lid.Units on water level gauge are in liters, not ounces.I’ll return and look for another one around town.
Very disappointed with the quality of this product. We used it only for a month before it started leaking water. We liked the different temperature features but when it leaks it is useless.

So temperature control and keep warm are all good and more handy than i expected. What i did not expect is that why pouring out the hot  water - when it comes to last cup of it - the water start spilling around the faucet in two streams and go right on the counter and get sprayed around - which of course is annoying and dangerous. you always have to keep more water when you may need, and that makes kettle heavier that you may want. certainly will not buy again.
Loved this electric kettle until it started leaking from the bottom. Only had it one month before it leaked so sent it back.

For the most part I like this kettle but I am very surprised a reputable company would take the safety risk by putting it on the market.  At first I didn’t realize how extremely hot the outside gets and stays hot a loooong time. I expected it to be well insulated like most everything in this category today.  Even knowing how hot it gets I accidentally brushed against it with my hand and wow what a surprise. I will never use this with grandkids around just because it’s that dangerous and no one would expect this to be hot. Would not have purchased had I realized this and do not recommend it.

text: Worked great until it started leaking
Body: I bought this teapot less than 2 years ago. It worked great, until this morning I discovered that it is leaking. I think for this price the teapot should last  longer. We took good care of it, and really liked it - but now I will find another model for a replacement. Sorry, Cuisinart - I expected more from you.

This kettle defaults to having "keep warm" mode on, and due to bad design it's quite difficult to know if the mode is on or not. Result is you pour out the water, put the kettle back, it turns on again and then fries the bottom before flippng itself off and buzzing. This also happens if you have "keep warm" mode off but you pour the water before the beep (even if it's already boiling). Put it back empty and it's on and frying.I would not get this kettle again.

text: Great Kettle-easy to use and customer service excellent! But second one blew
Body: 1/13/24: Well the new replacement lasted two weeks. It did the same thing the first one did--I emptied it out, put it on the base, hesitated for ONE SECOND and heard a click, and blue lights started flashing and it is no longer usable. Will not stop blinking and flashing. So I am done with this one. Really sad too because I liked the presets. I drink a lot of different kinds of tea so it was so easy to use. Even if they gave me a new one replacement (which I don't know if they would), I would not take it. I need a kettle that won't blow on me after a two weeks.We really like this kettle. We have had other ones (different brands) that didn't last. The day before Christmas Eve, this one, went haywire on us, all lights blinking and it wouldn't work at all.. Naturally this happens after I had replaced my automatic coffee maker with a Large French press that I was planning to use with the convenient boiled water I would get from this kettle. ! I called customer service at Cuisinart and did not expect them to be helpful. I was pleasantly surprised to learn that I was just within the warranty replacement window (I think it's 90 days), so they sent me a new one. A brand new one arrived New Year's Eve! Kettle is great for making all kinds of tea and boiled water for coffee or anything else you want it for. I drink a lot of Asian teas and there are very convenient settings for white, green, black, and oolong. Highly recommended.!

text: About the dumbest kettle design imaginable
Body: 1. The keep warm function. Why have this in an uninsulated device. It remains set even when you turn off the device and it will boil down to nothing eventually. At least do not put it RIGHT next to the start button, insuring someone will accidentally hit it. If you have children or inattentive adults using this kettle, assume that it will just always be on keep warm, and that you have a perpetual fire hazard.2. Why is there a separate start button? Each temp button should just start boiling up to that temp. How many times have I “boiled” my water only to drink luke-warm tea and realize someone else had set the temp to 160. I use this thing 5+ times a day. I don’t remember to check the temp EVERY TIME.It works, so it’s not 1 star, but I’m replacing it and giving this one away. Dumb dumb dumb—and I mean DUMB—industrial design.

Broke after only few uses over the span of several years. We've used other brand for many years and decided to purchase this one as an add-on when we want to prepare different teas at the same time. For a short time it worked, it worked fine. One day it just stopped heating water with three beeps every time the start button is pressed and subsequent disconnect. Do not recommend.

I have used this for over a year but am still fearful for the keep warm button. It is right next to the on buttons and I have found that sometimes the kettle stays on without my knowledge. I’m afraid that it may cause a problem one day.

text: Loved this Kettle until it stopped working
Body: I purchased this kettle almost 3 years ago. I used it several times a day for tea and just boiling water.  It came with a 3 year warranty, and thank goodness it did.  I am on my 3rd kettle and the current one just stopped working.  I loved this kettle while it was working and love the Cuisinart brand over all.  It heat up quickly and the temperature is accurate.  I am frustrated that each kettle lasted less than a year before it stops working.  Just wish it lasted longer.

text: Barely a year and this is already malfunctioning.
Body: After the kettle is emptied and returned to base, it will turn itself on — makes clicks and beeps until it is removed from base. I can’t leave it on the base unless there is water inside the kettle.  Seems like fire hazard.

text: Very difficult to clean, and you have to make sure to turn off
Body: Very difficult to clean . You Need to  remember to turn off every time you use

Don't get this kettle if you want a quiet kitchen.It BEEPS whenever you push a button, and continues to beep when the kettle comes to temperature.I have spoken to customer service, and there is NO way to shut the beeps up!Just Awful

Worked great at first, and the temperature control is wonderful.But now it turns off right after it boils, doesn’t stay warm. My less expensive kettle that I bought years before this is able to stay warm.

text: Surface of kettle gets very hot to the touch and will burn you!
Body: Kettle is loud, heavy and the outside gets very very hot. And it's too expensive.

The main problem is the built-in strainer. You can't remove all of it, and it breaks up the water when you're pouring, so it comes out in multiple streams, in a wide pattern. This makes it impossible to pour water into something with a narrow opening. Also, it bugged me that the power switch is labeled "On," but it's also what you push to turn it off. Finally, the outside gets very hot.

text: Well built kettle but with design issues
Body: This Cuisinart kettle is solidly built and operates fine, but I'm giving it only 2 stars because of several design issues:Operationally, the lack of a temperature display/thermometer combined with no low 105F or 110F preset greatly impedes the versatility of this kettle.  It seems solely designed for coffee and tea making but not for general water heating for uses like starting yeast and such.From a safety perspective, when you take the kettle off the base before it automatically shuts off and you put it back on base, it resumes heating!  You have to press the start button again to stop it from heating.  It may have a overheating safety shutoff, but this is a terrible design aspect and seems really dangerous.The other thing I'd fault the kettle for that its top opening is vary narrow and has a lip that makes it impossible to completely empty without vigorous shaking.  Without being able to easily empty excess water, scale builds up faster than in other kettles which can be easily and completely emptied.Lastly and perhaps only a minor nit, the fill tube water gauge isn't very accurate and doesn't fill smoothly as the kettle fills.

text: Hard to clean, difficult to fill and pour water.
Body: The opening to fill the kettle with water is very small and consequently makes it hard to get a hand in to clean the appliance. Even if the water poured out with more control than the 20$ Walmart electric kettle I got 4 yrs ago, I wouldn't like it. Used twice, works perfectly according to the manufacturer but functionally it is junk. I bought it of Wirecutter's recommendation and supremely disappointed.
It did not keep the water hot very long at all.

text: Does its job with annoying drawbacks.
Body: Have only had this a week so here are my first impressions.- I was excited to see it was stainless steel inside and not plastic.- Seems well made- All the buttons and water area are lit by blue LED lights….that seems unnecessary.- The thing beeps….a lot. Beeping to acknowledge buttons pushed as though the LEDs aren’t enough and beeping when boiling finishes. Not single beeps…loud, repetitive beeps. Unnecessary.- Otherwise boils fast.- Narrow opening for accessing the boiling chamber if you like to clean that zone. Outside is easily wiped down if you like to clean that zone.

text: Rust inside kettle after long use
Body: I bought this product in 2019 and it has worked very well. However, there are two issues that lower my rating to 3 stars.  First, the opening at the top is small and the lid doesn’t open all the way making it very difficult to get my hand inside to clean. Second, I realize I bought 6 years ago, but being stainless steel it should never rust, yet the bottom of the kettle has two rust spots that I noticed just recently. The product is out of warranty so I can’t exchange it, but it has performed well overall.  Doesn’t anyone make a “lifelong” product anymore?!
This failed too quickly - first the lid came off and then it started dripping on the base despite not being overfilled. Very disappointing
Bought this for my brother.He thoroughly enjoys it¡!

text: Discontinued model sent in current model box! Pour may drip and splash.
Body: Product is fine, though when pouring out 1 Liter of boiling water, the flow from the spout is not great.  If one tries to pour it out quickly (i.e. tilt the kettle too much) the flow can go over the 'splash guard' and splash beyond the vessel.  The top is also pretty narrow (3 inch diameter) so filling with water is a bit of a bother.  Also, be aware of the model number.  I did not know that the CPK-17(D1) was discontinued but that's what I received (bottom of kettle says CPK-17(D1) but box it came in says CPK-17P1).  So, when registering the product on the cuisinart website, that specific model was not available in the drop down.  The latest model is the CPK-17P1.

I really liked this electric kettle, especially the feature that lets you keep water hot. Unfortunately, after 2 years of daily use, this feature is no longer working (or I should say I am unable to turn it off). I now have to keep the kettle off the base after use or else it will continually heat up, which is a bit of a safety concern. Looking for another brand now.

text: Worked great for 2 years, and then died
Body: We use this every day. Most people do. It worked for only 2 years?! I am going to look into what brands the Brits use.

text: This kettle has a design flaw that can make a big mess on your counter
Body: Just below the pour spot is a protrusion on plastic of about 5/8" that blocks water from leaving the pot when there is about 1 to 1/2 cups of water left. when you tip the pot too pour the water backs up behind this piece of plastic until you tip the pot way up which then cause a bunch of water to rush out onto the counter. It works as advertised but I would not buy this again.

text: Fast build up of limescale and text on button wore off. Not great for pour over coffee.
Body: Unable to pour slowly for pour over coffee, get a bonavita instead.Built up limscale on lid and bottom which was impossible to get off. Temperature settings wore off on buttons after about a year. Not idea.

This was actually a really great kettle... for eleven months. Then it became convinced that it was empty no matter what the water level was, and the 'boil dry' protection function began kicking in. Sometimes after it was almost boiling, and other times after it operates for a few seconds. It now does it all the time and I am shopping for a competitor product.Very disappointing, because, as I said, for eleven months it was the best electric kettle I ever owned. And I have a lot of other cuisinart products which I am happy with, although they don't get the multiple uses per day of an electric kettle.

1/ The first one leaked from the bottom. Got a quick replacement.2/ The lid on the newest  one doesn’t open easily.3/ It is difficult to figure out the max fill level because of the position of the fill indicator window and no visible marking inside the kettle.Otherwise, boils in a reasonable amount of time. I like the different temp presets. The kettle is attractive.
This is CPK - 17 model which is discontinued by Cusinart. The latest model is CPK-17P1
The kettle did great until it started leaking after less than a year and a half of usage. This is not Accor a $100 water kettle!

text: Filter design is poor, too much plastic being heated
Body: Some design flaws with this kettle. It doesn't pour well at all with the filter; water gets caught on a plastic lip on the inside and comes out at the sides if pouring even slightly fast or to empty it. Not comfortable with the amount of plastic in contact with the boiling water. The water level gauge by the handle seemed a little detached at the top and would get foggy/water droplets clinging to inside top of it and I barely used it. Easier just to open the lid real quick to check water level. All that said, it successfully boiled water at varying temps. I ended up returning it for something else though.

After all the glowing reviews of it in the media, we thought we'd try it but it's only marginally better than our last bare bones one button kettle and it takes a longer time boiling water. Not to mention, we do see spots on the bottom once a week which means it needs vinegar to clean it and we didn't expect that kind of maintenance.

I bought this as a replacement for my favorite Cuisinart that has been discontinued.  Why I don't know - it was perfect.  All of the features work as advertised.  However, this kettle is very heavy and difficult to pick up when full.  I only use it to boil water, so I have to remember to click off the reheat function.  Otherwise I am wasting electricity.  It also feels like it takes about a minute longer than the previous kettle to boil water.  It could be because the element is not exposed directly to the water.  This may prevent scaling in the long run.  I end up just heating a liter at a time if I am in a hurry to make coffee.  I'll be looking for a lighter kettle and would not purchase again.
We use our electric kettle multiple times a day, however it recently started leaking all over the place. I don't think I would get another Cuisinart.

This kettle is probably great if you don't mind the features our previous (Frigidaire- no longer available) kettle had that we miss. First- we want to see the temperature in the kettle in real time. I use it for hot water bottles, mixing pet food, and many other applications for which it doesn't need to be at a specific temperature, but for which I want to know what the temp is RIGHT NOW. It seems that is not a common feature in kettles today. Madness!Secondly, the pour: you either get a little trickle (what you want for tea, I guess), or a great gush if you tilt the kettle more. Neither serve the purposes for which we use our hot water.Finally: the kettle does not turn off once you have used it for the reason you heated the water. It goes right back to reheating it. No thanks! I will tell you to do that if I want you to (and this is with the keep warm button off!).The world does not need hundreds of kettles specifically made for tea. The perfect kettle would show the water level and the temperature in real time, and let me set the temperature I want in small increments.

text: Rusty and giving out after 3.5 years
Body: Did well  with this electric kettle for 3.5 years, averaging 1-2 uses per day. Now it’s rusting at the bottom of the water chamber (stainless steel??), and I set it to boil and the temperature never gets above 200F before it beeps. Time to move on. Don’t think I’ll buy another.
This kettle lasted only 8 months
Glitchy, then 6 months, complete failure.  For $80 maybe a year?

text: The exterior gets very hot, not insulated.
Body: We purchased this kettel to replace a Krups kettle that just failed after 4 years. The only thing we were missing in the Krups was a water level indicator. It had everything above this one as it was insulated,  had unlimited temperature settings and a readout that told you the temperature as it was climbing to your final selection. I will miss it and now my wife wants me to find something similar. Unfortunately I threw out the packaging and doubt if I can return it.
‘Keep hot’ button is annoying. It gets accidentally pressed all the time.It gets rusty looking deposits at the bottom.Top opening is too small to clean inside the pot.

Heats up water very quickly, but released quite a lot of steam, so be careful around that. Also has plastic near the spout, but it’s BPA free so it shouldn’t be much of an issue. It also gets fingerprint stains and marks rather quickly

A good kettle overall... Until it starts leaking. Had two of them, both had the same issue. One day, maybe in a year, maybe in a few, you wake up and the water is outside when it should have stayed inside. And you have to buy a new kettle.Another issue is, the paint on the fancy buttons eventually comes off, and you have to remember what to press. But the good news is, it may start leaking before that, so you'll have to throw it away with the paint still intact.

text: No saber si los plásticos que usa son pfa free
Body: Me gusta es un buen equipo, es rápido, pero para mi la seguridad en términos de liberación de sustancias que tengan cancerígenos como los plásticos que tiene la jarra pues me parece muy importante, creo q por el costo no debería llevar plástico..debería se más metálica y si los lleva debería llevar la claridad de si es no plástico free..el que no lo diga me hace pensar q si los tiene..y eso la pone a la altura de otras muuuchas veces más baratas

text: lights do not reset occassionally and have to boil water; just get blinking lights
Body: lights for all choices start blinking and there is no way to start heating water; has happened frequently and is inconvenient to have to use a backup method for coffee or tea.
I am so happy about this product!  Everything seems fine but it is louder when heating than expected.  That is my only complaint so far.

text: Lid breaks fast making the kettle unusable
Body: Update: apparently this issue is covered by Cuisinart warranty (within 3 years and with proof of purchase) and they were very helpful when reached out, so improving rating from 2 stars to 4Original review:I loved this kettle, but it has issue with lid structure that breaks rather quickly - first it stops popping easily, and eventually it stops opening altogether.  It is old known issue - quick google search brings a lot of comments and suggestions about this, so not sure why it was not yet fixed by manufacturer. It is my second Cuisinart kettle that have same issue (first broke after 2.5 years, second 1.5 year), and this will be the last one. Moving on to something more reliable.

It does the job. Keep warm feature would be more useful if it auto turned off, once you lift the kettle from the base and return it. Obviously, you have poured the water from the kettle at that point.
I had two of these Cuisinart Kettles.  Both died winin two years.

After doing some traveling, I realized that a simple electric tea kettle was an obvious answer to the continual problem of never having the correct water temperature for my tea at work. Microwave it, walk away, come back it's cold, start the microwave again, now it's too hot. This Cuisinart tea kettle will hold the correct temperature to brew green or black teas to perfection. It's perfect.The only problem is that $100 feels over the top.

This thing will literally boils water in 2-3 minutes. Very nice product. The only downside is the stainless exterior gets hot enough to burn you if you are not careful. It has a great handle which stays cool but if you accidentally touch the exterior you can get burnt.

This kettle replaced an older, much more basic, plastic kettle.  The older plastic kettle actually heats water faster.  I timed them with the same amount of water in each because I thought this one seemed slow, and it is noticeably slower.  However, the features of this are nice.  It’s insulated so the water stays hot longer.  The different temperature settings are nice for different types of tea or drinks.  One slight annoyance is the “keep warm” function stays on by default, so if you don’t want it to keep coming on to reheat any water still left inside after you pour water for your cup of tea, you have to disable that every time you use the kettle.  That can be an energy waster if you forget to turn it off each time.

text: Easy to use. Heats up fast. Sturdy.
Body: It’s a bit heavy, seems well-made. Easy to use and clean. Nice looking, easy to read and use with options specific to various types of tea. Pricey, but if it lasts years, it’s worth it. If it only lasts a year or two I will be disappointed 😔. Brand reputation doesn’t mean much nowadays since companies are being bought out for their reputation by groups that have no conscience, they trash the brand then move on to break more things, or is it disrupt… anyway I hope this pricey purchase lasts and continues to perform well.

text: Sleek and attractive, heats water fast
Body: Nice upgrade from our old kettle which had begun to leak. This is attractive and heats fast.One caution though- the ‘keep warm’ button is so close to the start button that it almost always gets put on simultaneously - have to remember to shut it off manually otherwise kettle stays on in keep warm mode.
It works as expected, boils in seven minutes and stays warm if left on. I use it for tea in place of my microwave.

text: Great kettle, a little awkward to fill
Body: Quick to heat. Like the presets. Looks good in the kitchen. Didn’t give it a 5 because the lid doesn’t open all the way so it was awkward to fill. They stress not over filling, but it is hard to hold it under the faucet and watch the fill lines. We have a farm Hise sink, so the faucet is an extending type. I can work around it.

I'm a bit cautious as I've noticed that the life of kettles like this can sometimes turn out to be unexpectedly short. So far so good though.The water heats up quickly and the sound signal is very convenient.The only slight drawback is that when you add water, it is a little difficult to monitor the water level. Maybe it just takes some getting used to.

text: Very hot to touch but great overall product
Body: The kettle appears to work well, i was able to make tea after the first boil/rinse and there was no weird smell or taste. Boils in around 7 minutes when full and beps to let you know it's done. Outside of the kettle gets VERY hot but the handle stays cool. It doesn't slide on the counter which is how i found out it was hot, trying to move it back under the overhead cupboard. Led color is blue and it's very quiet when boiling.

This electric kettle works well, has great features, and looks attractive. But unlike every other stainless-steel-looking coffee related carafe in our house, this one gets hot on the exterior. I wish it were insulated. That would be more safe and probably use less electricity. Yes, I would buy it again.
This works great but you have to be really careful cause the outside also gets super hot.

I had a glass Hamilton Beach tea kettle prior to this Cuisinart.  This takes much longer to heat the water and I accidentally brushed the side of the kettle and SO SO HOT.  Poor design bc that was not an issue with the Hamilton Beach.

text: Works well. Looks good. Heavy and single walled.
Body: I like how well  this Cuisinart PerfecTemp tea kettle works. Boils water quickly and for various types of tea and French press there are different temps from which to choose.The tea kettle, however, is very heavy when filled with water and even without water, so I need to hold the handle and the bottom of the kettle to pour. It’s also too hot on the outside to hold on the side. I’m guessing this is because it’s single walled. I’m comparing it to my last electric tea kettle which was a  Brevile Variable Temp. It lasted 10 years and was pricier than this Cuisinart. It was not as heavy and when water was hot, I could still touch the outside of the pot if need be.  This being said, I’m still enjoying this Cuisinart kettle and am keeping it.I gave this pot 4 stars because of the heavier weight otherwise it would be 5 stars.

text: It makes loudish beeps when water is ready. Another sound would be better. Or at least fewer beeps.
Body: It makes loudish beeps when water is ready. Some other sound would be better. Or at least fewer beeps. Otherwise, it's a good product.Is anyone reading this review?Just read on NY Times that Amazon lets some sellers buy (presumably) favorable reviews for their products. Thereby making Amazon's review and rating system biased and often useless.

It heats water to a boil in 2 minutes, I timed it.  Fantastic appliance.  Now for the down side, it gets very hot to the touch and it’s heavier than I thought it would be.  But, I like it and will find it very useful.  I will work with the cons, as the pros outweighs the unit.  Very attractive and well made.

Best kitchen appliance purchased. Got tired boiling water in a sauce pan or microwave.  Best thing is the selection of the temperature of the water you desire.  The speed to heat up boggles the mind.  Construction is metal and sturdy

text: Great for tea and French press
Body: Was recommended by a friend, and it was a really good pick
Purchased in 2020. Keeps on working!

We purchased this 10 years ago, and it ran perfectly for that whole time, until the auto shutoff failed.  We were so pleased with it that we bought another one!The buttons to set the desired temp are particularly convenient, since we drink a variety of teas.

Very happy with this purchase! Heats up so fast and exactly the temp I need for coffee or tea! With my stovetop kettle, I'd often have to let the water cool a bit from boiling so that it didn't splatter while pouring. The keep warm function is nice if I start the water and leave the room for a bit. It's ready to go when I need it. Looks nice, too!
Boiling water fast and it looks beautiful on the counter.

I bought one of these for my wife probably five or six years ago, and it just started leaking. So, I bought the same model again since between her, her mom and her sister, the thing gets used probably 10 times a day, every day, and the only thing that broke on it is the plastic water level sight glass. Just plain wore out after several thousand heat cycles.Through the magic of having two of them, I felt fine taking apart the old one to see how it’s built. Short version? Really, really well.The power supply and heater switching is located in the base, while the microcontroller and beeper are up in the handle. It looks like the handle electronics at least could take a pretty good splash without being compromised, though the base certainly isn’t waterproof and if you immersed this thing it would be ruined.Everything appears to be stainless steel and except for some minor discoloration on the interior bottom, there never was any rust. I did find a couple standard steel screws and captured nuts in the handle area that showed signs of rust, and this was directly below where the sight glass leaked, so that makes sense. Still, would’ve been nice if the fasteners were stainless as well.Overall, build quality is top-notch for the price point and I feel really good about the expected lifespan of the replacement unit. Don’t change anything, Cuisinart!

I made the switch from a classic stove top kettle to electric with this one and I have had this now for 3 years and it still works and stays great. For me going from a stove top kettle to elector I find this to be pretty fast.I have never had any rust and I clean the mineral buildup easily once a week with a little boiled vinegar.  No special cleaners are needed. I empty it out every night and leave the top open so it fully air dries.I use this kettle 3 times a day at minimum. Anyone complaining about rust or minerals with this kettle is not emptying it out or treating/cleaning it properly. Also, sidenote, there's been a few times that I have accidentally left water in it overnight and it is fine.I also polish the outside of it from time to time with a little Bon Ami or Barkeeper's friend (Scrub daddy power paste would be ok too)If you take good care of this kettle, it'll take good care of you.
Was very happy to get this kettle. Looks nice in your kitchen & easy to use.
Best product for your money. Second kettle of this exact brand and style. Good for younger kids and those that forget about heating water! Highly recommend.

10/10 I didn't  know that it has a keep-warm for 30 minutes option and I love it. I also love the different temperature options for different types of teas and French Press. I would absolutely recommend it

The title says it all. I used this multiple times a day, every day, for 9 years until it finally broke (the lid won't open).The buttons all survived with mostly legible writing, and it heats up fast and to the perfect temperature every time.I will definitely buy a second to replace the first.

I have had the Cuisinart 1.7-Liter Stainless Steel Cordless Electric Kettle for 7 months and use it EVERY DAY for coffee, plus green tea, Jamaica/Hibiscus tea, properly dried Moringa leaves, and other teas which need a lower temperature than black tea. I use only distilled water in it so there is no white mineral buildup inside the pot. It has been worth every penny to me. Water heats quickly so boiling kettle gets left on the stove. It would make a great present.

I absolutely love this kettle. The preset temperatures are to die for and the speed is amazing. I will have even boiling water in less than 10 minutes. Plus, when I finish my cup of tea I can leave the water on warm and come back for more.

Replaced our first after less than a year but probably our fault for over filling it and  we liked it so well we replaced it and have been telling others not to overfill it as it caused small bits of plastic to settle in the water to
It heats water fast. Has different temperature settings for the kind of tea you are making. It holds the temperature for awhile after it heats up.

text: Good initially, but slow leak over time making it too dangerous
Body: Pros: This kettle is attractive, holds a lot of water, and heats nicely.Cons:- Particularly heavy when full due to stainless steel weight.- You have to always press the keep warm button to turn off reheating (it's the default to reheat)- Biggest problem is that ours has developed a slow leak over time. It's a design flaw. I thought it was just condensation, and you can see in the photo how I tried to clean the water calcification and the lettering came off. The bottom of the handle has a screw that penetrates the inside chamber of the kettle. Inside the kettle you can see the plastic cover over the screw where it attaches. Water from this weak point travels from the inside to the outside and drips down and collects underneath the heating element as it sits on our counter. This started gradually and initially the small amount of water probably just evaporated--but then it got more noticeable. To be clear, I have never seen water between the kettle and the base--but it has collected underneath the base. This is too dangerous a shock risk.I wrote Cuisinart via email and they were responsive, but since it's out of warranty (over 3 years old) they only offered a % discount on a new one. I'm not sure if the 2023 versions are built the same way, but I'll be looking for a replacement elsewhere.

text: The inside material chips off in 2-3 months, so unfortunate
Body: I thought cuisine art was a higher quality name brand so would be safer to order than some of these random companies but I was wrong, the inside of the pot corroded in less than 3 months and the sad thing is that I used it daily, and didn’t notice until I went out of town and retuned and decided to give it a look.I hope those paint chips aren’t poisonous because good chance i consumed some.It worked well, if you don’t mind the inside corroding into your beverages

text: Lid busted off and now the whole thing is garbage.
Body: It worked great till I spit out a little black plastic thing while drinking tea. I eventually figured out that little piece was holding the lid in place.  I could have easily swallowed the damn thing. Also, the kettle is now garbage now the lid does not go down. It looks fancy but the quality is not.

The product looks good. That's about it. Has flaws. Much too heavy with water in it, especially when full. Base is too light and flimsy. The preset temperatures aren't accurate. They run low. For example, preset temp of 175 degrees for green tea measured only 170 with a thermometer I stuck into the kettle. For boiling water measured only 207 degrees instead of 212. I tried various other tea temps and all were off. In addition, the various preset temps for tea aren't necessary. After experimenting, I found it's best to just the boil the water and then wait a short while and pour it over a tea bag. Also, you can't get rid of all the water in the kettle by pouring it out. Some stays in the bottom and has to evaporate. Could eventually cause calcification or rust. In addition, the price is too high except when on sale. Not a good value for the money. The start button is also the off button, but is only marked as start. Boil speed is five minutes for one liter and seven minutes for 1.7 liter. Seems long. Would be difficult to clean inside due to small opening at the top. You can't fit your hand in there. To close the top have to push it with your hand. Not a good idea if the kettle is hot. The kettle's outside is very hot and thus can be dangerous. Also, the beep doesn't work when the water is hot. Or maybe it's so soft I don't hear it. So, the kettle has some flaws. The idea is good, but needs an updated design. I might return it and go back to a stove top kettle. UPDATE: I kept it. Increased rating to two stars.

text: INEVITABLE WATER STAINS IMPOSSIBLE TO REMOVE; WATER LEVELS CANNOT BE SEEN UNDER HANDLE
Body: Despite using several kinds of stainless wipes and finally resorting to Simichrome polish, these water stains are still visible.  I've had the kettle for a week. Another issue is that the water level is invisible when filling, as it's virtually hidden under the handle--the nice blue light can't be on then, so what's the point??  Also, the unit must be unplugged after each use—apparently to preserve that fancy but completely useless blue light. Poor design, poor execution.  Thanks for nothing, Wirecutter and all those other online review sites that apparently didn’t actually use this kettle.

text: Decent kettle; the pour is atrocious
Body: I've had my kettle for a few months now. The temperature settings are convenient, but the pour on this thing is the worst I've ever seen. Because of the shape of the mouth of the kettle, and the shape of the filter inside near the mouth, when you pour the water it always comes out in 1 or 2 main streams, with 1 or 2 *additional* streams coming out at odd angles near the top of the mouth. It's bonkers how bad the pour is.

text: Ink on button fades fast--illegible after a few years
Body: Works great but lettering on buttons faded after a year.  We have had it 3 years and can barely read the buttons.  I called Cuisinart and they won't replace it. A shame they chose to use such shoddy ink for the buttons.

I really really wanted to love this kettle, my husband spent hours looking for the perfect gift and bought me this and I loved it... until we realized the water we have is not compatible. We get our water locally from a spring with extremely high magnesium content and it turns the water into a mess of white clouds when boiled in stainless steel. It does not react that way in glass though. Bummer, I think it would have been wonderful otherwise!

text: You will see rust occur inside on the bottom plate. Cuisinart will dismiss it.
Body: See the ring of rust in the photo. Cuisinart dismisses the fact that their kettle rusts.  Customer services told me to get some Bartender's friend or Bon Ami. and scrub it. Nice drinking that. And it's very difficult to get a sponge brush in down to the base. But seriously this kettle should not rust the price it sells for. Yes I understand hard water but this is greatly disappointing. And when you contact customer service they act like all kettles rust. Again hard water but not rust near the screws that you can see when you look inside at the bottom of the base.
Seriously worked so fast! Love the lights behind the buttons - makes it look so high tech! Super easy to use and I love how fast it boils a big thing of water.
You can burn your skin when not careful. Only grab by the handle and never touch the main body.
Worked fine the first year.  Now the water is barely tepid.

I received this kettle as a Christmas gift and am sad that I did, because I don't have the replacement plan. After four months the kettle would randomly shut off without completing a heating cycle, and will go hours without turning on again. We tried cleaning the connectors but everything looks fine; sometimes it'll turn on when you set it on the base and sometimes it doesn't. It worked wonderfully at first, but for something this expensive to break less than a year after purchase with pnly a 30 day guarantee is absolutely unacceptable.

I Have one of these for a little over 1 year. It has started to leak. I'm an electrical engineer, so I took it apart to see what happened, maybe fix it. No go. The metal section that sits inside over to the electrical components leaks, even posing an electrical short circuit problem and fire. The gasket section or connection point wears out. Let it sit and the counter top is covered with water. Plus; the push button top breaks and will not open. You have to use a knife blade to open it. The lettering wears off too. Sad, I really liked this unit, with its multiple temperature settings. But, it's a POS construction killed it for me. Buy, something else, as this unit poses a direct fire or shock hazard to you and your family.

This review is for the Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp Cordless Electric KettleThe darn thing rusted after a couple of months! It started with a tiny rust stain in the bottom of the pot interior and within a few weeks more rust spots appeared in there. I only use Reverse Osmosis water in the thing and haven't used it more than a couple of dozen times.The opening isn't big enough to fit my hand in there to clean it. In fact, the opening is small and the lid doesn't open all the way. That makes it awkward to fill.Another thing I don't like: There are plastic parts in the interior that touch the water - a screen (removable) and also the water gauge (not removable).Otherwise, the kettle is lovely. It looks good, it has easy, clear controls, and it heats the water quickly to whichever temperature you choose. If you make tea or need water at specific temperatures, this is a great kettle because it lets you specify the temperature.Since mine is rusted, I'm going to ditch it and buy a Cosori stainless steel kettle at under half the price. It has no plastic touching the water, a large opening and great reviews. Fingers crossed.

So close, but a miss. Why? Who needs 5 irritating beeps once your water is ready? How about a beep anytime you press a button? Then this is the kettle for you. For me, no thanks. But, surely there's a way for users to customize this? Nope. Listen up designers and engineers, empower consumers to choose the amount and degree of notifications they receive from their tools in their everyday life. It's really not that hard.

text: Mine is 4 years old and it still works great, but needs more frequent descaling
Body: My previous electric hot water kettle was a Breville Ikon (which I still have, kept as a backup). I started using the Cusinart CPK-17 because of the temperature control. It's not very precise to the settings, but it's close enough.What I don't like about it:1. The opening is too small! I cannot fit my hand inside to clean... so I need to use a brush implement. It's not a really big deal, but just 0.5" wider would've been about right.2. The warming feature is very useful, but I'd prefer if it was off by default. There is a button that lights up when you press START, so you can deactivate it. But most people aren't aware of this.3. As it ages, it needs to be descaled more frequently.4. The latest prices! I bought mine for $50 shipped 4 years ago. Today? The same model is now over $110! That's ludicrous.What I like about it:1. It's fast! It's just a little faster than my older Breville.2. While temperature settings aren't terribly accurate, they're good enough and it's nice to have at least some control over the water temperature.3. The weight is OK for the brushed steel version. I don't know why people are complaining about it.4. It's reliable and has a good base contact (my Breville Ikon required cleaning of corrosion on the contacts periodically--not necessary on the Cuisinart).

I was lifted this electric tea pot a few years ago. I love this pot. I find it very useful for any of my hot water needs. I use it to rebuild water for cooking it is faster and convenient than cooking on my stove. The vessel has maintained its look. I love that there are different temperature settings. It's very durable and looks nice in my kitchen.  I highly recommend this product

We purchased this Cuisinart (CPK17P1) to replace our 12 year old Cuisinart (CPK17) - Serial Number 00224 (yes we had this one for a long time) which worked perfectly well for many (many) years.  We love that it lets us pick just the correct temperature for each type of tea we drink.

This thing is a beast. I've had it going on four years now and it takes anything I can throw at it. I haven't really done a great job of maintaining it, but it still works as good as new. I love the different temperature settings and everything from the lights to the buttons still work. I would recommend this to anyone.

We bought this in December of 2010 and 14 years later it is still working. This has warmed up water for tea, ramen and a myriad of other things over the years and it works every single time. At the time we paid $44 for this. Without a doubt this is probably on our top 100 for best purchases ever and we buy a ton of stuff. Yes, I know consumerism is a disease, its okay we don't have a problem, we can stop when we want to.

Let me say upfront that the product works to heat the water at the various temperatures. I am taking it on faith that the temperature is correct. And the controls are easy to use.Why I have rated it so poorly has to do with form. First, the balance is wrong. You have to hold the handle in the middle or just slightly above and it is awkward. Because of the control point the handle gets thicker where it meets the body and make it impossible to get my hand in there for the balance to feel right. Perhaps if the kettle is two feet from the sink you might be ok but I have to carry it a long way down the hall at my office where I intended to use this kettle and when full of water you have to hold it with two hands, one hand on the bottom. My home kettle (another brand) does not suffer this imbalance.My second complaint is the lid, it's small. Related to the lid is is the filter tab, it's very large. So combined with the small opening at top and the filter tab the fill area is restricted. Filling from a sink is ok but not ideal. Filling from a jug of water as I intend very soon would be more challenging.The first complaint is why I have chosen to, hopefully, return this one and I have ordered a multi-temp version of the brand which I have at home. If you're young and strong this would be an ok problem I suppose. But if you're older or not a strong in the arms I would definitely avoid it. Even for me with my strength I just find it annoying. Perhaps I am spoiled by, in my opinion, the better design of the kettle I have at home.Generally I would say the Cuisinart, in my somewhat limited experience, makes a pretty good product. It's just that this product is not one of them.

Edit:  Initially I gave this kettle a much higher rating.  It could be wonderful.  Sadly, shoddy craftsmanship has ruined the experience.  The kettle I bought leaks profusely after a year of use.  I recommended it to a friend, and the circuit board on his crapped out six months after he bought it.  This is not at all what I have come to expect of Cuisinart products and my recommendation is now to find a different brand which will actually work for a reasonable amount of time.Original review: I love this water kettle!  I've recently begun drinking green teas and I always get the water too hot and the tea turns out bitter.  The first cup I brewed with this water heater was wonderful.  The keep warm feature is not as useful as I thought it would be, since I generally walk away from the kettle for more than half an hour.  I also don't like the fact that the LED turns on every time you pick it up off the base.  Other than those minor nitpicks, it is great.  There are no funny flavors, the beep to signal that water is hot is loud enough to get my attention but not so loud its obnoxious, and it heats enough water for me and several friends to all have a large cup.  The exterior does get warm as some reviewers have mentioned, but not truly hot.  You might be able to burn yourself if you held your hand against it.  I've brushed the outside with a hand several times and not been hurt.  Also, the handle is perfectly insulated.

This is my first purchase of a Cuisinart kettle. My others worked quite well and lasted for over 3 years. This kettle has a nice array of choosing the right temperature, but most of my usage is to boil, as I make my coffee per cup. Everything works as described, but I gave it only 3 stars. The first concern is that it scales quite badly on the bottom of the kettle. So you have to use Lime-A-Way and vinegar to keep it clean almost weekly.. Even with very little scale on the bottom, it makes a lot of noise when it is boiling. I never had a kettle that scaled up so fast, and I find it to be a nuisance. Another concern is the boiling temp. I really do not believe that it reaches the 112 degree boil like it says it does, as my coffee never quite gets that cream on top from the coffee grinds. I wish they had another version of this in a shorter and a bit fatter size. I think that would cause less scaling in the bottom and probably get to the boiling heat I need. When this fails, I will not purchase another like it.New Add On: As of today 1/21/2013 the kettle has failed after less than a year. The lights all work, but will not heat the water and automatically turns itself off. I am quite disappointed, esp. for a Cuisinart item. Will see about a refund, if they are honest about it!?!New Add On: Cuisinart sent me a new water kettle, but it only lasted 4 days! I was told I could not return for a refund! I will NEVER buy another product like this from them again!

text: works like a cheap water boiler
Body: I've only had this thing a little over 24 hours and it sucks already. When I first try to boil water, nothing happen. I just thought I forgot to press the "start" button. Then today, when I try to boil water again, nothing happens. I had to try it again before it would boil. The "keep warm" button is a joke. Once you take the kettle off the base, it goes off. The only way the "keep warm" will stay on is if you keep it on the base, which is pointless because then you can't use the kettle. The "keep warm" doesn't come back on after you set it back on the base again. It also says that the "keep warm" will keep the set water temperature for 30 minutes. It doesn't. I didn't time it but I left it on "keep warm" and the whole unit shut off after about 5 minutes. There was about .75L of water left in the kettle when it shuts off. It was enough water for me to brew two of my pu er tea on my clay pot. You can buy something half this price and it'll work the same. This kettle is a joke. I am return it.

August 2011 - What a pot!  Boils water so fast.  If you are a tea drinker, this is the perfect pot to boil water to the correct temperature for delicate leaves, which maximizes flavor.  There are different gauges/water temperatures to press on the handle.  The water can reach 175 degrees in something like 2 minutes. I can't say enough about this pot.  It's attractive and easy to use.  A must have for tea drinkers, or for those who want to boil water fast.March 01, 2016 - Update - After 4 1/2 years of using at least 3x per day, this kettle finally died.  I ordered another one and received it yesterday.  I made 4 kettles of water before it stopped working! The buttons would light up but the water would not get hot.  I have the item back in it's box to return to Amazon. I'm chalking it up to getting a lemon.  Now I don't know whether to buy one more to try, or just get another brand. I was fine with the first one lasting 4 1/2 years.  Interestingly, my first one cost $84 and this second one was $96, but when I went to return it today, the price went down to $85!March 17, 2016 - Update - I decided to purchase another.  The way the top opens is different than the last two. It now snaps open quickly and makes a popping noise instead of opening softly.  Even the one I just returned opened softly.  After close examination, the product is definitely not as well made as the first one I bought in 2011.  The window to see the water level is now plastic and opaque versus the old one which was clear and looked like glass.  I have decided to keep it for now and see how long it lasts.  I also purchased The extra 3 year warranty for an additional $6.99.  The kettle went up $4 when I finally decided to buy it ($89 was my purchase price).  So even with the extra warranty it came to the same price of $96 which was the selling price early March.

Maybe it is me, but if I pay this sort of money for a kettle I kinda expect a product that makes me feel great.  I really wanted to like this too (I love tea, and I want to enjoy the process of making tea).  Here are the reasons why I am pleased to be sending it back.1) The kettle comes with a label on it.  Peel off the label and the metal underneath is a different color to the rest of the kettle.  It aint adhesive, it aint coming off!  So for the whole life of the kettle you'll have a big rectangle area on the front that is a different color to the rest of it.2) It is way too heavy for a darn kettle3) The outside gets really hot and it is very easy to burn yourself.4) Too hard to turn on. Seriously, it is a kettle ... the whole 'pick your temp' thing ... i am still not sure if I have to hit start afterwards.  I think not, i think the start button actually stops it. Also, while I am ranting, during the water in the kettle must be different temperatures in different places, I am not sure I fully believe that when I pour the water it really comes out at the temperature it claims.  I'd love to know if anyone tested it (watch your household thermometers, though, they may go pop).5) Too easy to leave on.  First day of usage I kept leaving it on 'keep warm'.  Who wants this feature anyway?  Maybe your tea and drink it, manufacturers ought to be discouraging consumers from wasting the planet's resources by keeping their kettle boiling for half an hour.Two starts because it does look quite nice, it can boil water and I admire them for trying to make it beautiful.

text: Worked Great in First Year and Then Failed :(
Body: I bought this kettle close to a year ago for my parents.  I loved the fact that it was stainless steel on the inside and outside making it easier for cleaning and durability.  I tested it out before passing it to my parents, and I loved it.  Once they started using it, they loved it too.  I like the different temperatures you can program the kettle to heat the water to for different kinds of teas.  It is quite versatile.  My parent are older and it has the feature where it automatically cuts off after it completes the boiling cycle.  However, they called me the other day to tell me that now it keeps boiling and boiling and won't shut off!  One time it boiled all the water off and kept on boiling which is a fire hazard!!  They unplugged it an refuse to use it because of this terrible malfunction.  So I revisited the product's listing on Amazon and read the negative reviews which frequently mention this specific problem and how the product's warranty is lame.  As much as my parents and I liked this kettle so much when it worked, it's sad and disappointing that it only lasted a year.  Just something potential buyers need to be aware of!

text: It's a beautiful kettle and worked great for awhile
Body: I used this kettle for about a year and a half and for the last 6 months it's hardly functional. As a tea lover, I was very excited to have the quick temperature select buttons for different kinds of tea. It's a beautiful kettle and worked great for awhile. Now on occasion when I plug it in it won't tun on. When it does turn on, it will shut off mid boil cycle. Sometimes it will come back on after several minutes, sometimes it won't for far longer. On the rare times it gets to temperature, it sometimes will only beep once and shut off where before it would beep 3 times.
