Even with the keep warm setting off it sometimes will turn itself back on and start boiling so I just keep it unplugged when not in use. I've taken very good care of it. I descale it with vinegar, keep it clean, and baby it, but it didn't matter. Seeing other recent reviews this is a pattern and I hope the Cuisinart takes responsibility for this. They want me to pay shipping both ways to replace it. I may as well put that money towards a competitor's kettle. I'm just angry considering how much I paid for this expecting a higher end product. Oh well, buyer beware.

text: Poor quality build and potentially dangerous
Body: There is 'keep water hot' option - that often turned it self on even when unwanted. Yes, if you notice, you can turn it off, but it is easy to not notice. If you have used much of the water and put the kettle back on its base without noticing, it will come to the boil repeatedly and therefore risk running dry and causing a fire.Also, the lid became stiffer and stiffer after 18 months. To the extent where, at 24 months, it cannot be reliably opened and closed at all and so we are reduced to filling the kettle through the spout.For an expensive kettle, this is not good value.***************Update - I discovered the kettle has a 3 year warranty and Cuisinart have agreed to replace the unit. I will assume that the replacement unit will arrive and have increased my rating to two stars. For the price, the kettle should not have failed at all, and there is still the issue with the unsafe switching to 'keep warm' mode.

When making purchases I include Amazon reviews as a part of the decision and that is why I am writing today.  The Cuisinart CPK-17 was purchased in April of 2016.  Loved it until last weekend when it ceased to work.  Yes,  it came up quite short of working for an entire year, almost three months short of a year.  Called Cuisinart to find out  how strict their the limited warranty was.  Customer service calls (I had to make two calls  since they hung up on me after the first 30 minutes of waiting) took over an hour of waiting to find out that yes, they would send me a new one after I gave them my cc number for the $15.95 handling charge, then I had to send it to NJ and pay the mailing charge. I live in Oregon so who knows how much I would have to spend in shipping cost not to mention more time.  I spent $99.95 for this appliance and it is not worth the return in time and money.

We use the kettle between 4-6 times a day. We have had this kettle for a little less than three years and it has completely broken down.First off, the handle is not terribly comfortable to hold or pour with. The labels wore off the buttons within the first few months. The lid broke after the first year, no longer opening with the push button. Now the lid is held in place with duct tape.About a year ago the kettle would intermittently cut out, reset the temp setting and generally behave erratically.I kind of disliked it from early on because it was awkward to hold and pour, now that it is so unreliable it only works once every other try or so, I am looking forward to getting something simpler and more ergonomic.If you need a variable temp kettle, you may as well buy a cheaper version as you will have to replace this one before too long anyway.

Was looking for a new electric kettle as we drink a lot of tea. Wanted something that is not plastic, bigger (at least 1.5 liter) has a few extra features and looks ok. Did a lot of research and this kettle seemed like a good choice. Had it for 3 months now, works fine.The pros: looks good; stainless steel so no plastic parts come in contact with water; large - up to 1.7L, comes handy  for parties; has several temperature settings that are marked by the type of tea you'd like - black tea, green tea, white tea etc; has a "keep warm" feature.Now for cons: takes a while for water to boil- up to 5-7 min, I had a really cheap kettle before and it took like a minute to boil, with this one it takes long time even for a small amount of water; the "keep warm" function is crazy - it's automatically on all the time and unless you turn it off - it keeps boiling! It probably sounds ridiculous but it's really annoying that every time you pick up the kettle and put it back - you have to press 3 different buttons to turn it off!  Otherwise, the kettle keeps turning itself on and keeps boiling water.Also, recently the kettle stopped turning itself off automatically on "boiling" setting at all! I can get around it and either use a different setting or manually turn it off but for the price - I would expect a bit more reliability!Bottom-line - if you often make different types of tea, including "delicate" and "oolong" and need a larger kettle - this maybe a good purchase for you. If you don't care about settings and just want a quick cup of tea - this is definitely a completely overpriced product.

text: A product I want to love, but feel just kind of "meh" about.
Body: Ahhh where do I begin. I love Cuisinart products and I wanted a stainless steel kettle that would match the rest of my appliances. Before this, I had a Black&Decker kettle that had a digital screen that would tell the temperature, along with presets for different teas. Unfortunately that one was discontinued, so I bought this one and took the old one to to work. I saw this Kettle and loved the design, the reviews were pretty good, so I got it. After about 3 months, all ink on the preset buttons started to rub off. Luckily I remembered most of the buttons temperatures, but if I forget I have to look the product up online and look at the pictures (kind of a pain).Next, the kettle beeps to let you know that the water is ready. A lot of the times the temperature is not right, especially when you select boil. The water clearly isn't boiling, but the beep go's off and the kettle shuts off. For other temperature settings I've taken a meat thermometer to check he temp and it's usually way off. Either too hot, or not hot enough. This became extremely frustrating and I took this kettle to work, and brought the old Black&Decker kettle back home, since I tend to make tea more at home. If you want precise temperature for tea, look for a kettle that has a digital thermometer built into it. I really wanted to like this product, but it's just okay.

First , let me say I've used Russell Hobbs kettles for many years, as they lasted for many years and were known as an excellent product.  However, my latest RH Kettle  died after about  18 months  of use for no apparent reason. It just never turned on again. After reading other reviews it seems the general opinion is that they were once great but not any more.  Which sent me on a search through kettles reading numerous reviews. (thank you, all reviewers!)So far the kettle is great!  Some things I love: a)  The lid opens with a push button so it is no longer a two hand job to fill the kettle. b) There are various settings for different kinds of tea!  how great is that!  These settings include temps for white and green tea, french press coffee and plain old boil.  :) c) There's an optional  "keep warm" button which will keep the water at your selected temperature for 30 minutes and then turn off.  I especially love this as I would leave the room, do something while waiting for the water, it would take longer than expected and I'd always be reheating the water.... (maybe why Russell Hobbs broke??) d) It beeps when ready!  Why don't they all?  It's not a loud, annoying beep but if you're listening for it you will hear it.e) The window reservoir window clearly shows (and measures) how much water you've got in the pot' f)  Yes, it heats quickly.  I rarely fill the kettle to the top and the half kettle that I'm heating seems to take only a minute or two.What I don't love and why I didn't give this 5 stars:a) There;s nothing exceptional about the appearance of the kettle.  Nothing awful, but i could have enjoyed a style with a little pizzazz.b) Not sure if the cord is really going to wind up in the base as tight as I would like  (haven't gotten to this yet).The kettle arrived within 48 hours of being ordered. I rinsed it out, plugged it in and had tea within minutes.  Such a relief to have a HOT cup of tea as I've been using a keurig which doesn't have a real hot setting.I'm pleased with my selection and would encourage others to buy this kettle.  It's not a cheap kettle but the features are great and I'm hoping it will last like the old Russell Hobbs used to.

This is a good electric kettle. However, it is not the best-ever electric kettle. I lived in England for a long time so have had several excellent electric kettles. This is also my second model of the Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp because the first one did stop working within three weeks. However, customer service was good and agreed to send out a replacement which arrived very promptly and has been working every day for over a year. I use mine to make white, green, oolong, black and herbal teas at least twice a day.You do have to read the instructions carefully at the start to figure out how to turn it off/not leave it on the 'warm' function  or how to use the temperature memory function, but after you are used to it you don't think twice.Pros:-Looks good, stylish-Love the blue light-Not heavy when full with water-Takes a decent amount of water at a time-Heats the water pretty quickly-Metal not plastic-Enclosed heating element so you do not have todeal with cleaning the element-Heats it to close to the temperature you choose-Great customer service from CuisinartCons:-My first unit failed and I had to pay a moderate amount to receive the second replacement unit-The water temperatures listed seem a little high, I have to use "oolong" setting for green tea as the "green tea" setting is a bit too hot.-Somewhat pricey, I really feel it should be cheaper.I have found that the boil function is super-hot. The outside of the unit also remains hot so not suitable for those with young children.As there are not that many models of temperature-selection electric kettles on the US market I still gave this four stars because I use it every day and can adjust the heat of the water better than if I had a regular electric kettle and had to wait for the water to cool down. It dresses up the kitchen and is pretty easy to keep clean and in good condition. I just hope it lasts!

text: Bought this solely based on reviews across multiple sites
Body: Needed a new electric kettle as my previous one died and the Cuisinart CPK-17 seemed to be the best rated across different sites. After a week of use, here are my initial thoughts:PROS:The base has a slim profile and takes up little space on the counter;The electrical cord length can be adjusted under the base to avoid extra slack;The water level markers are convenient if you want to fill water to a specific amount without the need to boil more water than necessary, which takes longer;Water boils fairly quickly and accurately based on the taste of my French pressed coffee.CONS:The body of the kettle and lid are not insulated so this gets very hot to touch, which is a big letdown compared to some competitors;Although I was aware there is no digital readout of the water temperature, I found myself missing it when checking the heating progress or even the current water temperature after filling or sitting for a period of time;Wish the opening was bigger to fit my hand inside to hand dry;I'm not a huge fan of the rubber push buttons but that may not matter to some people. Although they work completely fine right now, my experience has shown that these types of buttons require more force over time and that the printing will wear out.I won't list it as a con since it's my fault, but the kettle did fall off my counter after I propped it up to dry up-side-down and the spout dented in while gouging our hardwood floor. It still works just as advertised and the rest of the kettle seems to have a decent build quality.

text: Weird Design Decisions, But a Good Kettle
Body: Works well a few weeks in. I DON'T like that you have to wait to put the thing back on the base, because otherwise it tries to keep heating the water again after you'd poured it over your tea or coffee. The location of the water level window is absolutely idiotic, though. You can barely see it half the time until you twist and lean over to figure out where the water is at. And you can't see it at all when you hold it, really. It should be on the side, like most of these have it, but it's not a dealbreaker, just weird.The buttons on the handle are really convenient, but so were the ones on the base of our old Breville kettle. The lights aren't too distracting, and they turn off in a decent time period. The keep warm setting would be nice if I ever used or needed it, I guess.The lid can spring kind of forcefully, where our old one had a soft-open to stop hot water droplets from spattering out should you open it just after boiling. Granted, I now just don't open it until it's had a moment to cool down. Doesn't pour as smoothly as our old Breville, but doesn't spill everywhere or anything, either. The base footprint is nice and small. The cord has a good length. This unit feels solid and reliable, whatever weird design decisions were made in its development. And it's very well reviewed everywhere.

I had purchased a Breville for brewing loose tea, but I wanted a separate kettle for boiling water. The CPK-17 is a nice looking kettle, cordless, and has variable temperature settings. I was previously using a very old plastic kettle that took forever and made a mess when boiling. This kettle, while not as fast as I would like, does the job without spurting hot water everywhere. It also has a useful Keep Warm function and can boil up to 1.7 liters. I like using this kettle for bagged teas, French Press, matcha, and boiling water to sanitize my sinks. It pours nicely for the most part. I had some mess with pouring into my matcha cup, but I guess I'll have to try to pour it lower next time.There is a tiny amount of scaling at the bottom of the pot. I haven't been using filtered water, but I think I'll start doing that from now on. The buttons light up in sci-fi blue and the heat will not start until the Start button is pressed. I like being able to see the water level and having many functions for various teas. This kettle is still fairly new, so if something changes, I will update this review. I have read reviews of the numbers fading off, so perhaps in the future, Cuisinart will consider making raised numbers. The settings are all in Fahrenheit, and there's obviously no way to set in Celsius, but this should not be a problem for most US buyers.

text: Brewing Convenience with a Durability Hiccup
Body: The Cuisinart 1.7-Liter Stainless Steel Cordless Electric Kettle, while boasting features I loved, ultimately lands a 4-star rating due to durability concerns. Owning two units now, both experienced the same issue: the scale window becoming unreadable within months, though thankfully not impacting functionality. But with the second kettle showing the same fading markings, it raises a red flag.What truly won me over was the precise temperature control, a game-changer for tea lovers like myself. Each brew got the perfect heat, unlocking its full flavor potential. Plus, the temperature hold function was a lifesaver for busy mornings, keeping my tea perfectly warm and ready to enjoy. The cordless convenience, ditching the cord clutter, made filling and pouring a breeze.However, the aforementioned durability issues cast a shadow. Both kettles suffered from the unreadable scale window, and the first unit's cap even broke after a year, requiring replacement. While not a dealbreaker, it adds another potential weak point.In conclusion, the Cuisinart Cordless Kettle offers unmatched convenience and temperature control for tea enthusiasts. But the questionable durability, particularly the scale window fading, makes me hesitate to wholeheartedly recommend it. If precise brewing temperatures are paramount and you're willing to potentially replace the scale window, it might be worth considering. Otherwise, exploring options with a stronger track record might be wise.

text: Great, fast, easy, no mess coffee.  Here's how:
Body: 2 YEAR UPDATE:After two years of daily use the kettle finally died.  I don't know if I will buy the same thing again.  It cost me about $100 two years ago and at $50 per year, that is a pretty steep price for a kettle.  Being able to select the temperatures was very nice though.  My AeroPress may get a new partner.OLD REVIEW:Using this Cuisinart PerfecTemp Stainless-Steel Cordless Electric Kettle with the AeroPress is like a dream come true for coffee lovers.The AeroPress makes great tasting coffee. It is fast and easy with almost no clean-up.The Cuisinart Electric Kettle allows you to have a fresh cup of coffee at the perfect temperature in less than a minute. With this kettle you can select the temperature at the push of a button and it will maintain that temperature.Here is how I have quick and easy coffee all day:Start the day by filling the Cuisinart Electric Kettle with water and select temperature of 175 or 185 degrees which ever you prefer.1. Insert a filter in the AeroPress and add two scoops of your favorite coffee.2. Add water from kettle to the "2" mark on the AeroPress.3. Stir the coffee grounds for 10 secs. and press in to a cup for 20 secs.4. Pop the coffee grounds in a trash can and quick rinse the AeroPress.6. Fill your cup to the desired level with water from kettle.Less than one minute per cup. No washing pots or coffee filter baskets. It is that easy.

text: Solid performer and is able to keep up with Englishman's constant need for tea
Body: I am English, and with that comes the insatiable need for hot tea.  I needed a good kettle to replace my 10 year veteran kettle and figured I would try for something much more useful to me.  I chose this kettle because of the variety of options for heat and the keep warm feature.  I am mostly happy with it but there are a few things worth noting.ProsLove the temperature featuresEasy of useGood constructionConsEasy to burn yourself on (If refilling after recent use the lid is in the perfect position to drop hot water straight down the handle...the handle also guides thumbs of big hands towards the hot metal kettle too)Keep warm keeps on keeping warm after you have used the kettle, wastes some $$$ on heating the kettle when you have got what you need from itThe kettle seems to catch on the base when replacing it, feels like that will cause a problem in the future.I do recommend this kettle, just watch your hand when pouring (no brainer, but thumbs easily slip onto the kettle body), and when putting in water keep the kettle tipped forwards if you have recently used it to keep the hot water drips from the lid away from your hand.

Last year we went to Europe for the first time, and I can honestly say I never knew about electric kettles. Didn't have a need nor did I pay attention if ever they were on the shelf at a store. In the UK, I was so impressed on how quickly these heated up to make my coffee in the hotel rooms.I didn't think to buy one of these until this year after my wife started to get more interested in making her London Fog's at home. When I bought one, I sent a picture to the English family we met for the first time, and one laughed and exclaimed about how many buttons it had!This has been working well and heats water up so fast! Like the keep warm and auto off functions. Very easy to restart if you need hot water longer.

text: Excellent electric ta kettle.  Cordless kettle is nice.  Love the temperature buttons for the different tea types.  A+++
Body: The Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp 1.7-Liter Stainless Steel Cordless Electric Kettle is a very good buy.  It is probably the best cordless electric kettle out there.  It has the feature of boiling to different temperatures for the different types of tea you will be consuming.  It is a very good size.  It sits on the counter nicely, and it has a very nice stainless steel look.  It is easy to operate, and it can re-heat to keep the water at the desired temperature.  It also has a boil-dry feature as well.  The blue back-color is very pleasant.There is a small slide mesh filter that easily comes out that you can clean.Pour our the excess water when not in use and let your kettle air-day.The bottom heating unit can start to discolor due to calcium deposits from the water.  Depending on your water source, you may need to clean more often.You can clean and de-scale the inside of the kettle with water and white vinegar or with water with baking soda and or lemon juice and set it to boil.  I've boiled just white vinegar itself for a more potent cleaner, and it works fine.I have read that some other people having issues with the lid mechanism rusting, but I have not had that issue myself.  Others have had the bottom heating unit start spotting with rust.  I've only had calcium deposit spotting and was able to clean it with vinegar boil and with a long sponge brush.Other stainless steel kettles rust inside as well especially regular stove kettles, but people can't see it or know it if they are not able to see the inside clearly enough on themI recommend the Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp electric kettle.  It has worked well for me, and I think it has made my tea drinking experience better with the temperature controls for the different types of tea being consumed.  The price is a little pricey for a tea kettle, but the features are nice to have.  The kettle is very solid, and it looks great in the kitchen.  If you have Amazon Prime, the 2-day Free shipping is nice.

text: Not the right product for me - 6 annoyingly specific reasons why
Body: I am returning this unit because it isn't for me.  It is a solid and great product though.  After the fact, I found a solid review by Johnny on this page - go there for details on this product.Dec2016, I gifted this to my Bro & SIL.  It is still going strong.  I have used it when visiting them.July2017, I bought a much cheaper Oster stainless BPA-free multi-temp for myself.  It died last week and is not for purchase (anywhere, even eBay).  So, I ordered this for myself.I am returning it because:(1) it is heavier than I was anticipating, about 9 ounces heavier than my Oscar(2) the handle is oddly counter-weighted so the trip is not comfortable to maintain and makes this feel heavier than it is(3) it is just awkward enough to hold that I stupidly touched the pour spot to assist in balancing a refill (the spout was very very hot)(4) the lid does not open as widely as I wish - I fill it from a higher-up faucet (filter) and the lid is in the way, this shouldnt be an issue for normal-height water sources.(5) the base has three little pegs/legs which means that the base wobbles when moving the kettle - I dont think this is a high safety issue to the point of it easily tipping and spilling (especially when full), but it is annoying.(6) The stay warm function is default.  At least the kettle has an INCREDIBLY LOUD AND CONSTANT beep when the boil-dry safety feature is put into use (which happens what you place an empty kettle on the base without remembering to turn off the stat warm function.Are these nit picky reasons for a return?  Sure.  If this is your first electric kettle, you may not even notice!For me, I've placed an order for the micro which is about 5 ounces lighter (despite double wall construction) and has a different handle design.

We had an older version before this one, and it worked for about 4 years, considering we are using a kettle religiously 5-6 times a day :-D The old one started leaking all of a sudden. So, this one, we had for few days, and this is what I have to say:1) do not just rinse it before use as they recommend; boil it full and empty, few times, to make sure all the smell disappears2) maybe it makes sense to finish the buttons with resin or some sort of sealer as the marks are going to erase soon (they did on our last one so I just printed “a cheat sheet” and kept it near (after being tired of writing them on with a sharpie only to watch them to dissolve again )))3) it’s great that it has a 160F option. When we were researching, that was one of the factors as my daughter only uses this temperature4) the light is definitely brighter on this one so it’s easier to see how much water is in it, especially considering that the scale is so conveniently located behind “in the armpit” ;)))))5) the ready signal is definitely louder than it was in the previous model. They probably think that people only make tea when there is a loud party; or only old people with hearing impairments do that. It sounds a little like alarm clock so I’m going to ask my handy husband if he can adjust it so kids don’t wake up when the kettle is on in the middle of the night!6) the “bump” on the base where you are supposed to position the kettle on, is taller and leaner than previous one, - too bad bc I was hoping to use both bases with one kettle (one for the basement), it’s easier to just carry the kettle rather than disconnect the base and connect it again , and so forthOverall, happy with purchase. We’ll see how it goes later.

text: Kettle is not hotting the water
Body: This morning the kettle was used, tonight I decided to use it and it is not functioning, see video attached. This is very disappointing for me , after purchasing this item and is unable to enjoy the use. So I will appreciate if something can be done as soon as possible. Thanks for your understanding. I await your response.
I don't know what have been done inside the bottom of the kettle, looks like it was opened for repairs.
Product delivered in a box but not manufacturer’s. See picture.
I ordered this kettle for my daughter for her birthday.  When she opened it, she noticed that it was dirty, rusty, and obviously used!  I was not only embarrassed but upset and disappointed.

They sent a used product. Not a new one. I’ve tried contacting but no response so far. It’s a shame because I had one like this before and it worked for many years. It was a wonderful product. Please sellers help me here

text: Mildew inside and cuisinart doesn’t cover!
Body: Cleaned with vinegar. And it’s mildew. I have cheaper kettles that have worked. Thought the name brand cuisinart would be great for our second home. However, after calling the customer service. They were less than helpful. I will toss this one and order the cheaper brand. That is tried and trusted!

The unit works great but rusted in less than 2 months.  Really bad design and quality.  The unfortunate part is that I bought this as a gift for my parents.  See pictures.Amazon always comes through and has helped me to return it!!  Love Amazon....not impressed with Cuisinart.
Only used for a year now that covers can’t close or open
We maintain it very well. always washed with warm soapy water and let it dry overnight everyday. For a $100 product and the name of Cuisinart this is a pathetic product.

text: Leaking from Handle after 1 and a half years
Body: The product works great when its not leaking, but started to leak from the handle after a year and a half of just moderate home use.  The limited warranty is ridiculous, with having to pay for shipping there and to include $15 for the shipping back, I could get a less expensive electric kettle for that price and it would probably last longer than this one.  For the price this one is it should last a lot longer.  The different temperature options are nice and it seemed to get to the correct temperature.
Just ordered this to avoid using microwave too much. Saw it have tea/coffee temperature option. Item came looked used, so didn’t get to try it out. Very disappointed.

After using it for about 4-5 times theres been some rust building on the bottom. I always clean it after use and can’t seem to understand why I’m getting rust, it even looks like it’s burn. Now thinking about it I have been feeling a bit dizzy and sick since I’ve been regularly using it and I hope it’s not related. I wanted to exchange but looks I passed the cut off time, I was going to buy another one for home but glad I didn’t

text: After a year of service it made anaudible pop, shot smoke and died.
Body: After using this unit for one year it suddenly made a loud popping sound, and shot black smoke out of the bottom of the pot. I turned the unit off immediately, but it kept smoking for about 30 seconds. Stuff like this does not make you feel confident about a product at all!

text: Bad quality overpriced don’t buy. Avoid.
Body: Don’t buy it. The steel it made from is a very bad quality. Look at the mold like looking stains on the bottom. It’s scary to drink that water now. Impossible to get rid of it. Paint on the buttons are disappearing slowly. It doesn’t detect no water and turn on while other kettles do detect. The build quality for this price is not good. Rip off.
The most expensive water boiler and the worst, had it replaced by cuisnart 3 Times.. until the warranty ran out and it’s dead again after one year!

text: I do not recommend this due to safety reason!
Body: I really want to like this kettle, but I just found a loose screw in it this morning. How is it safe for anyone?

text: The inner lid is not stainless but plastics!
Body: The inner lid is not stainless but plastics, which might be not heathy. The only reason for me to purchase it with a much higher price is to get a complete stanless kettle.

This Water Kettle was fine (although expensive) until it started LEAKING at the bottom of the handle.There is a Youtube video that explains how to take the whole thing apart and seal it somehow but who has time for that?? Disappointed. I'll buy a glass one to replace.
I used it for less than a year and a half and have to throw it away because the bottom has become destroyed by rust.

text: There is Plastic inside the Kettle
Body: It’s a shame that plastic covers the spout, causing the hot water to make contact with the plastic. Otherwise it would’ve been the perfect kettle.

This is the second one I have bought if these. The first one lasted almost a year and all of the sudden it stop working. So, I bought this one May 3,2023 and the open button is stuck and the lid won’t close. It’s a little over a month old.🤦🏽‍♀️ Now, I can’t return it because the window for returns was June 4th. 😠

Boil water for drip coffee daily - primarily.Ordered same model I had for 5 years.  Lettering on handle began to rub off after 3-4 weeks! It took the previous Cuisinart kettle, four years to wear off....can't wait to see what other "improvements" have been made!

This electronic kettle was lovely for six months, and then it rusted. On the inside, at the bottom along the sides. Do not recommend. Our last kettle lasted years with no rust; that was a Hamilton Beach.

text: It was great while it lasted
Body: I like all the feature of the kettle.  But the button to open the lid stopped working after 9 months.  Sad.

text: Sprung a leak after three years
Body: At first this seemed like a great product. Then it developed a leak in the water window which caused water to leak from the bottom of the pot and pool on the base. There seems no obvious way to fix this. Cuisinart's response was that it was out of warranty and only offered 20% credit toward the purchase of a new unit. I had expected more from Cuisinart to justify the rather expensive purchase price - not an appliance that would wind up in the land fill after only three years. And no, I will not be purchasing another Cuisinart electric kettle.
I was really excited to get this kettle but after 3 months, there is a weird build up at the bottom!Only reason I am giving a two star ; while there was no build up- The kettle was amazing !

text: Annoying to turn off, rusted in 2 months.
Body: Lasted 2 months before hinge on lid had noticable rust.Also annoying for my family to use as we only want it to heat up water once and then shut off, big waste of electricity to maintain the heat it we forget to press the "start" button twice to turn it off after use.

text: First impressions of this kettle are very good. Nice size
Body: Update as of 10/22/18: Originally I gave this kettle 5 stars. I was using it daily for tea and loved it. But last week it just totally died on me. The digital buttons no longer function at all and the kettle is unable to boil water. My guess is that it is an electrical issue. I am in communication with Cuisinart about getting a replacement as the item is still under warranty but the company's communication is very slow.First impressions of this kettle are very good. Nice size, easy to work, boiled water in about 5 minutes... looking forward to making many more cups of tea with this kettle!

This kettle began leaking profusely before 2 years was up and at the of cost $99, the value for money is NOT worth the price. The inside sediment build-up was just as quick as the cheaper Brand I had prior to this one which lasted much longer.I bought this product in Nov 2017 amidst mostly good reviews and I also had brand loyalty to Cuisinart as they delivered on other products in the past. Please note this Kettle is NOT one of their better products.

I have used two of these Cuisinart water kettles over many years and have loved them.  This one had a weird odor to it. I washed it as recommended and added water, brought the water to a boil.  Inside the pot there were melted black plastic (?) strands in the water.  I emptied the pot and pulled out the strands (see photo) I emailed the customer service at Cuisinart and never received a reply.  Is it safe to use this kettle, or will something leach into the water?  I never received an answer.  I gave it three stars because the heating function works as expected, but really what's with the strands.
This cattle literally broke after a year and two months now leaks excessively from the water level viewport.

text: Spots on bottom inside of kettle
Body: I just opened the box, looked down into the kettle and there are spots. Is it supposed to look like this?! I don’t think so! Afraid to use it! Enlarge the photo and see what I’m talking about. I’ll gladly change this review if you can explain these spots.

We use it about a year day to day, boiling a lot of water. Everything is good, but it has one minor issue - it switches to the auto-warming mode automatically by default. Would be great to find the way to disable this mode, because there is a danger to burn it out without the water inside.All the rest is pretty good, and we are quite happy.UPD: it's gone, almost 4 years after the purchase. Not bad, but not good also. My previous one, Panasonic, with similar options, worked over 8 years. This time it started leaking inside, watering electronics, so it started working weird: spontaneousely enabling, disabling, changing modes. So I decided to stop using it.Also, the rust appeared somewhere too.

so I really like this kettle. I love to grab the part of the handle at the top near the lid, which is a bad idea because of the steam, thus with all the buttons on the top part of the handle, I was forced to grab the mid section of the kettle, which to itself, is a safety feature.Then there is the temperature control, I don't drink tea or use it for other purposes, I just use it for boiling water to drink. So I use the temperature contorl shorten the time this kettle uses to warm my water, since i don't need to drink boiling hot water, which takes about 7 minutes to boil. I lowered the temperature control to 160, which only takes about 3-4 minutes to reach the desired temperature. This to me is the greatest feature the company ever implanted.with one fatal flaw. so fatal that i'm willing to return the kettle. That is the lid. it only opens up to about 80 degree. , so when you pour water into the kettle,  you have to tilt it to one side, which is extremely inconvenient. I have a fairly strong grip, but my girlfriend doesn't,  she needs to use two hands to hold the kettle at an angle for the water to pour in, and then set it aside, so she has the hand to close the water. An extremely bad design in an obvious way.

text: Good product, needs better quality parts.
Body: Great product, however lid came off just after a week!!! Poor quality build in some parts.

text: Disable disabling lighting lights water-level backlight
Body: I like this kettle but the water-level backlight is abrasive and unnecessary imo. If you want to disable the water-level backlight, simply open up the bottom and unplug the "LED" connection circled in the attached photo. The device will work as designed, just without lighting up constantly. This will only disable the water-level backlight, so the buttons on the handle for temp control and start/keep warm will continue working as designed.

text: Works great had it for 2 years now
Body: Works great had it for 2 years now, but the label disappears after some time. They use cheap labels. Now you just have to remember what they are.
Fast and easy to use!
excellent kettle, beautiful and easy to use
Love this tea pot! Heats quickly and keeps water hot enough for a second cup of tea! Definitely recommend if you are looking for quality at a decent price!

text: Controlled temp with stay warm feature
Body: The ability to set the temperature setting and have the “stay warm” setting it the best feature. It’s an excellent product.

With how much I drink tea, this is an absolute must! I finally bit the bullet and got an electric to replace the stovetop kettle and I will not look back. The keep warm feature is fantastic for when my partner finally decides they want a cup too and it holds a good bit of water! It doesn’t take up a lot of space and I couldn’t be happier! Quick, easy and clean!

text: Should Have Bought This Years Ago
Body: We were using a beautiful old mid-century modern kettle with a wooden handle for years but it didn't have a whistle so I kept leaving it on the stove and my husband would yell at me that I was going to burn the house down or at minimum ruin the kettle. My sister had an electric kettle but it is ugly and a space hog. This one is as elegant-looking as a kitchen appliance can be.  My husband drinks a lot of different types of teas so he likes that he can set the temperature. And it shuts itself off, so my nerves are a little more relaxed.

text: The bit that's visible is not glass!!
Body: I was so scared of getting another Glass Kettle. Had a glass one just a week ago, for about 6 months before it shattered and cut my husband's fingers when he picked it up as it finished boiling. So we got this replacement and it's beautiful! Perfect. It has many heating options and it has no glass!! Has a lot more cleaning accessibility than my other one as well! So 10/10 Would Reccomend! Thank you!!
This electric kettle ROCKS! Lots of temperature settings, heats up quickly and is very high-end looking. Cuisinart for the home run! I can’t rave enough about this appliance.

text: Must have it, if you’re a tea lover
Body: It is a must for tea lovers. Easy, safe and quick. You can select different temperature for your need with a decent accuracy. Will keep your water hot over a period of time, so you can enjoy your second cup!!!

I make 1- 2 cups of tea at a time 2 - 4 times a day every day. After 7 years, the word open has been rubber off the button, and the R where I push start is starting to fade, and this kettle just keeps going! The previous 2 I had each lasted about two years. A friend recommended Cuisinart when the 2nd one died. They were right.

text: One of The best gift I got my husband for Christmas he loves his coffee

Body: I compared several types of electric water kettles and this one continued to show up as being one of the best models so I went ahead with the splurge. Made my first cup of herbal tea and I was very impressed with how fast it heat up! When it beeped that it was ready I thought there had been a mistake but it had reached temperature and within minutes I had my tea. Unit has a cool touch handle and it easy to lift. So far I'm very pleased with how it works. I like the blue light to make it easy to see when I fill it with water and the temperature control buttons make it fool proof to make tea without having to look it up. Would definitely recommend!

A great water kettle. This is my second one after dropping and breaking one. It probably would have lasted over a decade if I hadn't. Simple buttons to choose your desired temperature. While you can’t choose the exact temperature, the 10-15° increments are fine. I don’t need that much precision. The Keep warm setting works well, especially if you’re doing other things in the kitchen. The only slight I might have is the water measuring system can lag a bit so you have to pour water in and wait a bit to see the measurements.
Love this kettle, love the fact that it has a keep warm feature, most others don't. Worth the price!!

text: Absolutely Love that I can make tea and coffee too.
Body: This saves me so much time! I Love it. It looks great and is so simple to use.
Just rcvd my new kettle , hope can use at least 3 years

I just got this tea kettle and already love it. I drink black and green tea throughout the day and now it’s brewed at the perfect temperature. This has a keep warm button which is amazing for the times I forget and walk away from the kitchen. I also like that it boils the water very fast. Overall, it’s a great kettle and highly recommended.
Like that different temperature modes are available to make perfect tea. A must-have for tea lovers!

text: Is four years equal dependable …I think so‼️⁉️
Body: I am a tea drinker, soup sipper.  I want my water at 190° (not 212°) kind a guy.  I am cursed with a palate, that can taste when tea leaves have been burned in boiling water. This electric kettle has been a dependable product in my home for 4 years. There have been very few days that have gone by when my Cuisinart CPK has not been a reliable part of my kitchen cooking endeavors. This production line’s durability has been tested and found to be wanting for nothing. I cannot believe how much I’ve grown to rely on this kitchen asset.  I will purchase a new one with the expectation that the build quality will be the same. I’ll know coming out of the box whether or not my new purchase has the same build quality. if, the bill quality is not the same… i’ll let you know.

text: Very nice electric kettle Purchased December of 2019. Still working GREAT in Feb 2025
Body: Bought this Dec 2 2019. $64.77 We have used it daily since. Works like it should. I really like that it keeps water hot at the temp you set for 30 minutes, then auto shuts off.  This AM I did a quick test. It took 7 minutes (stop watch) to bring 1.7 L of water to a boil from room temp (68 deg F). I then set temp to 200 let it sit for about 10 min then checked the temp with a food thermometer and it was very close. I had some difficulty seeing due to the steam. I would buy again.Update 02 10 2025Still works great. One of the best purchases I've made. Gets used 2 or more times daily.

I bought this in 2011 and it's now 2019. It is still going strong after almost daily use. The selectable temperature is a godsend for my green tea. It also boils water so quickly that I normally start-off my boiling needs in the kettle before pouring into a pan on the stove. This is as durable as a stove-top kettle. At least two of my friends have purchased this kettle after my recommendation and have been just as happy.I suggest you put ONLY water in this kettle. That way you don't have to clean anything. So, don't put tea, teabags, or coffee in the kettle.
Love the speed and quality of kettle. Like the  different settings for different uses. Quality reflects price point.
It's perfect quality, style, design and color. It's being almost 2 weeks that I am using it, but I can tell it's satisfactory.
just what I needed - works like a carm- easy to use too.
So far I like it very much, I use it once a day to make green tea or ramen noodles. It's nice to have the temperatures for each tea preset.

This product contains black plastic that is not removable near the spout. This means that the heated water is poured over plastic, which releases microplastics into the water you're drinking. This is not a healthful or sustainable design!
2nd tea kettle bough and it died just over 3 years. Very disappointed.

We were excited to purchase this kettle, but unfortunately, our experience has been really frustrating. The first unit arrived with visible scratches, so we requested a replacement. The second one looked fine, but after setting it up, we discovered it didn’t work properly.The blue light turned on when plugged in, so we knew it had power, but none of the buttons responded and it didn’t heat the water. We tried unplugging and retrying after a few minutes, but the issue remained.Having two issues in a row has shaken our confidence in the product. It’s disappointing and stressful, especially for something that should’ve been simple. We’re now hesitant to try a third time.
The electronics on this kettle started to fail after 2 years with light use.Do not recommend for quality.

We used this kettle on a regular basis until recently when we found it in a puddle of water. Yep, still PLUGGED IN after boiling water this thing leaked out all but the two cups we used. We had water all over the counter, and down the cabinet to soak the kitchen rug below it! This thing is a hazard! After years of replacing their coffee makers & kettles, I will never again purchase a Cuisinart product. Dangerous junk that doesn’t last much more than a year or so!

text: LEAKS WATER OUT OF THE BOTTOM!
Body: Leaked water out of the bottom the first time I tried to use it.  Wondered if I did something wrong, so refilled, and it continued leaking.  I am actually stunned… who designs a kettle with a hole in the bottom?  That’s just bizarre.  I have been trying to find a good electric kettle for several months.  My previous one worked well - an unknown brand that lasted 7 years and isn’t made anymore.  But it seems like they all have issues now.  I took a chance, hoping I might get lucky and get a good one.  Nope.  At least it didn’t work from the beginning and was still in the return window.

text: Not insulated and will burn you. It accidentally touched.
Body: Very disappointed. The exterior is a cheap brushed stainless steel. It is not insulated so when you use it, the outside becomes dangerously hot and will burn you if you touch it accidentally.

text: Keeps flashing when not in use
Body: Keeps flashing when not in use, which is very annoying.

After 2 weeks, plastic/machine smell persists.  Spout/filter poorly designed - pouring last cup of water runs out the side of the spout and from under the lid, missing the cup.  Fill level column difficult to see because of positioning behind the wide handle.  After 2 weeks use, there's a rust spot on the bottom plate.  Returning this item.
Zero stars. Garbage! Didn’t work after one week of use.

I bought this kettle 13 months ago. I have used it on average since then about once a week. Two weeks ago it quit heating properly. It will not get hot enough to boil water for tea, for instance. Given that it’s Cuisinart, which was a very deliberate choice, it should last longer than 13 months, especially with minimal use. Cuisinart has been my go-to for many years. I’m wondering if it is time to rethink that brand loyalty.
Lasted 6 months, then Kaput.  Wouldn't buy again.
I’ve only had mine for approximately 6 months and it already is trash! To pay that much and it’s already bad

text: This is rusting after only 3 months
Body: This is rusting on the outside and the inside: I want a refund!!

text: not worth the money- breaks after a few years
Body: Lid broke after 2 years of gentle use (once a day)

text: WAREHOUSE ITEM - DID NOT HEAT - NOT INSPECTED BEFORE SENT TO RESALE
Body: WAREHOUSE ITEM - DID NOT HEAT - NOT INSPECTED BEFORE SENT TO RESALE.Returned to Amazon.

text: Electric panel malfunction after few months
Body: Totally dislike it. This is much more expensive than the other brands and the electric panel is malfunctioning after four months.

Updated Review 4/7/24:It hasn’t even been a year of use and this kettle has a serious problem. It sometimes uncontrollably boils. It will go to a boil despite the temperature setting and even when you turn it off it keeps boiling. I have to physically unplug it to get it to stop. This is not ideal for a smart kettle and certainly not convenient. It also has me concerned for the safety. I do not recommend this product.Original Review: My last kettle finally had to retire after years of service.I got this one to replace it and was not disappointed. Excellent features. The memory is very helpful. Very happy with my new kettle.
Stopped working in 8 months
I received defective item. Do not recommend this seller.
It lasted for 6 months and buttons started to malfunction. Could not start and set the temperature. TOTAL GARBAGE! DON’T BUY IT!
My daughter has this same electric kettle. Hers works wonderfully. The one I ordered did not. The heating element did not work properly. I returned it.
Kettle broke after about a year. Don’t get this product. It won’t last.

I’ve had this kettle for over a year and have noticed black plastic in the water after boiling. At first I thought it was something I did, but it happens every. single. time. I did nothing to chip or break it— the functioning work fine. But there’s a design flaw in the plastic pieces in the kettle itself.Sadly, I don’t feel safe using it.

I upgraded to this unit because my old one only had one setting: boil.  I do think getting an electric kettle with the different temperature settings is crucial.  My family does a lot of tea, along with coffee, and I feel that it does make a difference.My biggest knock on this item is that the lid stopped opening after about 14 months.  It's locked closed.  We still use it, but have to fill it through the spout.  I'd expect something at this price point to last longer.

text: Four your lifespan, make sure you're okay with that
Body: Was this Kettle only meant to live for 4 years? I bought it in 2020 and it stopped working in 2024 just stopped getting hot some of the time or the light would come on and then just turn back off. It was quite expensive and I expected it to last a lot longer. Is there a recall on these?

We bought this kettle to replace our Krups electric kettle that finally died after 7+ years of steady use. We were pleased with how it functioned, but after 5 days the OPEN button jammed and we were not able to close the lid. Tried to unjam the mechanism to no avail. Contacted Cuisinart. Since we only had it a a few days, they advised us to return it to Amazon. I will not buy another one. I'll probably buy another Krups.

I’ve had this kettle for a year now. After a few months I noticed spots inside the kettle. Upon further inspection I noticed it was rust spots! I have tried everything to remove them. I wanted to love it. The selection of temperatures is what sold it. But I don’t want to drink rusty water.
Heats water fine, however, the lid constantly pops open while heating. I have to place a heavy item on top of it to keep it shut, definitely a design flaw

I was excited to have a kettle with all the preset temperatures and keep warm function and all the things it does; i bought it  march 2024 and in September 2024 it started to leak out of the bottom.  Since it probably isn't a good idea to plug in a leaky kettle to an electric outlet i had to throw it away. i bought a Brentwood stainless steel kettle for $28.99  in 2016 and it still works great - it just doesn't have all the preset temps, but it is much more reliable and quieter.  First time i have had a bad experience with Cuisinart. This kettle disappoints and is not worth the price.  I could buy 3 of the Brentwoods for the same price.
pretty convenient while it lasted.  But it wouldn't turn on this morning..  :(

text: After two years, flip up top broke
Body: I used this electric tea kettle daily for two years. Last week the top broke and does not flip up, anymore. I’ve had trouble with the lid sticking on and off for at least a year, but worked with it. However, this new rendition of that problem is unacceptable.For the high price, I expected more from this product. Do not recommend you wasting your money on this expensive electric tea kettle.
The package was opened and casually sold as new!
Product is great, it’s Amazon’s pricing that is the reason for my low review. I bought the item the evening of Aug 22, the following day, it’s $40 bucks cheaper right after delivery. What a rip off.
Ours lasted five months.  The one before that was fourteen.  Either way, not great.

The kettle looks nice. The reheating feature is handy. My main complaint, and why I will no longer use it, is the inability to properly clean the scale buildup in the bottom of the kettle. (I only use filtered water so I wouldn't imagine that much scale). You just can't easily get in there to clean it. With difficulty you can reach some areas but it is impossible to reach all. Consequently, you are basically drinking that stuff in your tea or coffee. I've gone back to my old Russell Hobbs kettle that is shaped in such a way that it can be easily cleaned inside and out. If you don't mind drinking and tasting scale, then it's a fine kettle.

text: The water heated in this kettle tasted like hot plastic
Body: Rinsed it, boiled and threw out numerous rounds of water, boiled water and vinegar in it.  The hot water, the tea brewed with water heated in this unit, tasted horrible, like plastic.  It did heat the water quickly and was easy to use.  But I have returned it and am getting a glass electric kettle that I have used before that does not have the taste problem.

Good: Large capacityBad: Annoying alarm that cannot be disabledWho on earth wants an alarm on a kettle?It beeps quite loudly three times once it has boiled.In this electronic world I need something else beeping at me like I need a hole in the head.
Just died all of a sudden. So sad. Too late to return it.

text: Great kettle until it began to leak after 3.5 years
Body: The temperature control is great.The keep warm function is really useful.But, a kettle should last at least a decade. After three and a half years of ownership, it leaks. That's not acceptable, especially for the price. As the warranty is three years, it does make one wonder if it is designed to survive the warranty period and no longer.

Really happy with it for 1 year, 10 months. Then it failed. Lights come on, but buttons don't respond and water doesn't heat.Used it almost every day, usually several times a day.For the price, I thought it would work much longer.
As the title says. Worked great until it stopped heating and only beeping. Lasted about 6 months for me before it broke. Hopefully will get a replacement and be able to update this review.

text: Wish it would turned OFF completely on its on
Body: I love different settings for boiling water. But I cannot stand that once it boils, eventually you need to shut it off. It's annoying and dangerous!

I have many Cuisinart small appliances and consider this as my go to Brand. The electric kettle has let me down. My first Cuisinart electric kettle lasted 18 months of daily use . This second kettle lasted 9 months. I'll go back to whatever Costco has because those kettles lasted years.

I had a kettle that would always spill so I wanted to buy something fancy. This is a fancy kettle and everything looks fine, but it has unnecessary features that are irritating.1. All the temperature choices are ridiculous. It boils down that I have to click two extra buttons after I put the kettle on. Default is always 170.2. Reheat might be OK but for the most part it is reheating whatever is left of the water so one has to get up and turn the kettle off.It’s a good and sturdy cattle, but I wish there was an option without all these extra features.

I bought this teapot in February 2022. I used it to heat water for morning tea. It just stopped working recently. Seems to be a heating element issue. It turns on but very shortly after beeps like the water is at the desired temperature but is not. Our last teapot lasted years so pretty disappointed.
After heating, the outside of the unit is really hot and could burn be careful.

We have had this kettle for less than two years and the top doesn’t close, making it dangerous to boil the kettle (lest it boils out). The keep warm and different temperature functions are useful, but the kettle beeps when you use up all the water and the lid is now broke ; overall, would not recommend this product.

text: The cover of this kettle does not lock into place. It pops open when in use.
Body: I use this electric kettle to boil water for my tea/coffee. Unfortunately when the kettle is in use for boiling the water the cover does not stay closed. It pops up and poses a danger of spilling hot water. I would appreciate it if the kettle is replaced.

Unfortunately there is something seriously wrong with Cuisinart's manufacturing or quality control as I have had two units stop working on me within a year of purchase. I use them a moderate amount and only according to the manufacturer's recommendations. I will not purchase this product again.

pros: easy to set and turns itself off when desired temperature achieved, also has a setting to continuously reheat itselfcons: the biggest one is that outside of the pot is a MAJOR burn injury risk - DO NOT put in high traffic areas or leave unattended in a way kids / vulnerable populations can get near it ... and the other con is that it has also started to stain on the inside and it's REALLY difficult to clean.overall: don't know if i got a dud or not but this product is feeling less and less worth the money
Too much plastic. Controls are not intuitive. Not what I expected.
Water doesn’t flow well, and I spilled every time. I returned and got another electric kettle.
When being left on its base it randomly switches on and boils at any time

The controls stopped working in March 2023. We ordered it in November 2020.  I'm not happy with a lifetime of 2.5 years, no matter how nice the unit is.  Another complaint is that the handle is not particularly comfortable, especially as the amount of water goes to 1.0 liter or above.

text: The highest heat stopped working on mine
Body: The heating element is not accurate. I had no problems at first but after about 6 months it no longer gets to the highest heat option.

We loved, loved, loved this Kettle. So much so that I am tempted to buy another because when it worked, it worked beautifully. Almost a year to the day we bought it, it stopped fully heating. If set on boil, it would self switch to a lower temperature setting, then take over an hour to just heat to that lower temp. So disappointed, especially since another reviewer said theirs stopped working after 11mos, and another said their's stopped after one year like mine. I have always loved the Cuisinart brand, but now I am concerned about the quality.
After 7 months, mine has started to leak at the bottom of the handle.  For the money, it should last longer. Very disappointed because there were so many features that made this seem like a good buy.

text: It is hard to fill with water, because the gauge is on the side, not visible when you poor water in.
Body: It is not like my old one, I really liked it.

text: Exterior is burning hot, except the handles.
Body: All good except it super hot on the outside
stopped working 7/2022, 3 month after purchase.  Cannot return.

text: Worked great, then it started to rust...
Body: For over $100 I was hoping it would last longer than two years, but it is already rusted at the pour spout and any weld points. It started rusting after 1 year, and by 2 it leaks when pouring... I liked it otherwise.

text: Was a great kettle but it doesn't last
Body: We bought two of these kettles. The last one lasted for 2.5 years. Both kettles were excellent initially but both kettles developed the same two issues. The first issue is the lid stopped popping open. To get it open we needed to use something like a knife to lever the lid. Very annoying. The second issue is the buttons stopped working reliably and after a while stopped working completely.After the first kettle stopped working, we bought a second because we liked the kettle. With the second kettle developing the same issues, this suggests it's a design feature and not a flaw. For the price of these kettle, definitely not worth it. Look for an alternative.

This is a wonderful product, but so difficult to get inside the walls of the kettle to clean it. So for me it doesn’t work. I also wanted a kettle with an infuser and this one didn’t have one. Also be careful don’t double boil, it will spill out and burn everything on your countertop. It’s a no for me.

This is a great electric kettle for coffee and tea drinkers, probably the best on the market, but my 2nd purchase just died on me. They each lasted approximately 5 years. Eventually they start to leak and then will not heat anymore. For $100, I’m not going to bother with another 5-year lifespan. I’d rather pay $20 for something with less bells and whistles and then I won’t care if it breaks after a couple years.

text: This is a great kettle, but you might not receive a great one
Body: I purchased this product over a decade ago it worked wonderfully the entire time until it didn't. Purchase this is a replacement it's the exact same product however immediately upon opening and using the lid isn't functioning very well, this product was on sale when I purchased it these might be faulty ones.

text: Wish I had bought a simpler one
Body: I thought all the different temps would be cool but turns out I don't drink that many kinds of tea so kind of a wasteful distraction. Wish I had bought one with simple on/off.  But it works fine otherwise so if you drink a lot of different kinds then you might enjoy.

text: Not the best quality in stainless
Body: Very disappointed, a lesson that popular brand like cuisinart doesnt guarantees its product quality. so beware.I see  some rusting inside by the cover.

We use it daily (sometimes more than once a day). It does the job but I wish we can see the temperature of the water like our previous one. A feature I don't like about it is that it's very difficult to see how much water is in it when you are filling it from the sink.

text: Stays on longer than you want it to
Body: We like it overall. It has a 'keep warm' button which sounds great and ok, works. But after a month there's no rhyme or reason to it and it just stays on every time you make tea until you turn it off manually. Lots of whistles and bells but little effort to make them tell you what they mean or whether they're even functioning properly. Not a great value.

A full-featured and well made product, with the exception that it doesn't do the basics well, which is boiling water and turning off.  When selecting boil, once reaching full boil, it will continue at a rolling boil for 30+ seconds, which is far too long, spewing hot steam until it decides that it's really boiling before turning off.

text: The open button doesn’t work well.
Body: The open button doesn’t work well.
Bottom stays cool, but metal side walls do get hot.And they are LOUD. Really loud.But it does the job.
It does not auto shut off.
This is my third kettle but first of this brand. So far so good! Seems to be holding up after a month now

Love the kettle and features. Top got stuck open within 2 weeks but the return and exchange process was easy. The kettle itself is great. Hoping it holds up now with the replaced one.Edited - received our replacement quickly and it has been great now for almost 2 months. Heats quickly. Love the temp settings.

I like the size of this cattle!!It holds more than 3 cups of water for tea, but it does get extremely hot to the touch so make sure you hold it by the handleI do find the different parts of boiling water to be an overkill, one button should be enough
I ignored other reviews that said it was heavy when filled. My bad.It is heavy without having to fill.Love the temp options but not enough for battle lifting and trying to do a pour-over.
Boils water, but it's hard to clear the calcium out and the water gauge is difficult to read. Probably prefer something simpler and lighter
It’s nice but it’s missing a schedule option to turn on at a certain time and also because it’s metal, if you touch the metal part, you’ll get burnt.

text: Really good ... but this is our 4th one. A staple, but I wish it was more robust.
Body: It heats well. The I like the temperature selections. It is fairly quick.Of our Prior 3 -  two of them stopped heating (one was a warranty replacement within a year), and our last one the lid will not open.A staple in our house and we really like it; hopefully this lasts longer.Also the outside gets hot so only touch the handle, and make sure you don't over fill it.Only 3 stars because they only last a few years.

I bought this after reading several glowing review. For the price, it's a disappointment. On the plus side, it heats quickly, and the various temperature options are nice. However, fit and finish aren't really premium. The flip top, while sealing reasonably well, doesn't align perfectly with the body. The metal body shows every little stain, so unless you are the type of person who wipes down every device daily, don't expect the kettle to look as pretty as in the pictures. The electronic system is not intuitive at all and every once in a while, it will decide to reset itself to make 160 degree water instead of boiling. Worst of all is the aggressive beeping, which can't be disabled. Not sure about you, but the last thing I need in the morning is a kettle that beeps at me like a commercial oven at Subway. As far as I can see, the only way to get rid of the noise is to kill sever the connection to the beeper.I'll keep using the Cuisinart because I have it, but I miss my simple $30 Amazon Basics kettle.

Nice looking, but...it doesn't have and auto OFF. It does shut off when water has reached the desired temperature, however, it'll keep turning on and boiling it again and again, unless you actually press the Start button again. Another thing, if it's a START/STOP button, it should be labeled as such. It isn't. Didn't leave up to my expectations.

text: Less than two year now it's broken
Body: A weeks ago, top cover was stuck to open, and now all temperature button stop working all the sudden. No more hot water!!

text: NOT SUPER FAST HEATING.  KIND OF BULKY.  TAKES A FEW  MINUTES.
Body: BROTHER IN UK HAS A DIFFERENT BRAND (different electrical than U.S.) which heats water so fast you can just wait a minute or less.  NOT this one.  Unsure if I would recommend.  BUT, it does heat the water!

I liked the features of this kettle a lot, and it's one of Wirecutter's top picks. But the hinge that holds on the lid failed after 3.5 years (6 months after the warranty expired). It doesn't open and close right anymore. I called Cuisinart, and they said that there's no fix for it -- you just have to throw it away. I don't like that. I'd rather have something that can be fixed.

I've used this Cuisinart electric kettle multiple times a day for almost four years, making it my second unit in eight years. While its performance is satisfactory, I expect a product of this kind to last between 10 to 20 years. If durability doesn't improve, I'll consider switching brands. Additionally, a rotary dial for precise temperature control would be a better feature than preset options. The current design caters mainly to tea drinkers, but I use it for my single-cup Aeropress coffee maker exclusively.

Having used electric kettles in the UK, I decided to get one for our home.  I have had confidence in Cuisinart products, and admiring their aesthetics, I chose this kettle. I also liked the temperature selection and keep-warm features. Boiling to black tea temperature takes a long time, and it is noisy. The handle needs to be redesigned-pouring is fine, but lifting is awkward.

We have owned two of these kettles. Pros: reasonably priced, the water temp variety is helpful, the design is sleek and modern, the beep for when water is heated is helpful, the automatic keep warm feature is handy, the handle is cool to the touch, the touch pad is easy to operate. Cons: each of our kettles lasted about 5-6 yrs. and then quit boiling; when full, the kettle can be on the heavy side; short life. Other highly rated(and slightly more expensive models) have been reviewed as lasting 10 yrs. If I have to buy two of this model in 10 yrs, it's more expensive than the one model that lasts 10 yrs. Plus I save time having to shop for another kettle. I'm trying another model next time.
Kettle leeks from the bottom. Lifting it from the base, there is a puddle of water under and on the base, every time I use it.

The good: heats up the water quickly, i like the buttons that allow me to choose the temperature. The keep warm button is also helpful. Looks nice.The bad: The light is ugly and useless, and it stays on even after the water is no longer hot, and turning it off requires pressing the start button, or the keep warm button, or some combination of the two. Seems like every time i want to turn off the light i have to just keep jabbing at those two buttons randomly until it goes off. Also, sometimes the water just dribble out of it instead of a nice steam.Overall it’s good though and i’m happy with it. just takes some getting used to.
We have now our 4th kettle (same each time.) It is used every day. They were purchased 2012, 2016, 2019, 2023. Good overall, just wondering what exactly makes it fail.
Works fine but...Less heat output, hot steel surface and narrowish opening make it a C+ not an A.

This thing is great as long as you remember to turn it off after you use it. Unlike other kettles that automatically turn off after you pull it off its base this one is dedicated to starting on, bringing the water back up to temperature and making a lot of noise when it does it.It also weighs a lot when empty which makes refilling a pain in the butt.

text: Not good enough, keep warm feature allows about 10 degree range
Body: I was hoping that this kettle would be perfect for my french press coffee making, since it has a 200deg setting and that's just the temp I like to use.  And when heating up cold water it was quite decent, the kettle stopped at 201deg, which is close enough.  Unfortunately, when the keep warm turns the heat back on, the temp shoots up to 206, and then it takes more than a minute to cool down to where I'm willing to pour it out.  So it doesn't work for me, I'm returning it.  Better to use a much less expensive kettle with an accurate thermometer, that way I can buy almost three kettles for the same money.

text: It’s starting to make loud poping noise
Body: It’s started pretty good, but now everytime we boil water it makes very loud popping noises. Like it’s gonna explode.

Well, everything is known in comparison.  I bought this kettle because my KitchenAid stopped turning off.  Of course, beautiful design, etc.  but this kettle is made only for tea, you might say, what else is it for!?  For me and my needs!Very often I just need warm water, for various needs, like 50C or 122F.  This kettle does not display the actual temperature but only buttons with presets.  And yet, why do I need this nightlight!  Every time you put it on the stand, the light burns for 5 minutes, it feels like it stays on.  To turn it off, press start twice.  In my opinion, the teapot is overly complicated.  While it working.  I giving it 3 stars.

Sadly it’s awkward to use. For such an often-used appliance that’s a big drawback. I do like the ability to select the desired water temp. I really wanted to like this kettle but I wish I had stayed with my previous style.

I am on my 2nd cuisinart electric kettle and I’m disappointed in my second purchase. Since I received the kettle it automatically blinks with all the lights going crazy. Initially I thought maybe it’s a new thing since this is my 2nd one, but now the blinking lights has gotten worse and I’ve tried unplugging and replugging. Now I’m scared of getting a third one but I love these with it’s multiple tea selections.

text: My favorite electric kettle so far, but.....
Body: We got our first iteration of this kettle over six years ago after having two less 'fancy' kettles quit on us after ~2 years. The first kettle (bought at Bed Bath and Beyond in-store) was amazing, never had any problems with it until it finally started to leak. Since it lasted so long, we decided to buy this kettle again; however, the one from Amazon lasted about 5 weeks before it broke, signaling that it boiled dry even when it was full of water, never heating again. Didn't matter if we unplugged and plugged back in, dried it out, etc., nothing worked.Gratefully, Cuisinart replaced the kettle under warranty and the replacement kettle we received from them is working well. I don't know what caused the issue in the end, but just beware of buying electronics 3rd party, I suppose.

text: Too heavy and too many buttons
Body: This water kettle is heavier than the one I used to have that broke and I’m replacing. I think it could be too heavy for younger children who are more capable of using it and older adults too. While the heating choices are nice to have there are too many buttons with blinking lights leaving me unclear about what needs to get pushed and in what order. The warming feature is nice but is automatically on so if you don’t want it to reboil three more times on its own every few minutes you need to press the button when done with your first boil to stop it. Overall it’s more complex than necessary.
Lovely kettle, settings are very convenient but a little loud
This kettle has been pretty good over the last few months. The build quality was a little underwhelming for the price point (we paid $80), but it does what it says.

text: 9 Year workhorse, but will it last?
Body: Well reviewed for a reason – good capacity (1.7L), adjustable temperature, boils water fast.After 9 years we're running into a couple of serious problems though:* The temperature alarm is sporadic.  The safety features still turn the kettle down when it boils, but sometimes we get the tone when it's up to temperature and sometimes not.* More annoyingly, the lid hinge is starting to fail in a somewhat mysterious fashion.  Basically the lid no longer opens or closes smoothly, and feel like the plastic hinge back is going to break as you try.  The button to open and close no longer works at all, you kind of have to pry the lid open with your fingernail.

text: I can have my hot water
Body: It's ..ok

This kettle has been around a long time with little to no changes. I can see why. After having this now for a few weeks, we've been able to enjoy the multiple options this kettle provides. From varying temperatures to "keep warm" settings, this has been a useful add for the whole family. I love that I can fill the kettle and have it warm for a while so I can continuously have hot water in the morning while the family is rushing around to get out the door. It provides enough hot water for the whole family.A few cons that only take being aware to avoid. It's metal so it remains hot for a long time. Don't set it near anything and always be aware when working around or near it, that it can burn you if you rest your wrist or hand on it. Definitely keep it away from little ones. Also, it is quite loud when warming up and if you don't turn off the "keep warm" setting you will hear it turn on while keeping the contents warm. I don't mind these things as I usually leave the room and continue getting ready for the day while it's doing it's thing.
I’m satisfied with this kettle.  I deducted one star because I would’ve liked a different designed spout for more control when pouring.
Sigh, water level is in liters, but included recipes are in ounces.
This seems very nice and works well, but is very heavy when filled with water. My hands aren't good, so I had to return it.

text: We like this, but doesn't consistently turn off
Body: We've been using this kettle for 28 months and it's started staying on instead of going to keep-warm.  Not all the time (maybe half the time.)  So we have to keep an eye on it.  Husband still bought another.  We'll start using that after determining if using a lower preset temp is a good solution.
Extremely high quality
