It is heavy and it is awkward to see the water level while filling, particularly if you hold it by the handle.
Really fast heating, tons of capacity, accurate enough temperature. After a few months the fill lid doesn't open easily. Plug does get warm, however.

We purchased this high end Cuisinart product in 2016. We used it a good eight years and took care of it as the manual states. The reason I’m not giving it five stars is I think something like this should at least last 20 years. I guess not this day and age with the disposable society. Anyway, save your money buy something less expensive.

text: works well but water level is difficult to see in the blue light for some people
Body: Used for boiling water for coffee/tea.  Works fine, but my husband has a hard time seeing the water level. It really doesn't need all that blue light!

Please note after using this electric kettle for a while, the inside of this kettle will begin to have rusty. There will be several small dots all around the inside of the kettle which it can make this kettle not cleanable anymore. Also, the weight after the water are finished boiling, the outside gets very hot (DO NOT TOUCH IT WITH BARE HANDS)!! Also it's very heavy after boiling. So If you don't have enough energy/strength to carry this electric kettle, look for another product that best fits you!! Also stay cautious when using electric kettles (they can get hot and your hand can get burned)!!! Return this item back to Amazon if you see it gets rusty!
Worth the price and doesn’t take up much counter space. The keep warm button is awesome!
yes
Good unit, makes great variety of teas with different temp requiremnts.  Recommended.

text: Love the temperature presets! Excellent Cuisinart customer service.
Body: We love the presets for brewing coffee and tea at the correct temperature, and our hot beverages have never tasted better. We're sensitive to noise, so we like that the beeps to let us know the water is hot are not loud or annoying. And the alert lights are an attractive blue and not too bright.Cuisinart customer service is excellent. Soon after the 30-day return window closed, it started leaking from between the plastic base plate and the carafe. I called Cuisinart, described the problem and gave the agent the serial number from the Amazon listing page, model number from the bottom of the carafe (printed in white ink) and my contact info. A new electric tea kettle was delivered 4 days later.Unfortunately, the replacement was defective. The spring that pops open the lid when you press the button only works when the carafe is sideways or upside down, never when it is upright. Time to call Cuisinart customer service again. Aargh!FYI:  Calling Amazon customer service after the original-purchase tea kettle started leaking was a waste of time. The agent said she would call Cuisinart during business hours, give them all the details, patch me into the call, then follow up to make sure my problem had been solved. None of that happened. I wish I had contacted Cuisinart to begin with.

I thought I hated green tea. turns out I was just making it wrong. I love this kettle and the temperature settings. If you are into teas, then I highly recommend this kettle. My daughter love hot cocoa and also appreciates the precise temperature settings so that she can enjoy it without the scald.  The only concern is how small the opening is when it comes time to clean, but, I'm sure my silicone bottle brush will come in handy for that. Well worth the extra for the extra features. I'm very satisfied with this product.

text: Reasonable Price and Easy to Use Features!
Body: This electric kettle heats up very quickly and has a 30 minute memory that will retain its temperature even after you pick it up and pour some water into cups. The only negative it that the light up fill indicator is sometimes a bit hard to read.

text: Great features and ease of use
Body: I love this teas kettle. Easy to use features, heats water quickly and hold the temperature. Perfect preprogrammed settings. I wish it was clear though.

After forgetting (and burning) several kettles on the stove I finally invested in an electric kettle. All my friends in Europe use one (so I figured there must be something to it). Now I don't know how I ever lived without it. The only reason I gave this 4 instead of 5 stars is that I don't think all the extra features on this model were worth it. Cuisinart makes a basic model that's cheaper and just as good. One tip I would recommend is if you don't want water scale at the bottom of the kettle, empty it after each use and let the heat evaporate any residual moisture.
Loved the temperature options, no more guessing.  I like that it keeps the water warm. I Only had it for two weeks, so i cant comment on durability
Works great…just a bit heavy when file with water ( arthritis people)

Very good quality pot, had it for sometime now it does the job, has different settings for different temperature,  it would have been nice if it had a screen to tell you the temperature like the kitchen aid one
Only had this item for a few months I think, and the silver plate on top of the lid just popped off. It still functions fine, but this little defect makes me wonder about the overall quality now...
This is a different kind of kettle but what’s great is it tells you what temp to set according to tea type
I bought this for my wife for her tea and it works amazingly. It isn't able to be set to a custom setting but it has plenty of options for brewing your tea.

text: Heats to 200 degrees for French Press quickly
Body: Generally pleased with the kettle. However it is difficult to pour out the last couple ounces of water. A redesign of the spout is badly needed.

Like the stainless steel  look and lighted water fill display. Variable temp controls also a plus. A bit heavy when filled to capacity. Keep warm function a plus as is automatic shutoff if you forget.

This is a good electric kettle with many temp settings. The only 1 feature 1 don't like is the keep warm, it on all the time unless we turn off. I think it should be the other way round, should be off all time time unless we turn it on.

I drink a lot of tea (I’m a Brit!). This kettle has a pretty good water capacity and boils the water quickly.The design is functional and its very easy to use.My one concern is that it seems a little lightweight and will not last long for a heavy user like me. Time will tell.
Perfect for my kitchen!
No complaints!  Buy it!

This thing works really well. I do wish it stayed on longer, but I get why it doesn’t. My least favorite thing about is is this…..when the kettle is full, it’s got a little weight to it. Naturally you want to hold the handle and support it somewhere else with the other hand. However, the pot gets really hot, so you can only touch the handle. But even holding the handle is weird since it’s got the buttons on it.
Water cools off too fast. Pot should be insulated
I like the kettle.  It is a little difficult to check the water level.
It’s perfect for my morning tea or to make my instant breakfast cereal. I bought two.

Update: Mine broke after a year. The control panel buttons stopped working. But Cuisinart customer service was great. This is covered by a very long warranty. I emailed customer service and had a new, replacement tea kettle shipped and arrived within 2 weeks. Great job Cuisinart! The warranty and good customer service just might make this worth the cost!This is a 5 star product, but I'm giving it 4 stars because it's so overpriced. However, it works great and lasts - I've had mine for about a year. I purchased some cheaper temperature-controlled kettles before this and they just wouldn't last, each would die after a few months. I bought this one to try and fix that problem, despite the price. So I'm pretty happy with this one. Works like I want and hasn't broken. However - come on! $100 for a water heater?!
Would like to give it 5 stars but the on button is glitchy. Also, it doesnt turn off unlessyou click “start” again. Not a very intuitive design. Looks nice sitting on the counter.
I bought this as a replacement for the same item that was years old. The newer version has a very low beep to let you know the water has boiled. That’s my only complaint.

text: Fool proof, but low visibility when filling
Body: I can't see the fill line when I'm filling it, so I'm always having to guess and check on my measurement. That's annoying, but it's great at getting the water to the temperature I need for various drinks, and I absolutely love that it will maintain the temperature for half an hour unless I tell it not to.
As good as we've found over the years. AFter a couple of weeks, performing as advertised.

Temp control is awesome, but the fill indicator is hard to read as it's hidden behind the handle. Also, the keep warm feature is more annoying than useful as I have to remember to turn it off each time.

I love all the features of this kettle. But after 6.5 years of constant everyday use, it has started leaking water. However, it still lasted longer than similar other kettles I owned previously. I'm debating whether to replace it with the same model, or go for a less expensive one with fewer features (I rarely used most of the temperature control buttons).
The only problem that it by default try to keep water warm - and if you forget it - it may be a safety issue
Works quickly and is pretty quiet. Nice, easy to read display, simple to use. Just what I needed for a quick cup of tea or to boil water FAST.

Quality kettle that heats water quickly.  The only feature I dislike is the "keep warm" feature, which automatically engages when you place the kettle back on its base.  This requires remembering to turn the keep warm feature off every time. I almost never want it to keep the remaining water warm and would instead prefer the keep warm feature not be the default.
So far so good after 5 months. Do download manual & read Troubleshooting so you know what to do when lights all start to flash
good quality. I recommend buying
Works exactly as described. Great variety of temperature options, easy to use, a beautiful design.  This was a Wirecutter recommendation and it delivers.
Love it, lasts longer

text: Perfect for the avid tea drinker
Body: I love the different temperatures of the different kind of teas. And the keep warm feature. I'm happy with my purchase.Cuisinart is a good name brand. My husband has a cuisinart coffee maker and we've had for a long time with no problems. Another reason I chose this brand.

works as described

Very good. The color and stainless steel interior is super good

text: Nice to Control the Temperature & Minimum Plastic
Body: Adjustable heat features are fantastic for a tea lover, especially water temp for black tea.  One thing to know is the kettle does not automatically turn off if you take it off the heating element before it is finished, and you must manually turn kettle off.  Kettle will automatically shut off if you let it reach selected temperature.  I like the minimum amount of plastic.  Former kettle (another brand) was great, but after time, the plastic around lid and inside lid started to deteriorate and break off.

I bought this in January 2012 and just today when I went to turn it on, I learned it stopped working. I already have another one on the way. For 13 years, I’ve used it pretty regularly for tea, ramen, and whenever else I needed hot water quickly. It works well, and I’ve found that I can’t live without it. Sure, I could heat up water on the stove or in the microwave, but it’s so much more convenient to have this tea kettle.I’m hoping the quality of the new one I purchased is just as good as the one I bought more than a decade ago.Regarding auto shutoff, I never intentionally used that feature. I find it doesn’t work well, but I’m good about keeping an eye on the water level.When my current one died, I considered shopping around but decided to stick with this one. I know how it operates, I like how it works, and I’m hopeful it’ll last me another 13 years.
Have used it every day for years.

text: MAKES TEA 3 TIMES FASTER THAN STOVE DOES!~!

I bought this in 2011. It’s 2025 now and it finally started to show issues after multiple daily uses.This is an amazing product. Well made and designed to last.  I’m ordering it again.
Appears to of good quality. It is relabeling a lesser quality product that had to be returned.
We use mostly for hot tea. Rises to desired temperature quickly. Seems well made, only time will tell. We like it. 2 thumbs up!

So glad we bought this. It’s easy to use. Take it out, set it on the electronic disc (round disc), plug it in, fill with water. Choose one of the settings that you need for your tea or product and it will let you know when it’s ready.Our daughter loves this.

My former electric tea pot finally died after 10 years.  They no longer make that model, so I decided to try this one.  I have friends who use this one so I decided to get it.  Now I can drink my daily green tea with water at the perfect temperature.  Who knew?  I’d always just boiled water.  Green tea is actually simmered at below boiling temperature.  The only complaint I have about this tea pot is that it is single walled, meaning I can feel how hot the water is in the pot, so I have to remember not to touch the outside of the pot.
Very pleased.  Works great.
I use this constantly. I love this tea kettle!

We got used to having a kettle in our room on a recent trip to the UK. This is a great kettle with choices of water temperature for different optimal brewing temperatures.
Quickly boils the water then holds it at that temperature.  Would be helpful if the handle had a few finger grips to help when pooring.
This heats your water to specific degrees you set and keeps the water hot for 30 minutes.  Fast heat up.  If you are a tea connoisseur, you will love this!
Great , like the warming button and different settings for teas , worth buying
This has everything i was looking for and I am glad to have it!
I love my new Cuisinart electric kettle.  The temperature controls produce the best temperature for tea.
Most used appliances in my kitchen. Love the auto programmed temperature

This replaced an electric gooseneck kettle from another manufacturer after it died and I am so glad that we replaced it with this Cuisinart unit. This kettle is easier to fill, easier to pour and holds more water than the previous kettle. There is finally enough water for my French press coffee and my wife's tea.
Fast heating the water. Don't need to use microwave to heat water. Love various temps to make special teas.
This is my second purchase.  The first one lasted 4 years.  Works great and I don't have to clean very often if I use filtered water.

My kettle broke before a year but they replaced it.  This is my second kettle. The first lasted 8 years and the second less than a year. However, I called them and they are sending me a prepaid label to send back the broken one and they will then send me a new one.

Body: I'm not a tea perfectionist so this is good enough for my purposes. Overall this is an excellent hot water kettle with multiple selections. I'm sure there are more precise kettles out there but this is more than good enough.
Fast and good control at temperature you need

text: Multiple spots of rust and corrosion only after two months of use
Body: Avoid. Multiple spots of rust and corrosion only after two months of normal use.

No matter how well you maintain this kettle, you will fight mold. I clean it after every use (1 cup @ 190°) and put on elevated drying rack to dry. Next time I use it, I always find mold. text: Mediocre kettle, happy about long warranty, not happy about rust for the price
Body: Most expensive kettle I've owned, more than double the price of the last one, and within 3 days it had rusted on the inside. While the discoloration isn't poisonous, I'm surprised something this "premium" is built with the poorest materials. My previous Ovente kettle looked this rusted after a year but started to leak from where the bottom of the handle was attached thus the replacement. Other than the rust, the Cuisinart looks and boils alright, and the "keep warm" setting is useful for people like me who get distracted and remember much later that they started making tea. I'm happy that it comes with a 3 year warranty, which is more than most, just in case I have issues down the line.

This is an excellent tea kettle overall. I’ve had it for a little over a year and I use it pretty regularly. I love how uncomplicated and streamlined it is. It is light weight, yet sturdy and well made, a strong example of a great Cuisinart quality product. I love the 6 temp settings and that each temp is labeled with the type of tea it’s best for. I also love the keep warm button bc I’m always busy and forgetting to pour my water when it boils. That brings me to my first reservation, however. I never notice that the water has reached the desired temperature bc the kettle doesn’t beep or make any sound, not even an audible click. That means I turn it on and continue with my busy morning of prepping breakfast and lunch for kids, and I completely forget about my water for far too long. I often then feel like I need to re-boil it, which starts the whole problem over again.The keep warm button should probably help with this, but the blue and white lights for the buttons are not super clear in letting me know if the keep warm setting is on or off. The blue light is very nice looking, but when many buttons are lit up blue and one is white, I don’t know what the means. I could reread the directions, but can’t it just be more intuitive?I like that there’s a window to see how much water is in the kettle. The pop open lid is very easy and never gives any issues. Boil time is pretty fast, though I don’t time it. There is a little screen to use as a filter for making loose-leaf tea in the kettle, which is nice, but for me, unnecessary. It’s nice that I can just take that out. I generally do leave it out because another minor drawback is that the opening for the kettle is not very wide, so when I fill it from the filtered water on my fridge, it doesn’t fit easily under the fridge filler. I have to aim the filler into the spout in order to fill it, and if that little filter screen is in there, the water splashes back and pours out everywhere. If I forget the filter is in there, it’s a rude way to find out, but it’s easy to avoid the issue and I like that the filter allows the kettle to be used in different ways for the tea experience you want.the price point seems reasonable for the quality and durability. cleaning it can be tricky because of the narrow top opening, but a bottle brush works fine and if u just use clean filtered water inside you dont need to clean it too often. i also love that the cord for the base cab role up inside the base so you dont have a bunch of extra cord cluttering your counter. i love that the base is very simple and barely noticeable.Overall I love this kettle. Just would make a few minor changes to design to fit my own ease of use.
The pot works as it should, but does anyone else’s look like this inside? Concerned that the coating is coming off and could be bad for your health

text: Great life so far, random black piece in water?
Body: Bought my kettle almost ten years ago! (So older model than listed here, of course.) It has held up well. I noticed the buttons are starting to fade so I am careful with not using anything abrasive on them. I read reviews a couple years ago about the lid not popping open and had never had that problem, but of course it started soon after I read that... I just fill through the pour spout now instead. (It does still open, just trying to preserve the function by not using it.)I’m posting because today we found this random black piece inside the water... it doesn’t come out because of the filter. No idea what it is from... or if it needs to be reattached. Anyone know?

This review is after using the unit for at least 2000 heating cycles (at least once per day for 6 years, although more likely 2x per day realistically).Pros:- Boils water quickly.- Easy to use.- Requires very infrequent cleaning (unless you have hard water).- Great for coffee and tea due to variable temperatures. I tested these with a digital thermometer, and the temperatures are accurate within a couple of degrees.- Large capacity.- Spring-loaded lid that is attached to unit.- Low-profile base, no wasted counter space.- Good quality cord, built to last.- Auto-off timer after 30 minutes.- Overheat protection (turns off unit until cooled down), which is useful if it is turned on while empty.I really want to give this unit 5 stars, but there is one major con, which is a common issue found in many of the reviews here on Amazon: the unit is leaking from not one, but TWO separate locations: water leaks from the handle, with the water running into the base (see photo); and water leaks from the base itself, (see photo). The entire base that contains the electrical components is totally full of water. Water and electricity do not mix, and it looks like a highly dangerous situation.The water leak started a couple of months ago and slowly has gotten worse, until today it flooded my kitchen with a liter of water.Otherwise, this is truly a amazing water kettle, and I wish that the one flaw wasn't a potentially life-threatening one...I will update this review should I hear from Cuisinart about any updates to prevent leaking on future models, as I see from the reviews that this is a common issue.

I have used this kettle daily since 2014, on average 4 times each day. Despite the button labels slowly fading away (see picture) it is still going strong. Compact yet with ample volume, it has a simple button interface to vary water temperature and a clean design.Literally 10's of thousands cups of tea of all varieties have sourced from this appliance.Highly recommended.

Exactly as described! I was skeptical about purchasing this,  let's be honest we can all boil water from the stove. Saves us so much time and the temperature controls are awesome for avid tea drinkers. Love it, and am completely satisfied with this purchase.
I’ve had 2 of these in less than a year.  Works great for a minute, then doesn’t when you can no longer return it.
It just stopped heating water after a year. It powers on and then powers back off. It was working off and on, but now it’s dead.

All of the positive things in the other reviews are true, but only as long as the kettle lasts.  I have had this for about a year and it no longer boils water.  When I put it on boil, it only gets to 172 degrees. That makes for some weak tea--yuck.  So, I then have to put it in the microwave.  Truthfully, I should just put it in the microwave and just pass up using the kettle.  So, despite the good qualities, I will not be replacing it with another Cuisinart.  I think this is something that should last longer than a year.

text: Product received in an open box
Body: I bought this item as a gift and it arrived in an open box

The ketlle is all bells and whistles, but in point of fact when you push the boil button and it heats up the water, said water is nowhere near the boiling point of water--it's very hot, but not "boiling hot".  Do a test: let it "boil" water and then boil a pot of water.  Put both liquids into two separate cups.  One will actually steam, the other will not-the latter will be the Cuisinart.  Buy a teapot.

text: Black plastic inside exposed to hot water :(
Body: If you care about micro plastics in your system this is not for you.  I otherwise love this tea kettle, works great.I just became aware of all the black plastic and clear plastic the water is exposed to.  Being mine has lasted for years, it is a real concern for me that the plastic is surely getting in to my tea.I would not buy it again.
The kettle leaked after 18 months

I have used this kettle for a few months. I like the kettle overall. It heats quickly and the ability to select a variety of temperatures is a wonderful feature. However, as you can see from this picture the cheap plastic parts in the lid have failed rendering what is a great kettle useless because the lid refuses to stay closed. If Cuisinart would spend an extra 25 cents on a nicer lid it would be a great buy. Instead I have spent the last 30 minutes trying to figure out a way to repair or an easy fix. I’m going to give the Amazon Basics brand a try and for $28 I won’t be out a lot of money if it doesn’t last like this Cuisinart.
This kettle used to work great until suddenly one day it simply stopped working. We only had it about 15 months, and it’s not like we were rough with it. For the price it’s totally unacceptable.

The tea kettle performed beautifully for the first ~12 months we had it, but after that it frequently has an error while heating and has to be taken off the base for a minute to reset before it will resume heating.  Sometimes it does this repeatedly without heating successfully.  We have cleaned the kettle and descaled regularly, so not a problem with scale buildup.  Maybe the electronics are failing.  Either way it is a bit too expensive for the time it lasted.

I've had this kettle for two years and I hate it. It frequently goes into "stay warm" mode on its own, reboiling the little bit of leftover water. Eventually this will run it dry, but it's dangerous because when you think the kettle should be cool, it's still hot. This feature should not exist on a kettle. This device is far too complicated.

The kettle heats fast.  However it is extremely heavy, awkward, and difficult to clean.  We only use one temperature setting so the temp choices are irrelevant for us.  The kettles we used in Europen Air BNBs were both efficient, less heavy, and more attractive.  Wish I had noticed the brands.

We've used this kettle for about 3 years.  It heats well and we like that you can choose different temperature settings.  BUT, it is so noisy while heating up we can't hold a conversation in the kitchen.  The beep when its ready is super loud as well.  It's gotten really bad scale buildup and because the opening is so narrow, it's hard to get your hand in there to clean it.  We've tried de-calcifying it with vinegar, baking soda, ice, and cannot get it clean.  We're going to be getting rid of it for a quieter model.

This was good while it lasted - which was just under 2 years. Very disappointed. The water would heat up fairly fast but does not stay hot very long. The auto shut-off works and I understand the "safety" part of that. Would be nice to be able to toggle that off or on, depending on how long you need it for.

Ive had this Cuisinart model for 6 years so I'll give the pros and cons.Pro-I love the ability to change the heat settings and while its not the fastest, Id say it boils water in a reasonable amount of time-I use it everyday so its withstood heavy use over a long period.-The design doesnt take up much counterspace-stainless steel has held up well. It's sturdy.Cons- the reason why I'm disappointed is that despite my routine cleaning, it still developed mold inside the plastic water chamber, right at the top. An area that is difficult to access and honestly I can't see how it would be avoidable. So an overall poor design!It's a shame because the average person would be deterred by this and throw out the kettle, resulting in unnecessary waste.I was able to watch multiple YouTube videos on how to disassemble the entire kettle, so I was able to remedy the mold situation but it was very time consuming.To this point, the opening on top is small, thus making it hard to clean. A solution of diluted white cleaning vinegar/water has prevented scale buildup, but it's hard to get your hand in there to scrub with soap. And there's no way to get into the water chamber to clean.

Have had this kettle now for a few months and I think the nicest thing I can say is that "it works as advertized".  Some observations: 1) the water level is very hard to read even with the LED lighting,  particularly if you are at all 'vision impaired'--i.e., wear glasses  2) I don't mind a "keep warm" feature but it should have an automatic shut off once you take the kettle off the plate. Genuine waste of electricity.

text: Stay warm feature keeps boiling water when empty
Body: We only use the kettle to boil water for black tea, so the different temperatures are not useful for us.  While it boils quickly, the default "stay warm" feature is really annoying.  So many times I have sat down with my cup of tea only to hear the kettle trying to boil water when it is empty and I have to get up and switch it off.  With so many lights you have to pay attention that the stay warm button is off each time.  Sounds simple but I am making tea 8-10 times a day (I am English!) and it makes it more complicated than a kettle should be IMO.  So we are replacing this.

text: It's NOT cordless!  Temp buttons are good.
Body: I prefer the color scheme of my Haden or Smeg is better!  I find that they are more solid too.

I expected more from Cuisinart. Yes, it boils water, but it is poorly designed.o The outer shell is not insulated. Similar kettles are wrapped in a vacuum layer of insulation. That allows you to pick the kettle up with two hands: one on the handle and the other on the opposite side. That's important when the kettle is fairly full, which makes it too heavy to pick up convenienty by the handle alone.o It has a guage that shows how full it is. But the guage is between the handle and the kettle, making it difficult to read.o The keep-warm features turns off too quickly. I've started the kettle and then left to walk our dogs. When I return 20 minutes later, the kettle is completely off -- even though I had pressed the keep-warm button before leaving.My overall impression is that the kettle was designed by inexperienced product designers. I expected more from Cuisinart.

I bought an earlier version of this tea kettle and wish I'd just bought a less expensive one.  Every time you take it off the heating element, you must push button and be sure there are NO lights on or otherwise, it will keep boiling.  This is what another reviewer said and it is true; it will "boil dry".  I have to be so careful myself and I use it multiple times a day and even more careful when guests want to help themselves.  I thought I would use the varying temperature settings for different teas as I'm a big tea drinker, but I don't.  As far are quality goes, I am very satisfied; it is made well and I've had it a long time.  Also, it is hard to gauge how much water to put in; you can see the amount once it's on the element and  the blue light is on, but, there again is a problem.  I'm not good at the metric system so I'd prefer it was in ounces.
Good but the lid mechanism broke and cost $55 to fix it after warranty. More McGivered than fixed!

text: Love everytning about it except for...
Body: I love how quickly this kettle boils my water, and keeps it warm for a few minutes, I don't have to worry about unplugging it because it will automatically shut off, and will detect when there is no water so you don't have to worry about leaving it on. The only two things that I don't like about this kettle compared to my last kettle is 1) too heavy, the kettle is heavy without water you have to hold it with two hands of you want to fill it up all the way up, so I only fill it up half way. 2) the other downside to this kettle is how hot it gets on the outside, since it's all metal, you have to be careful not to touch the outside when the kettle rings the bell. I supposed this is how the old fashion kettles used to be, except this kettle is supposed to be modern.

DurableWeaknesses:1. Very noisy while boiling, approx. 70 dBA (loud as driving inside a car)2. Very noisy beeps, on every button press3. Slightly ugly

Apparently some sort of seal failed, making the kettle useless. I'd recommend an all glass kettle so that does not occur. For the price, I'd expect more than just a few years of use.
