Until the lid mechanism malfunctioned a few weeks ago (May '23), and ultimate failed altogether.I thought of finding someone who can fix it, but with labor prices in SoCal it would have come out more expensive than buying new.I guess 4 years is not a bad run, but I still figure it should have lasted longer.
After a few months the thermal switch prematurely shuts kettle off. Or at times never starts. Needs improvement. Seems like other companies have similar problems

text: Worked great for 6 years until the bottom leaked
Body: Worked great for 6 years until the bottom leaked... I really liked this kettle.  Given the price, I'm very surprised it didn't last longer.  It leaked and shorted out the heating element.  That said, I used it roughly 3 times per day on average, so maybe it deserves more stars?

Accidentally boiled-dry the kettle this morning.  Then it stopped working/wouldn't restart.  Thought it was a goner.  Looked online for info on how to reset.  Ultimately found this in the Cuisinart manual:  BOIL-DRY PROTECTION:  Your kettle is equipped with boil-dry protection.  If it starts heating without enough water in the unit, the heater will automatically shut off to avoid damaging the heating element.  The lights will flash and the unit will beep to alert you.  ONCE THE KETTLE HAS COOLED DOWN, lift it off the base, then replace it to reset and restart the heating cycle.  The quickest way to cool down the heater is to fill the kettle with cold water; however, you can also wait for it to cool down by itself.It worked!I gave it a 4 star rating because it can get SUPER HOT on the front part of the kettle, where I naturally want to place my hand when pouring.  There should at least be a sticker warning the consumer of this issue.  I know better now . . .

We use this every single day at work. There is no stove and we all drink a lot of tea and hot chocolate. This makes it so much better than having to heat the drink in the microwave. It is a little loud when it's at the end but not so much I will say it's not worth it.
Excellent addition to our kitchen. Nice features, looks good and heats up fast too. No complaints 5/5 Highly recommend.
I've owned this since 2018 (it's 2025) and it's a great kettle! It's still going strong and we use it almost daily!
We just ordered another one after our 8-year-old kettle died on us. If this one lasts as long, it's a worthwhile investment!

text: Much faster than boiling water on the stove.
Body: Boiling water for tea is the number one use of our Cuisinart kettle. There are several different temperature settings for different foods and drinks.  Other reviews led me to the Cuisinart, even though I don't use all the settings.  But I really like it for everyday use.

I’ve had mine for over 10 years and it’s been great, still works like new! Love the temp settings and the keep warm option, they allow you to brew at correct settings for best results! Highly recommend!

This kettle looked like a great choice based on reviews. Well... as I unpacked it, my first impression was "oh, it is heavy". But as they say "I really wanted to love it". So i pushed the button to open the lid... it opened smoothly and slowly... and I assessed the opened hole. It was not big. Also, the lid construction and filter parts were half closing it. I could see water splashing when pouring. One has to aim hard!! Anyways, I aimed and succeeded. Then i plugged it in the socket and discobered that blue light is constant in the window to show water level. And it is bright. Kind of too bright. I wanted to unplug the thing but went ahead and pushed the "boil" button. It boiled fast. I made mistake by touching the lid and burnt my hand. It is not just warm. It is hot like a frying pan on high setting. My old "inferior" kettle does not do it. Oh yeah, when the water came to boil, the kettle made a ringing sound which sound as if something broke, sort of alarming. And the constant blue light was illuminating the kitchen warning off the accidental touch on kettle lid. No, not my thing. Two stars are given for fast delivery and sturdiness of the kettle which one can clearly feel by heavy weight of it. Returning.

text: Great concept, but fails on numerous fronts
Body: Save your money.  The idea behind this kettle is perfect, if only it did what it was supposed to.  When I am able to get a cup of hot water I am a happy camper, but my issues with this kettle are as follows:* When I fill the kettle, with 1L of water, and immediately set it on to the base for heating, I get a constant beep.  After filling the kettle I have to set it on the counter and wait 3 minutes before the base will receive the canister.* The water goes cold VERY quickly.  There is a button allowing option to keep the water warm, but it keeps it tepid at best.  If you're hoping to top up your tea or coffee you will be sorely disappointed with the temperature.*  More often than not I am unable to heat the water without setting the kettle down for 3 minutes to reset.  I never overfill, so I'm not sure what the problem is, but if you have guests, or are trying to make coffee in a rush this is extremely frustrating.*  What I DO like about this kettle is that WHEN it works it heats the water quickly.  With my old kettle I had to wait 4-5 minutes for the water to boil.  This boils much faster, but I'd say overall I spend much more time trying to get this kettle to work properly.  Between trying to reset the kettle and the actual boiling time it can take more closer to 6 minutes to make a cup of coffee, if I'm lucky.The concept is great, but it's not without serious glitches.  If you're hoping for a good cup of coffee I'd stick to a simpler design.

Pro's -Looks great !Perfect fashion accessory for your kitchen.Can heat water to a variety of temps if that's what you need.Con's -Lid / open mechanism failed after about 18 monthsCost of ownership Very High as a result of failure / repurchase of a replacement kettle.Reports of  malfunctions from other reviews made me uneasy about leaving it plugged in when away from house for extended periods of time so would always have to remember and unplug from wall.The notion of being able to heat water to the perfect temp for a cuppa was appealing however in all practicality all we ever did was boil water in the traditional manor.If you need a bright shiny object that boils your water to the temp you need every now and again and you have deep pockets, this is the kettle for you, you might want to consider buying two incase the first one malfunctions in some way.If you need a shiny object to jazz up your kitchen and impress your friends, buy one of Cuisinart's other non electrical products and put it on proud display in your kitchen.If you just need to boil water, pick a more basic kettle and save your money.This product did not meet my expectations of Cuisinarts high standards in beauty and functionality combined and now I'm faced with scouring amazon for my new perfect kettle :-(.Disclosure: I own other Cuisinart products and love their combined functionality and looks.

text: Overrated- heavy, wobbles, and hot to the touch. not worth the cost
Body: Just got this to replace a TFal kettle that broke. First impressions upon appearance: not worth the price. The kettle is heavy even without water, the handle is bulky and not comfortable to hold if you have carpal tunnel, buttons appear cheap ( other reviews say they wear off as well). I got the Hamilton Beach version that looks similar before this and hoped this would be of better quality--they both seem cheap and look very similar.This kettle does not settle firmly in its base and wobbles when it comes to a boil The exterior is hot to the touch as well and collects fingerprints.To be fair, most of the electric kettles are poor quality. I use one all day for tea, and I usually need to replace in 1-2 years. I was willing to pay more for this one in the hopes it would last longer. It is going back. I can't believe Wirecutter rated this so highly either. Aesthetics aside, it does not seem safe.

Too expensive. Difficult to see how much water you’ve put in it because the window is very thin and located behind the handle. The buttons being on the handle, while I have yet to experience fading as others have reported i have felt the need to be careful and i am always worried about water getting on the buttons and somehow into the electronic parts. There is some kind of drip proof thing at the spout that can lead to hot water splashing everywhere when you are trying to empty the thing into your desired vessel. And while its a similar size to other kettles it seems to hold less water than other kettles I have had. In the end it does what it is supposed to do but its too expensive and more trouble than its worth. To do over, I would either just get a cheap one from wal mart or try a kettle where the heat control buttons are not on the kettle itself.

text: So far, so great!!  --> Update --product failure after 7 months
Body: Got this about a week ago. So far, it's proven to be a tea lover's dream! We just started drinking loose tea (no comparison!!) and we're loving this machine. I didn't realize how much I didn't know about tea quality until recently when I discovered the ultimate taste is largely dependant upon the temperature at which it is brewed. The "strong" flavor I didn't care for was a result of too high heat, not steeping too long. Who knew!? Anyway, now I know, and I'm enjoying many different teas already with this amazing kettle.It's super easy to use. It heats up very quickly. And the 30 minute keep warm feature is handy! It also looks super sleek in our kitchen.I was a little stand offish with the price tag (about twice what we usually pay). However, I'm sold! I would definitely purchase again (although I hope I won't need to for a few years).________________Well, 7 months after purchase, our tea kettle stopped working. So I changed my review from a 5 to a 2. While it worked, it worked great. But while we used the kettle a lot (several times a day) I still feel that 7 months is too quick. I don't I'll spend time submitting a warranty claim over $100.00. Just doesn't seem worth the time and aggravation, but I won't repurchase this product. We love our kettles. And the temp. select was a big selling point that I will look for in our next kettle. Stainless internal components are also a must.Back to the drawing board....

Everything is perfect except, it started to not turn off even after the temperature of the water was at boiling and the kettle beeped saying it is done, but the water kept boiling until we either unplugged it or took the kettle off the stand. Just looked up my past orders and I purchased one just over 8 years ago so and another 4 years ago so the 4 year protection won't cover it. The original one from 8 years ago left a puddle of water after 4 years of ownership and almost everyday use. Otherwise it is a good electric kettle with multiple settings. If the 1st one didn't leak and the 2nd one wouldn't malfunction I would leave a 5 star review but that is not the case.

text: IT STOPPED WORKING LESS THAN ONE YEAR AFTER PURCHASE
Body: Cuisinart is a top brand. I have other products by this brand. I ordered this electric kettle in May  2020, it stopped working today, less than one year after purchase. It is not my outlet, etc. There is nothing in the manual to "trouble-shoot" the unit. There is no circuit breaker or trip switch, nothing. It is dead. Did I save the box or receipt to send back, No I didn't if I did that my house would be full of boxes, etc. It worked well enough. I used it once a day for ten months---one would think that something like this would be made with enough quality to work as intended for years. I still have a toaster from 30 years ago! A blender the same, I am very disappointed.

text: Still Sorry I bought this - keep warm feature a bother
Body: I read about this as the recommended pick on a popular website.  I dislike it because it requires an extra step to turn it off. After you heat the water, it appears to have a keep warm feature. Well that sounds great it means it will continue to boil or heat the water for some period of time. I just need to boil the water and be done with it. I have the extra step of turning off the feature or unplugging it. I wish I had bought a different model.Later review:  after year of ownership, I still would not buy this again. You have to remember to click a button off after you use this. Otherwise, a keyboard feature will make it boil again for the next 30 minutes and shut it run out of water. it will be bet you I just don’t like to have to press another button once I use the boiling water.  It would work better for me if you had to press the keep warm feature after it boils and you pour your water.

text: Have You Considered How Heavy This Is?
Body: Before I bought this -let's face it, it isn't cheap - I read the reviews. Everyone is concerned with speed and whether it performs better than the much cheaper competition. I went ahead and bought it.The kettle performs well but is completely useless to me simply because it is so heavy I find it almost impossible to lift when full of water.The answer, of course, is to fill the kettle with only a cup full; however, if you do, then that expensive keep warm feature is also completely useless.I want to point out that although weight is not a technical problem, it makes the kettle completely useless to me. I keep it in my kitchen where it looks very nice, but for myself, a bought the DEZIN electric kettle which IMHO is much prettier, MUCH lighter and hence does the job.My recommendation is to forget this kettle and buy a lighter, cheaper one.For your information, I am over 60, but I am not a weakling. My daughter, who is in her 20's also has problems with this kettle and no longer uses it when cooking.

Purchased this kettle a few months ago, we needed a new one due to an overseas move, so our old Sunbeam kettle had the wrong voltage. I have been a bit disappointed as it was certainly not a cheap item.  I think that the boiling the water at different temperatures is a bit of a gimmick, we didn't like our tea not made with boiling water (what we are used to after 40 years I suppose). The feature of bringing the water back to boil has been irritating, as I make tea, sit down and then the kettle boils again, some may find this useful, we have switched this feature off, which thankfully you can do.  The main thing that is really disappointing is that the lid is quite small, so the opening to fill the kettle is small, which may not seem a big thing, but if you want a full kettle, it gets quite heavy and having to keep it in a very exact position, is a nuisance. Other than the fact that I have paid for features I don't use, it is reasonably quick to boil, isn't too loud, and has no plastic inside so we have no issues with the water being tainted, which I know is a big problem through friends' experiences.

text: Like It But It's Not Always Accurate
Body: I really love the look and function of this kettle, which I got for Valentine's Day, using a gift card. It's sleek-looking and the button presets are excellent. It's certainly not like the Breville One-Touch in the way of efficiency, but I certainly love the Keep Warm, which you can shut off and on, along with other benefits. I previously used (and still have as backup) the Aroma kettle, which was pretty decent and reliable for the price, but lacked the ability to control the temperature. It was always too hot.While this kettle provides those wants and more, I have to say that, during the times I've checked the temp immediately after it's beeped "ready", it hasn't always been at the temperature of the present selected, but rather well under. My thermometer is pretty consistent and professional-grade, so I don't think that is an issue, but it could be my particular kettle or other factors, and I'm waiting to purchase a better thermo later to confirm the issue. For now, it's not a big deal; I just set it a little higher for my delicate teas to reach 175, 180, etc., and have since gotten it down pretty well. It also brews slower than the Aroma I had. I do love the delicate beep (I hate beeping lol), but could see some people complaining about it being too quiet in loud households, and I also appreciate the light that makes it easier to see how much water you have.With that said, while I love the kettle, I'm not sure I would repurchase it again at just around one hundred dollars, should this be an all-around or ongoing issue with the kettle and not just my own. I just don't feel it's worth it in that price range, though perhaps a bit lower. I tend to find it a little overpriced as it is, but it is a great piece otherwise and I love at least being able to have it stop at a certain point, even if it's not completely accurate, sometimes being off by 10 degrees or more. I just recommend checking your temp if you're into temperatures while making tea.You can also find plenty of product reviews on Youtube if you want to see how it works.

text: Owned for 2 years - only one complaint
Body: We bought this product a little over 2 years ago, and have used it nearly every day since. Here is a quick summary of our experience:1) It is well made.2) It heats water very quickly.3) It holds water temperature very well.4) Depending on how you have it set, it shuts off immediately or holds temp for 10 minutes - even if you remove it from the base.5) Temperature is pretty accurate, regardless of setting.If you make single cups of tea, instant coffee, or use a 1-cup coffee maker such as the Melitta or Aeropress, this kettle is perfect. I can make a single cup of coffee almost as fast as a Keurig, and in my opinion it tastes better. We loved it so much that we bought one for our son, who also drinks lots of coffee and tea.The only complaint I have is that the lettering on the buttons began to wear off after only a few months. At this point, most of the buttons have almost none left. If you remember the functions, this isn't a problem, but I think it shouldn't happen.I read through most of the 1-star reviews, and we did not experience ANY of the problems mentioned. We have no rust, even though we don't keep it fastidiously clean. It has performed flawlessly, except for the button wear problem I mentioned. I wonder how many of the people with problems may have possibly used it incorrectly, such as over-filling it? Since we have had no problems, I can't speak to the customer support.If you buy based on my recommendation, I hope that you have as good an ownership experience as we have had. We would buy again, ESPECIALLY if Cuisinart managed to make the button markings more permanent.

I had a Chef's Choice for the last 6 months and I am glad that it broke. This one comes close to the SAECO ( discontinued / went out of business ) we had for 3 years before that...not quiet as intuitive however. The basic Kettle's just boil the water and shut the heater off. This one goes into a "keep warm" mode after it reaches the target temperature. That makes a lot of sense. It takes a couple of days to figure out the buttons and in which sequence to push them to for example shut it completely off etc...but we are glad to have that functionality back in the kitchen. I read a lot of complaints about the Cuisinart not being reliable...will see..I will downgrade it if it lasts less than 1 year...Update after a couple of weeksWe have had it for a couple of weeks now..it has a couple of flaws..you really dont know when it reached the target temperature the first time..it does a beep ( not very loud )..if you miss it you would not know ( it may change the "blinking" pattern or go from "blink" to "steady" )...especially if it is in the "keep warm" mode..that mode is the next issue...each button is backlid and the light shows whether it is activated..unfortunately the lights are so close together that you can't make out which button is on or off. For example , if the "Keep warm" button is on together with the " boil" button, you may think the "start" button is on as well. It may be off, in which case nothing happens until you realize the mistake..I still give it 4 star just because of the lack of any good alternative kettles..

text: Pretty pretty pretty pretty pretty good
Body: Just received my tea kettle, been looking forward to this purchase and it does not disappoint.First run was to use the 160 degree present and brew some white tea (one note - their suggested brewing temperatures are a little higher than what I think is more commonly accepted, please don't brew your white tea at 185 degrees). It heated up quick and was the right temperature, gave me a nice gentle steeping. Second run was oolong at 190, also hit the spot, very happy with the results.I deducted 1-star for the afore-mentioned issue with tea-steeping temperature suggestions and, more importantly, b/c it is basically impossible to see the water level unless the backlighting has come on (when in operation the buttons & water gauge glow blue). Not a huge deal but slightly annoying and I have used less fancy tea kettles where you can always see the water level. I have to check, pretty sure there is no floating bauble so you need the backlighting to see where the water rises to. Ok, still really happy with it and would suggest it.I chose this over the 1-L Bonavita Gooseneck Variable Temperature Kettle, figured that having the capacity needed for guests outweighed the pour control of the gooseneck spout. The Bonavita also allows for more temperature customization but the presets on the Cuisinart are sufficient for me, and I am quite particular about water temp so that is saying something.  Last several years I've just used a stovetop kettle and have added a bit of room temp water to my tea before pouring in boiling water, that was fun and artful but this is much easier.

I have only just received this and am happy with the shipping and packaging. It's a little smaller than I had imagined, but it's fine and actually takes a little less space on my counter than the old electric kettle it is replacing while holding the same amount (1.7L). I did a lot of research and expected to get a glass kettle this time, but many reviews steered me away from them and towards a stainless steel one, and this was the best of the those I researched. It has many temp settings that I don't really need (as yet) not being a tea drinker, so I just use it on boil. I'd prefer that it would have that as a default setting but it's no big deal to push that button and then the Start button. It does heat up quickly and the water level window lights up in blue. If I designed it, the window would be bigger and not underneath the handle - just easier to read from across the room. With the handle facing you, you can't see the water level. I also find it a little unwieldy and unbalanced when picking up a full kettle - it's not a perfect design and I felt the need to grab it with my other hand. It pours nicely and the Keep Warm feature is nice. I'm pleased, and hope it lasts - the old one, a plastic Merlita, was over 10 years old! Nowadays I don't expect things are made like that, but fingers crossed...

I drink tea daily, and have an assortment of teas be it white, green, black, or herbal from which to choose.  The company from which I purchase the teas recommends the optimum brewing temperature for  each and it does not make a lot of sense to pay for some of the worlds finest teas and then not prepare them so as to extract all the flavors and nuances proper brewing can produce.  It is not analogous to taking a 20 year old Chateau Margaux from my temperature controlled wine cellar and boiling it in my tea kettle before serving, but you get the idea.I like that you can read how much water is in the kettle, I like that it will hold the proper temperature for a few minutes after it is reached. I like that the kettle will swivel on the base so it is convenient to pick up. I like that the kettle will shut itself off if I forget. I like it that the kettle has been able to get me within 5 degrees F of all optimum temperatures I have thus far encountered.I do not like that the kettle gets hot when the water is hot. I would like it better if I could hit all of the recommended brewing temperatures spot on.I am enjoying my teas much more since I have started using the Cuisinart kettle.I would recommend it to any of my friends or family trying to decide on the purchase.Thanks to Cuisinart for making my tea drinking experience significantly more pleasant.

This is a very nice kettle. I like the separate housing of the element and the whole look of the kettle in general.  I went ahead and got this kettle based on the reviews I read.It heats water very quickly, as mentioned, and the different, lower, temperature settings are great for making hot chocolate and tea for my children so it doesn't burn them.  There is no strange taste like I have heard there is from plastic kettles and the easy flip up lid is so convenient- I use to have to wrestle the lid off my other kettle. The water level indicator is wonderful- clear and precise and the blue light is an fun addition as is the cute beeping that signals the  heating process is finished.My biggest disappointment is that it is NOT quiet like some of the plastic ones are. Hence, only 4 stars.  My kitchen overlooks the family room and when the kettle is in the middle of the heating process it is so loud that no-one can hear the telly ( TV ). The children turn the telly up very loud to hear it over the kettle. It is only for a little while, perhaps 30 seconds, but it is a nuisense none-the-less.However, since the telly isn't always on when I am making tea and it is a very nice looking, easy to use and efficient kettle otherwise, I will keep it and I am happy to do so.  In fact, if I had read that it was not quiet I would not have gotten it and going on what I know now, I would regret not having it.

text: Amazing Kettle to Serve All Your Needs
Body: I have had this kettle over a year now and noticed that I hadn't reviewed it yet.  I use this kettle on a daily basis.  When I make tea, it is really nice to get the water to the exact temperature.  I set the temperature of the kettle and then add it to my cup or tea pot and let the tea steep.  I have a coffee pot but on mornings I just want one really good cup, I use the French press setting.  This kettle is also useful for things outside of drinks.  It's great to heat up water for oatmeal.  The no drip pour actually works and I've never had a problem with it.  The stay warm will keep the pot at the desired temperature for awhile in case you need to make more than one cup of tea.There are two minor quirks.  The first is if you turn it off, take it off the plate, then put it back on, a blue glow will appear on your last setting.  It won't actually heat the water up but the blue glowing light is on for no reason.  The other is you want to clean it out when you see buildup.  I use 1 part vinegar to 4 parts water and set it to a boil.  I pour it out and then fill it with water, boil it again and its good as new.

text: With a fixed solution to the lettering - It would be the perfect kettle!
Body: Finally know what good tea is supposed to taste like. Tried this with my collection of white and green teas and what a difference. It keeps the temperature right at the perfect spot. I have a 16 oz Loose tea infuser. I do the first infusion and put into my warmed teapot. Then do a second one with the same tea to extract more flavor and mix the two. Now get two brews from my tea at the same temp.I would have given it 5 stars except for all the reviews about the letters wearing off. Tried the solution one review suggested. Clear nail polish. Do not get the Quick Dry kind. Tried the first button (160) and then looked like it was going to dry with ridges. Went back over it to smooth out and it looks like the lettering was dissolving. My mistake. Did one coat on all the rest and they all look fine.Really should not have to do this at all if they had quality labeling. But as far as heating water to just the right temp - Perfect!Liked it so much, bought one for my sister for a birthday gift - and her birthday is not for 5 months, but she is getting it early! (And telling her not to use quick dry clear nail polish.

text: I loved this Cuisinart - it is well built and despite ...
Body: I purchased this as a gift for my son who loves to brew various teas which require precise temperatures.  This Cuisinart kettle performed very well, rapidly heating water to the preferred temperature and then maintaining it that temperature.  The unit eventually turns off automatically after a  certain amount of time, but the kettle is well insulated and water remains heated for an extended period. There is a one-year warranty which I did have to rely on, with the unit failing just one week shy of that anniversary. I called Amazon which put me in touch with Cuisinart. They replaced the unit after I mailed the defective one back. My only issue was having had to pay for the return shipping. The new unit has lasted beyond another year after continual use. My son has since moved out to college and taken the kettle with him, which leaves me searching for a new one. I loved this Cuisinart - it is well built and despite the first failure, remains a sturdy product. I will not be using one as much as my son did so I will likely purchase a less costly model for myself.

I didn't know how much I needed one of these until I got it. It's so much more convenient than heating water on the stovetop or in the microwave. And it looks cool on the counter. Water heats up fast, and it's at the perfect temperature for whatever tea or coffee we're drinking at the time.The only thing I'd like would be a larger capacity, since my husband and I like to fill two French presses with his coffee and my Teecchino on the weekends. We have to do two batches of hot water for that. If you overfill the container, water will get all over the counter.One tip for new owners that I would recommend is to make sure that the light is blinking after you press start to get the water heated. Sometimes I forget to check this, and when I come back, the light is on, but no hot water.Despite the four star review, I wouldn't trade this kettle for any of the other ones that I've seen for sale. I did a lot of research on electric kettle before I settled on the Cuisinart, and I believe I made the right choice. Our food processor and blender are Cuisinarts too, and I'm very happy with their performance and simplicity, so perhaps there's a bit of brand loyalty at work here also.

text: I like the cozy blue light
Body: I was looking for an electric kettle and this one is.It's bulky and heavy, but keeps a lot of hot or warm water for a very long time even after being turned off.It's noisier when heating up, than I expected, but in a few days I got used to it.My issue with the steam: a generous amount of steam at the end of heating cycle is a bit troublesome. There is no way around it. Since I don't want all this moisture to end up at the bottom of the hanging kitchen cabinet, I found the only open space: near the sink under the window. Now the counter looks too busy and cluttered, the window glass over it - is often misty from the steam, but I always have my hot water in a reasonable time.I am also is still looking for the way to wipe out the traces of my fingertips all over the walls of this kettle.I like the cozy blue light, which it emits (when on) in the dark kitchen.I bought a fancy kettle with a temperature control in case I ever serve something different than black tea or hot water with lemon, which I drink a lot.And the most important: I don't worry anymore about leaving a teapot on the stove.

Very utilitarian, with a few flaws. The good points are that it has a large capacity, it has several temperature settings, and it has an auto reheat/off system. A minor annoyance is that the temps can be reset easily by brushing against them unconsciously and you only realize after you heated the water.What doesn't work, mostly, is the water gauge. It's hard to see in any condition except bright light, and, after a year or so, the numbers wear off. Maybe a floating red ball in the indicator and simple etched lines (¼, ½, Full) instead of painted/decal lines and text.I use filtered reverse osmosis water, so I can't speak to scaling problems. It still heats quickly after 4 years almost daily use and, except for the worn indicator numbers, is attractive and easy to clean. I notice that a lot of my friends get this one. That's probably because it's among the top picks on both Wirecutter and SeriousEats. It's definitely a good choice and a good price.

So I'm a coffee junkie.  So much so that I have an awesome grinder, french press, pour over drip ceramic, vacuum pot, all the stuff.For me, 90% of the electric kettles out there, fall short of the mark because they don't have the ability to adjust temperature.  You get boiling, or nothing.  This is the lowest entry point for that except for the Adagio Utilitea.  Which has better reviews and can be had for $45 in the back corners of the internet searches + retailmenotI chose this for two simple reasons - 1.) I'm married and my wife likes brand names for the kitchen <sigh>  2.) It has 3 yr warranty, compared to 1 yr warranty on Adagio product.If you see all the bad reviews on Adagio - it is because of 1 yr failure rate and lack of support.  I didn't want to quite risk that.  It felt like for +$30..hedging my risk for 3 years was smarter.Everything else it does fine.  Something important to bring up - there is no reasonable electric kettle that lets you set temp..you get presets.  (e.g. there is no 184 degrees, or 178 degrees if you want to dabble with brewing temperature of your coffee or dark/light roast)...but there is a french roast setting (200), as well as 160, 175, 185, 190 & 212 (boil)

Just got my ne Cuisinart kettle and have used it once, so this is just a first impression.  Even though the weight is stated as 1 lb., I found this heavy to lift, particularly with water in it.  Now that said, I have a right shoulder rotator cuff injury so I've lost some muscle power in that arm temporarily.  I'm in PT so I expect to gain back strength in that arm.  Also the handle, as has been noted, is a bit wide.  I guess that's to accommodate the different temperature displays, but really, Cuisinart needs to fix this.  Also, the beep that tells you when your water has reached the right temperature isn't very loud.  You really have to be listening for it.  A.M.'s are busy at my house and unless I was standing near the pot I didn't hear it.  That was a disappointment as it was one of the features that convinced me to buy it.  I wouldn't suggest buying this to a person with small hands or weak arms.All that said, it is attractive and does just what it says it does.  I used it for french press and the temperature was perfect.  So for now, 4 stars because the handle is too wide.

text: Not accurate enough for science experiments, but makes a great cup of tea! ;)
Body: Love this kettle.  I understand from other reviewers that I should expect the writing on the buttons to wear off sooner than I would like, but I am willing to live with that for the plus of having multiple buttons preset for my teas and the stainless steel "innards". As to that, the interior is nearly 100% stainless steel. The only places that are not are the area around the little hole near the bottom that lets water into the window area so you can tell how full the pot is, the underside of the lid, and the tab that holds the filter screen.  The water-level window is BPA free per the manufacturer, but it is nice to know that most of my water is not touching it as it boils away.  As to the lid and the screen tab, these only touch the steam in the kettle, not the water.  Granted the steam can condense and fall back into the pot, but this does not seem to cause an off-flavor that I can identify.  As to accuracy, I'd say it is good enough.  I have tested it at full boil and at the Green Tea setting of 175 degrees.  I'm at 5600 feet, so full boil here is 204 degrees not 212.  The pot is clearly confused by this and wants to keep working to get the temperature up.  However, it shuts itself off after a minute, then a minute later it tries again, boiling the water away.  Since it has an automatic "boil dry" shutoff, I am not worried about this issue, but I will keep and eye on it when it is set at the Black Tea (boil) setting.  When tested at the green tea setting, I noticed the water was always heated about three to five degrees past the set temperature (it took 1.7 liters of 67 degree water to 178 degrees in 6 minutes, and 7 minutes to get to full boil).  When the water cools to one degree below its set point, it turns on the heat again and heats the water up to 178 again.  In two cases, it went up to 180 degrees.  I don't find this a problem though, because as soon as you pour the water into a cup, even a pre-heated cup (using the hot water in t he pot), it always cools down three to five degrees (I tested this too!).  So, it is the perfect temperature IF it is overheated in the pot.  Finally, the beep.  It beeps when it reaches temperature, but it is a very soft beep.... kind of like hearing a truck back up way down the street from you when you have all your windows closed.  Easy not to notice if you are in another room.  I'm good with that too, as I have excellent hearing, and if I miss the cue it automatically keeps the water warm for 30 minutes anyway.  Highly recommended.

text: Great water heater: efficient, quick, and accurate.
Body: Great, so far.  If it dies in the future I'll probably come back to tell everyone.  I've had this unit for approximately three weeks now, and I use it to make 2.8 liters of tea, for iced tea, every morning. I let it steep in glass 1-liter carafes, and making it right after breakfast gives it time to slowly cool down naturally as well as suck all the benefit from one standard-sized tea bag per carafe.  At lunch I have a liter plus a little and my wife has about .8 liter.  For dinner I have another liter of tea, and mi esposa has water.  That's in addition to the glass of wine we each have with dinner.  I've been looking for something like this for a year, and I hadn't been impressed enough to even  try anything I could find until now.  There were either control issues or size issues that made the other kettles I'd considered unsuitable for my use.  For years I've used my coffee maker to heat the tea water, and my coffee maker, one of the discontinued Braun models, is getting rather long in the tooth.  I really like the coffee it makes, so I'm using the Cuisinart tea pot to absorb a great part of the workload.  I heat the water for two of the carafes (1.8 liters total) together, and after I pour them from the pot into the first two carafes I immediately pour the third carafe containing the final liter of water into the Cuisinart pot.  I don't have to do anything to restart it since it remembers what it was doing for about two minutes after it's removed from the base.  Finally, after it finishes heating, and I've poured the hot water into the third carafe along with a tea bag, I set it back on the stand, it lights back up, and I hit the start button again to turn it off, and I'm done with it for the day. Very efficient operation. Since the tea we use is almost always black tea I normally use the highest or boil setting.

There's no denying that this kettle is high; there are plenty out there that are cheaper (the best seller on Amazon right now is $14), and you don't need a fancy kettle just to boil water. That being said - this kettle is worth every penny.My husband drinks French Press coffee most mornings; I drink tea occasionally, and we make a lot of hot teas and hot chocolates during the colder months. Since we both use it for different (and very specific) things, this kettle is perfect. He uses the French Press setting, and I use the black or chai tea. You pick your temperature, hit start, and walk away. It is a little loud, but not annoyingly so, and I like that it helps me to remember it. The beep definitely is quiet. If you are in the next room, or watching TV, or just humming to yourself, you won't hear it. But since you can choose 'keep warm', it doesn't bother me. Next time I hear it warming back up, or walk into the kitchen and spot it, I can take it off the base and it's just as hot as if the beep just sounded. The base is another bonus - no cords to mess with, and you can spin it on the base to tuck the handle out of the way, or pull it back around to grab. And make sure you only grab the handle- the sides get HOT. Not warm, not a little hot. Straight up hot. I have brushed my arm against it a couple of times and quickly yanked it back. If you have small children, you will need to be careful with it.Despite the price, and the occasional arm-scalding incident, we couldn't be happier with this kettle. One kettle works well for our individual needs, it has a stainless steel interior (less plastic is always better in my book), the 'keep warm' setting means you can set it and forget it, and let's not forget that it just plain looks pretty sitting on the counter.

This is one of my favorite things that I have ever purchased! I use it every single day to make tea in the morning, and occasionally in the afternoons as well. It heats quickly, is relatively quiet (a bit noisy when getting up to a boil, but the noise doesn't last long). The little beeping at the end is nice, not too loud.I originally wanted the pricey tea maker from Breville, because I liked the idea of setting the tea maker just like a coffee maker and having the tea ready to go in the morning. However, I usually only drink one cup of tea in the morning, and it seemed a bit too expensive for my one cup. I decided I could live with pouring the water over my own tea and brewing it that way. I've been very happy with my decision.One of the best features is the "Keep Warm" function. I like this because I don't have to go running the second I hear the "I'm done" beep, the way I used to have to run to the kitchen to calm down the shrieking stovetop kettle. If I don't hear the beep, or just can't get there right away, no problem! The kettle will periodically reheat to keep the temperature up. For multiple cups of tea, however, I don't use the "Keep Warm" function. I just shut off the kettle and then get it going again when/if I want a second cup of tea. It reheats so quickly that I don't bother keeping it warm and listening to the reboil over and over.I haven't done any testing of the temperatures to see how accurate they are, but all of my different types of tea taste great when brewed at the preset temperatures. Unlike some previous reviewers, I have not had any issues with the words wearing off the preset buttons. The kettle still looks brand new, nothing fading or peeling after about a year now of daily use.Buy it, you won't regret it!

All I can say is I am sitting here thinking, why did I wait so long to order this? I have been considering this product for a few years. The cost was a bit of a barrier but also I had one of those 5-gallon water coolers with the typical hot water option. That is what I used for years and before that I pretty much just heated water up in the microwave. Yes. Sad but true. Recently we moved and downsized and with that move we lost the space for the nifty 5-gallon water cooler. So, I was back to heating water in the microwave. Anyway, I finally broke down and purchased this item. And let me just say; W-O-W. This is perfect in many ways; easy to use, heats up fast, temperature is perfect, great safety features, very attractive appliance, takes up little space, perfect size, etc. All this translates to my absolute love for this product but also the proverbial regret of why did I not but this sooner? Also, I must say, I have been drinking tea at the wrong temperatures ALL my life!!! Honestly! What a wake up call. My first cup of green tea at the appropriate temperature in this Cuisinart was an a-ha moment for me! Previously, I had been heating my water to nearly boiling and just flat out ruining the delicate notes of my green tea! What a shame. And here all this time I just thought it was bad tea and eventually got accustomed to drinking bad tea! So, to say I am happy is an understatement. I am so glad I finally fronted up the money to buy this. If you appreciate a perfect cup of tea-look no further. Note: I am a big coffee drinker too but I have not used this Cuisinart for that yet. I have however used it for hot water for oatmeal, cooking, etc. and, just like for tea, it works perfect.

I had previously bought this kettle almost a decade ago and used it heavily. We're talking at least once a day if not 2-3 times a day. I've gone through coffee, no coffee, green tea, black tea, and herbal tea phases and the temp controls make a difference, as far as I can tell, as to whether or not the tea leaves or coffee grounds come out perfect or slightly off. I love it.I love it so much that when it stopped working after our most recent cross-country move I ordered the part I suspected had fizzled and soldered the new one in. It worked! Except I then misplaced the tiny screws that hold the bottom on. I proceeded to fight with it every day for weeks with the bottom half hanging off but I still didn't want to give up, I loved the kettle so much.Eventually a family member sent me a perfectly nice kettle with a few temp settings but it just wasn't the same. I ordered my beloved Cuisinart electric kettle and I'm hoping to get another ten years out of this one.PROS: Fast. I find this kettle heats up to boiling much faster than other electric kettles I've found. I also really like that it's steel and I can't see into it because we have very hard water where I live. I know the white mineral buildup is safe but I don't always like seeing it, you know? I clean it every week or so but still. The multi temperatures pretty much all get used. Maybe I don't use the delicate/white tea setting often but everything else for sure.CONS: It's pricey. In the long run I paid pennies per day for this thing but I've had some people look at me funny when I tell them I dropped a hundred bucks on a kettle. Other than that I can't think of any cons. If I hadn't lost the screws for the base I probably would have kept using the same, repaired kettle for as long as possible.

text: Good price over my other top choice
Body: I bought this kettle as a gift but I get to enjoy the tea made with it and see it in action almost every day. It's been a really good purchase so far; at the time I was considering buying this kettle or the Breville One-Touch Tea Maker. Below are the reasons why I chose this product:1. At the time this kettle was a whopping $175 LESS than the Breville Tea Maker. Big difference there!2. The Breville seemed cool with its "one-touch, brew the tea too" option, BUT if you like to make different teas then you can easily switch temperatures with this kettle to go from black to green or oolong, etc without having to clean out the pot (which, with the Breville, would have all your steeped tea inside) to change teas. This works well because I rarely drink the same tea as the owner of the kettle (they prefer stronger flavored teas while I prefer sweeter, flowery notes in my tea).3. Did I mention $175 less? :)Other nice things about this kettle:* It's really sleek looking with the steel and blue backlight.* The buttons are easy to read and I like that the temperature and type of tea are on the same button, for those who may be forgetful about what temperature goes with what type of tea.* Reaches temperature within minutes. Very fast and easy to pour/refill.* Doesn't take up too much counter real estate* Doesn't have a million pieces (to lose/break)I don't know how loud other kettles are or if any are whisper quiet so I can't really compare the noise. This one only makes sounds when its reaching a boil and even then I think it's just the water boiling. The sound stops after the water reaches its temperature. The kettle's owner brought it in to work and said the sound is not too loud (and this is in a quiet, cubicle environment). The beep when the tea is ready is not too loud, but since the kettle keeps the water at temperature, it's no big deal. Just see if the temperature button you set has stopped flashing, and if so, your water is ready.You still need a mug and brew basket or tea bags or whatever you use to steep your tea, as this is just a variable temperature kettle.

text: So nice I bought it twice
Body: I've had my first one for over 7 years. The only wear is one of the buttons is starting to fade/wear away. I had a house guest who had never seen an electric kettle and placed it on the stove for a little bit before the burnt plastic smell indicated his mistake. Thankfully the kettle still worked. When I furnished my apartment closer to the city this was my first appliance, since caffeine made the rest of the tasks easier.
